Headings: It will help you to learn to read Spanish. Listening and speaking requires more than this.
Base_Reviews: Duolingo is a great program. I have been learning with it for just over two years now (I upgraded to the Pro version) and by studying at home, with just Duolingo, I am now able to read some Spanish novels, read some magazines and newspapers, and I have a general understanding of the language.But ... if you really want to converse with others, you will need more than this to do that. When I listen to Spanish TV or music or a movie, I"m lost. I have Spanish speaking friends and if they speak slowly, I will understand but in order to respond, it will take me too much time to think about how to properly frame the response. If I were asked to write down my response, I could do that more easily than speaking.My point is, this is an excellent program and I enjoy using it and feel accomplished. But, to truly learn the language, you will need interaction with others who are fluent in the language.Let this get you started and, if you find yourself enjoying it, get a tutor, take a Spanish class, or travel and do some immersion learning. As you're taking lessons, Duolingo will help along the way.Great things about DuoLingo -** It has an active discussion group, so if you're confused about an answer, just click and you'll likely see 100's of posts about that issue.** It has a dictionary so that you can find words that are not part of your lesson** As you learn words, it adds them to your personal word list and shows you when you last used that word so that you can practice vocabulary that you might have not used in a while.** You can read stories that are based on your reading level; it is not just grammar.** The Android version is very easy but I prefer to use it on my laptop or Kindle. Fortunately, Duolingo has platforms for all as well as iOS.** It lets you set your own pace and will remind you daily if you've met your goal for the day. You can change the time you spend per day whenever you like.** Duolingo has a podcast as well which is good to practice your listening skills. It may be too advanced, but it's still good to help you learn the flow and tone of the language.I deducted one star because many people will think this IS the answer, when in fact it is only a part of the answer. The program also has a bit of trouble with voice recognition but then, it might be that my Brooklyn accent does not translate well into proper Spanish.

I am working on both Spanish and French right now.  They are both languages I've studied previously but need to refresh.  Duolingo is helping me and I enjoy the daily work.I have not yet tried a totally new language, but that will be next.  Thanks Duolingo!

I find myself understanding parts of conversations in Spanish when I'm out in stores or flipping through Spanish television stations. It's very simple and fun. More like playing a game than a tedious language lesson. The best part is I'm actually learning! I can't believe this amazing tool is free! Now there is no reason not to be multi lingual!

A free app that uses both written and verbal practice to help you learn several different languages.  Only two things I would want from it is an option to learn in lessons before exercises for practice, occasionally you get asked to translate words before you see them used but usually they appear in yellow and you can tap them,  and an option to use a different keyboard to correctly use the appropriate characters unique to that language.

Fun presentation mixing graphics, listening/speaking and reading to immerse students in a gradual escalation of difficulty within their chosen language course. The app doesn't overexplain like a textbook, so be prepared to just dive in!You can repeat any lesson when you need to, and you receive points for completing sections that you can use to unlock supplemental lessons like idioms.
its very cool b/c it's teaches verses that u can use. app is easy to use.

Headings: An easy and fun way to learn Spanish or many other languages.
Base_Reviews: Spanish is the fastest growing language in America. We need to know enough to be conversant.Duolingo was my choice out of many to accomplish this task. It is fun and easy if you have the desire and discipline to do your homework every day, or even every other day. You can practice over and over until you speak Spanish like a native.Other languages are available too, so get ready to meet the world!

I love this app. It's just as easy and intuitive as Rosetta Stone only free and easy to use on my tablet and phone. It teaches and tests at a comfortable pace, often incorporating vocabulary and phrases from previous lessons to keep your old lessons from fading in your memory. I love the multifaceted style of typing, speaking, imagery and multiple choice. Did I mention free?? No ads. Seriously a great app. I'm brushing up my Spanish while discovering German.

Great app! Quick and easy way to introduce new language skills in just 5 to 10 minutes each morning while I drink my coffee. This would probably be more effective used alongside a full language course, but for those of us who don't have time it is an easier alternative.

I downloaded this app a year ago and was mildly impressed with the approach for picking up a second language so I uninstalled it.  I recently decided to give it another chance and was surprised how much more I enjoyed the process/approach for developing second language skills.  You are only as good as your study habits.  I'm a hit and miss user, so my skills have only marginally improved, but I see the real value this app provides.  Great App

It has helped me read, write, speak, and understand Spanish!I LOVE IT!!!!!!!YOU WILL LOVE IT!!!!!!!! ( ALMOST GARENTEED)(WARNING)...  IT IS SO ADDICTING!!!!!!! ;-) Which could be good or bad.â˜ºI HOPE YOU LOVE IT!!! ...( It deserves it.)

I really like this language app. It's got a couple of shortcomings but not many. Occasionally it will ask you to translate a word it has never shown you. Also some grammar rules aren't explained very well. Takes a few times going through each one before you really get it. But that's language for ya. Otherwise it's awesome. I can now understand a bit of german. Enough that if I was dropped in Germany I wouldn't be completely lost. If someone spoke slow and clear in German to me I would be able to somewhat understand. And that's after just a few weeks.

Headings: Makes it easy to learn a language, has several language choices.
Base_Reviews: Learning more words thru this app than any other. Really like it. Wish it was easier to start at the beginning, for review of words. Like that it goes from English to Spanish and back, then even incorporates spelling!

I have been using Duolingo for a week and love it.  I can set how much time per day to dedicate and the app creates lessons to fit the time limit.  It reminds you if you missed a lesson.  It says a phrase in the learning language and has you repeat it.  This really helps in retaining what you've learned. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because it docks me for misspelling certain French words.  But my keyboard doesn't have the punctuation required.  Awesome otherwise!
I've been using Duolingo for about 2 weeks now to learn Italian and feel like I am learning quickly. This seems to be a great way for me to learn.  Ciao!

Headings: fun way to learn other languages
Base_Reviews: Very easy to use, designed to be fun, and the program emails reminders to help you stay on track (because retention necessitates regular lessons).  I've taking Italian for about a year now and know quite a bit of vocabulary, but am only guessing at structure, which is why I gave  4 stars and not 5.  I wish that links to explanations of syntax and pronunciation would be added.

I love this language app. It is fun and easy to use with match the words, repeat phrases and type in translations. I just wish you could skip ahead to sections you really want to learn instead of going through the whole set.

My only quibble is that it doesn't really give any explanations.  When you guess incorrectly, and you do, sometimes have to guess because words are thrown in without introduction, it often tells you that you've used one form instead of another, but it hasn't explained how and when the forms are used.  I understand the natural learning strategy it uses, it does work, but I think I would catch on more with very basic usage explanations.  For free, though, this is a gift to the world.

This is better than Rosetta stone! I've been working on the French for a month now and am able to understand quite a lot. It's fun quick and you can follow friends and their progress as well. It also lets you earn ringots which let you purchase some other levels such as flirting and phrases that are common in our language. Only complaint is they don't have a wide selection of languages.

Headings: fun way to learn a new language
Base_Reviews: My 1st grader wanted to learn a new language, a friend told me about Duolingo, thought I'd give it a try. I started doing it to stay ahead of him so I could help him if he needed it. Now my 5th grader is doing it to. We are having funny using our new language skills together. Bottom line it can help at a by age.My only 2 critiques would be, a better reward system to keep kids interested. Maybe a reference area to explain a little about how the words are formed to have a better understanding.That being said it is a Free app, so it is great!

It's a great app that teaches you different languages. But sometimes it can get confusing when you respond to a question it gives you it tells you your wrong and thEn it later tells you your right a different time. Besides it's small quirks I still enjoy this app. I use it and it's easy enough for my kids to use it as well.

Headings: Sentences are sometimes odd but good app
Base_Reviews: I'm currently using the app to learn 2 languages. The computer-created sentences can be a bit odd. I doubt that los pajaros leen el diario. (The birds read the newspaper.) The main thing keeping me from rating it 5 stars is that there is no alphabet tutoring for the languages. If I'm learning Spanish, it isn't an issue. But, what if I want to try Greek? What are the letters, and how are they pronounced?

Duolingo is a wonderful language app that teaches through immersion. One actually learns conjugation in the early lessons without being "taught" how to do so. It is terrific how each lesson seamlessly builds on the previous one and brings back vocabulary learned earlier on to keep it fresh in one's mind. My son is using it to teach himself French before he studies abroad this Fall and I am using it to dust off my college French that I took quite some time ago. I would therefore wholeheartedly recommend this app to someone either learning a new language or brushing up on an old one.

This is a great program to learn with. Try it and you will immediarely be learning a new language. Before you know it, you will make connections between words that are meaningful and easy to remember. There are a couple of glitches but overall, this is an incredible program.

If you want to learn a new language, this is the app for you! It makes it easy to learn a new language, and if you need to you can go back to re-read words. The only problem is that you can't learn very many languages, including Chinese/Japanese, which I wanted to learn. With how great all the lessons are, I assume they will be updated to have them in the near future. Otherwise, this is an AMAZING app!

I've always wanted to speak another language, but I could never find an app that made learning something new fun and easy until my grandmother showed me Duolingo. One lesson and I was hooked and showed all my friends.

Headings: Excellent way to learn another language
Base_Reviews: I really enjoy this app.  The lessons are short, painless, and fun.  The teaching is a mix of assorted styles that actually enhances memory retention.  I don't mind taking the few minutes needed to complete my lesson and I feel like I actually learned something when I'm done.  Make a Japanese app next!  I would get that one, too!

Headings: Great practice and was surprised how much I remembered
Base_Reviews: Got this to brush up on college French over 30 years ago......Great practice and was surprised how much I remembered.  Strength exercises are particularly helpful to keep what you've learned fresh as you progress through the lessons.

Headings: Wow! I can't believe this free but it is.
Base_Reviews: I have been through the lessons on food terms, animals and some other lessons. I can only say very simple sentences right now but it looks like it provides an extensive list of lessons that will come as I continue to work through the lessons. I have had some trouble with getting the hang of conjugating verbs which this program doesn't spell out for me. So, I would recommend this program to anyone who wants to learn a foreign language. Although it will take a large commitment to work at it.

I've had 7 years of Spanish classes to help me learn the language and I still cannot carry on a conversation. I downloaded this app with my former classes in mind thinking the basics were going to be extremely dull and basic  enough for a child to learn at a young age. I was wrong. It seemed as if you needed some sort of knowledge of the language you wanted to learn or else you'd get lost. This app is helpful so far and I am surprised at how much Spanish I remember during the lessons. The lessons seem to get longer as you progress, which I find to be a great idea in duolingo. I am impressed. I hope to learn more than I already know.

very cool and easy app to practice a language.  Only disadvantages is that if a language has unique symbols like umlauts, etc  the Kindle keyboard does not show those options. and Duolingo marks it incorrect.  Also, the microphone does not always work.

Headings: Duolingo is an excellent language app
Base_Reviews: Duolingo is an excellent language app! It covers listening, writing, reading and speaking. You complete excercises at your own pace.  It also  enables you to redo parts of already completed sections to refresh the vocabulary and grammar you have learnt. It is the best language course I have ever come across.It allows you to listen again to sections to be translated as many times as you want before translating. When you mouse over a word, the English is displayed so this helps you translate when you are stuck on a word you don't know. It also lets you learn  different languages at the same time on the one app just by switching the language at the push of a button! You are awarded "lingots" after completing each section which is an incentive to continue as you can buy different additional bonus sections with them. This is a really well thought out language course and to top it all it was a free app! well worth 5 stars!

Incredible learning experience, reinforces what you've learned, reminders to invest time in learning, encouragement, everything Rosetta Stone isn't, everything Pimsleur should be.  This is a great tool and free, not in the current meaning of free (i.e. free for a few days then pay), but free as in no cost - ever, no ads, no pushes to upgrade, the only investment that is required is your time (so I guess its not really free ...)

Headings: I love Doulingo so much!  ðŸ‘�ðŸ˜‡
Base_Reviews: This app gives me a great experiences to learn new languages. It teaches me from the basics to the high level step by step. I would recommend to everyone who would like to learn new languages to strart with Doulingo first. Thank you so much for providing us an excellent service Doulingo!Kai ðŸ˜‡

This app is amazing! I t goes over everything you need to. Earning ingots makes it a fun experience. You also get to play with friends and family, make your own home page and it tells you when and if you need to go over lessons. I give this app a 5 out of 5 stars!

Easy and fun to use! I have my doubts I can really reach fluency with just the app, but my German reading skills have definitely improved. I may not reply well, but I understand more and can navigate my way around much better even after just a couple of days! It's super easy to get in a few minutes a day, and it's enough like a game that sometimes I'm on it for much longer.

This is a truly wonderful program, but I am not a texter, and typing answers on the Kindle is very tedious and frustrating to me.  I wish they would make this available on a regular computer, with keyboard and mouse access.  Too often a slight mis-tap gives me an incorrect response, and taps on a small word (like "I" or "a") simply don't take, and I have to keep tapping them over and over to get them.

This works very well and I use a little every day. I find I learn better with this than with Rosetta Stone. The comments provided when you make a slight error typing or in accents is very helpful. It graduates you to higher levels as you learn. This is very encouraging for learning.  Having you speak a sentence in the language and then grading your result is very helpful feedback.  This is provided free making one wonder what the business model is.

The content is beautifully crafted, grouped and presented. Following goldilocks "just right" feel -  my French lessons were complex enough to be challenging while simple enough to persist through the lessons- at least for me! Focussing on complete language development be it vocabulary, spelling, pronounciation or other aspects it also comes with fun bonuses like lingots - so, you just need to bring along willingness to learn when you come to the class! :) I would highly recommend duo lingo to all language lovers :)Merci beaucoup, duo lingo team!
It's free and helps the kid in spanish.

Headings: I Wish I Knew About Duolingo Sooner
Base_Reviews: If you're not using Duolingo, you should be. The App provides a simple way to learn any language. I have a set goal to practice French five minutes a day and often stay on the App longer because the interface is user friendly and even fun! I tell everyone I know about this App. Quit saying "I want to learn Spanish one day" and start now!

Headings: I think this is a very good program. They use pictures
Base_Reviews: I think this is a very good program.  They use pictures, voice recognition, and recorded voices to aid you with the learning.  The sound quality of the recorded verses isn't the best but you can more or less make out what they are saying.  The give you daily email reminders to prompt you to study.  The only down side to the program is the limit choice of languages.  Otherwise, a very good program for learning a new language.

My love of  Italian music prompted my learning the language.  I'm so glad I found this program!  Now I find myself singing along and understanding a lot of it already after only a few lessons!  The program is really easy and fun at the same time, making understanding of the language just fall into place!  My son now uses it and I have it on every device I have! Love, love, love it!!!

Fantastic, easy to learn program and fun. Besides the written language you also get voice prompts so you hear how to say it. By the end of the first lesson, I could say several phrases and even a week later I still remember them. That is pretty good for woman  of 61 who is on several medications that cause short term memory loss. If you don't have memory problems, you will love this! If you have memory problems, you will love this! Win Win!!!

Headings: Great tool, but the Kindle version needs work
Base_Reviews: I love this app! It's easy to use, and reinforces the things I've learned in  class. But, the Kindle version doesn't give the option of using accents (at least, it doesn't for Spanish). The windows and  apple version do. The kindle app doesn't mark answers wrong for not having the accents, so you can still use it and  learn, but I feel like it builds bad habits. And, I wish there was a "vosotros" option, rather than just the Latin American version.

Headings: pretty good app for keeping your memory fresh
Base_Reviews: I'm always skeptical of language apps because  they're usually pretty limited but this turned out to be great. I've been learning French for the better part of 8 years but I'm not constantly practicing like I should so those basic words and phrases start to fade but this has really helped in keeping my memory fresh. Only thing I don't like is that the vocal exercises are a bit difficult because the app doesn't always hear me properly.

Headings: love this app, it goes great with the website
Base_Reviews: I use this app a lot. It is one of the strongest tools I've found to get me practicing French on an almost daily basis. There is more to learning a language than just this but practicing consistently is extremely important. Sometimes I play more than I intend because I'm close to finishing a section or completing a level or even passing a friend. My only gripe is that the one in the Kindle store doesn't keep up with the Google Play store.

They really make you work hard to learn a new language. So many real life scenarios and as you progress so does the work. You can test out your skills with others threw the online community. You also can translate web pages to earn your keep. You can't get bored because there's always something new to do and learn. I like how it helps you learn even if your late in life trying to learn a second language.

I'd always wanted to learn a second language.  I have a Rosetta Stone program but was very frustrated with it.  They never speak English making it extremely difficult to understand the proper grammar rules.  Duolingo is a wonderful program in the fact everything is explained in English.  Give this program a chance!!  It is very entertaining and additive in a great way.  If you've always wanted to learn another language, give it a try!

Headings: Fun, Easy to Use, and a Great Way to Learn!
Base_Reviews: I came across this app, because I was looking for a way to learn German, but without having to pay the price of Rosetta Stone. This game was exactly what I was looking for. It is a great on the go app, and is very easy to use for all ages. You can learn almost any language using this device and FOR FREE. I like how the app has matching games, pictures, and even voice recognition to make sure you are pronouncing the words/sentences correctly! It also gives you the option to turn off the voice recognition. I am thoroughly impressed with what this app has to offer!

Duolingo is a fun and easy way to learn another language. It's a little easier on a computer, but fun the same. The only problem I have is I don't know how to delete languages on my account. Apparently I am learning four languages now. And, they don't state the word very clearly on French. But otherwise, muy bien!

Duolingo is such a great app for language learning that exposes you to a variety of languages.However, while playing on Duolingo, it is VERY important to remember to also use materials to supplement your learning! Just using Duolingo and nothing else won't help you much with understanding grammar. In addition, I would also recommend you to use the web version as much as possible! The mobile version is slightly easier than the web one because writing out a sentence is just tapping words. :)Have fun!

Headings: EXCELLENT - levels get progressively harder, and it's all free
Base_Reviews: This has been a great app to review and deepen my Spanish. It's similar to Rosetta Stone in some ways, but I actually like this (FREE) program better.  There are great exercises to work on grammar as well as vocabulary, which is important, and each "lesson" is pretty short, so you can easily fit one in every day.  You can test out of each level if you're more advanced, so it's not boring. Highly recommend!

So well designed.  I took French in high school, so I do believe it's easier for anyone who has already studied how to learn a second language.  But this program is so pleasant and the strategy is excellent.  I'm doing well and enjoying the process.  Some additional materials will be needed, especially for learning verb tenses and possessives, but I would recommend this program highly for all beginners.  And...........it's free !

Headings: Best app I've seen to learn Italian
Base_Reviews: This app has a nice combination of written, oral, and aural practice. Also, it does a nice job of mixing the words together so that I have to remember each word individually as well as phrases.I knew some Spanish, which may have made this a bit easier, but other apps I've used to try to learn some Italian (for an upcoming vacation) have been little more than glorified flashcards. This app makes me recall vocabulary while actually using it, which makes it more fun and interesting, thus I am learning and retaining more.

Headings: this is the greatest app ever conceived. no, really tho.
Base_Reviews: this is an a amazing app and I'm so glad SOMEONE finally had the good thought that paying at least $500 to teach yourself a language is ridiculous. ive done Rosetta stone and this is not only comparable,  but better. it gives you "lingots" as prizes for doing perfect on quizzes, and then you can use those to buy stuff for your character,  or even bonus lessons I already speak Spanish,  I learner it inhigh school andill admit,  I'm really good at language. but you don't have to be to use this thing. I also like that it keeps track of your progress on a graph. it makes me want to study harder and harder each day so I get more XP than I did the day before. it truly is an amazing little tool. I work as a receptionist and I study with this app probably about 4 hours a day. I think to learn a language effectively,  you really have to do it everyday. right now, i'm teaching myself Portuguese. I plan to work my way through all the romance languages.

I've been listening to German for years now. I started because I love music and as it stands I love musicals one of my favorites has never had an English translation. So I've watched it in German many times. I know the story so I can generally recognize some words. But when I started duolingo it's like it all clicked. Everything I already knew made sense and I was able to rapidly increase my skill and better yet...I did it for free. It's one of my favorite apps now not only because the presentation makes it easy to practice anywhere but also because it made practicing fun!

This is a fun way to practice language. I got it before I took a French class, and I learned a lot of vocabulary and had a head start, but I wouldn't recommend trying to learn a language just through the app because it is harder to learn the rules, conjugation, etc. You get much more out of it when you use the app alongside an actual class.

Headings: Good for forming a habit of practice.
Base_Reviews: A good tool for basic practice of words and grammar. I am using to form a habit of daily practice. I recommend the app.

I'm surrounded by bilingual, Spanish speaking people, and I thought it was time I made the effort to learn Spanish.  Simple, easy to use, app. My favorite part is, I can go back and repeat a lesson, for a refresher or if I think I've done badly. Pictures to help you learn, voice commands, and sentence structures. It's fun too ðŸ˜Š
Translate review to English

I'm a linguistics major and there are some definite advantages to using this app- the fact that it lets you practice pronunciation and translating things from the target language to the native language and vice versa is very useful! It also is a great way to practice vocabulary and I love that it sends a reminder every day to practice! The downside....it has very few phrases that you would use in a real life situation..."The shark is red, I am a butterfly, the cats are drinking tea..." part of the reason language programs do so poorly in public school is because you learn very few ways to apply the language to real life. Great app but I would use it alongside another.

Headings: I like if for what it is
Base_Reviews: I like if for what it is. If you are a complete novice in a foreign language it helps you develop a vocabulary base. It lets me practice basic language skills, but it will give you no instruction whatsoever. If you are like me and want to understand why certain verbs are conjugated in different ways, the difference between words that appear to have the same or similar meaning, or grammatical rules, you will need to find other resources.

You practice reading, writing, speaking, and listening, giving you a full experience with the language. You can also hear from the learning community about things you're struggling with, which I've found very helpful.

This app is FABULOUS when I can't get on my computer but still want to keep my streak going.I do have one criticism, which is that it doesn't have buttons for accented vowels, so you do get reminded "watch your accents" but at the same time, it is not helping you remember to use them since you can't put the accents in at all.

This is interesting.  My brother has been using it for a while and got my son and me interested.  My son has done it daily since he downloaded it.  We'll see if we learn anything long enough to be able to casually speak a few sentences.

I had been thinking about investing in the Rosetta program when this popped up on my kindle apps.  I tried it based on everyone else's reviews and was pleasantly surprised.  It is fun to use and they repeat, repeat, repeat in different ways that make the lessons stick.  I am married into an Hispanic family and learning Spanish is my way to try to fit in a little better, or at least know if I am being talked about!

I definitely think that this is great for learning. I first started using this for school in Spanish class, but now I'm taking my after school time to learn some French too!I suggest this for learning. It's definitely worth your time. â­�

I really like this app.  I've never been fluent in Spanish but took some classes in college.  Having forgotten a lot of what I learned, I needed to brush up on my Spanish since my wife is from Costa Rica and we travel there every so often.  I can tell I'm making progress and I don't study nearly as often as I should. With more practice, I just might surprise her family next time we go.  The test out feature is really useful--you can skip the drills for things you already know.  I like the format. I like how you are required to answer in English and in Spanish, as well as listen to Spanish. Again, great app.
Excellent second (or third, or as many as you want) language skills. Employs many ways of learning. Wish I had more personal motivation to use it!

Headings: This is a great app for learning languages
Base_Reviews: This is a great app for learning languages.  I'm using it for Spanish and my daughter is using it for French.  It's a lot of fun and reminds you to do a little bit each day.  It also has you review things you've learned previously so that you don't forget.

My daughter is studying in Paris this semester and I am going to visit her. I wanted to surprise her by learning a little French.  Duolingo has been perfect for me!  I actually enjoy using it daily on my kindle fire.  A lesson does not require an absorbant amount of time. In the short time I have been studying using Duolingo I have already learned many phrases and words. I feel confident that by the time I leave for Paris in the spring I will have mastered enough French to impress my daughter!

Headings: Duolingo - Improving My Spanish Language Skills Is Now Fun
Base_Reviews: This is the best free product that I remember ever getting. What a fun way to improve my Spanish language skills. It allowed me to test out of the beginner stuff, and put me right where I belong to start learning. It's quite amazing the way it picks up on my mistakes and gives me extra time to learn what I don't understand. I also like the way it covers reading, writing, AND speaking. Then, to boot, I feel like eventually I will be contributing to translating all of the world's books to every language. What a visionary Luis von Ahn (founder of CAPTCHA) is, shown by his desire that every book on earth be translated and available to every person on earth. And he made it FUN.

love it, love it, love it! it is easy to navigate and i find myself noticing what i have learned as i go through my day. it encourages more learning and gets more and more challenging as you learn! i like the reminders that pop-up as well.

This is such an effective app, and I'm now bilingual, thanks to this application. The only things I would like is that it should work in no-WiFi areas, considering some people such as I have a tablet, that cannot have data. The other thing is I'm trying to teach my brother Spanish, but he says that even with the little green owl, this application isn't exciting for younger people wanting to learn a new language.

This is a fantastic app for those with an unquenchable linguistic thirst. I'd like to see a few additional languages -- mostly ones that don't use the Latin alphabet (Arabic, Mandarin, Korean etc.) as well as maybe a dead language or two (e.g. Latin). Other than that, I've no complaints or suggestions. Thanks ^.^
My kids love this app and it works great on their kindles

It,s fun, and easy except for the pronunciation, but I guess I have to get used to it.I gave it 4 stars because I have not been able to understand the lady.Patience, my boy, it will come with time.Thank you

Headings: missing the facebook sharing but still love it
Base_Reviews: I'm learning more every day. I can understand some Spanish but now I'm becoming more proficient with speaking. I wish they didn't take away the option to share progress on Facebook

Headings: A wonderful app to learn a language.
Base_Reviews: An excellent app. if you want to learn a foreign language.You can learn at your leisure.You can decide how much time you should devote per day and plan accordingly.They have a daily routine to persuade you to learn andyou get a daily reminder, if you miss your schedule.That's great.Vijayan.

This is a clear easy to understand tutorial that I can do at my own pace. Can double back and refresh when ever I feel the need. My daughter is even using it now. I have told total strangers about it. One of my three wishes would be to be thoroughly fluent in every language ever spoken on the planet. No this isn't that good. but it ranks right up there.

Headings: Good basic french lessons totally free
Base_Reviews: I don't think I'll be able to speak fluent french because of this program but I do a lesson almost every day and I am now able to read basic french which is all I wanted from the app.  I enjoy it, its easy to use and does progress as you learn.  Oh, and it is totally free !!

Headings: It would be nice to be able to turn of the pronunciation exercises ...
Base_Reviews: My son (8) uses this for Spanish, and I have my students who need enrichment use it for Spanish. I use it for French. If you keep getting the pronunciation wrong, make sure you are speaking into the microphone of your phone. It would be nice to be able to turn of the pronunciation exercises so that one could practice while commuting, etc.

It is very early in the game here for this app.,but so far very impressive in the direction that it has taken me.I love their format for learning a new language and it has been rewarding so far ,I'm only into lesson number 2 but their is no reason why ,given what I've seen so far that all the lessons won't be just as much fun and challenging as the first two.Just for the sake of interest I am taking lessons for Italian.Will update as the program continues.

Whether your learning strength is auditory, visual, or vocal, this application addressees it. Many simple reviews, many opportunities to review, and instant feedback. I think the main shortcoming is that occasionally an input answer is rejected in one example, but accepted in another, even though the context is the same.  Overall, I really like the lessons and find them effective and appropriately challenging.

I have tried Rosetta Stone and I believe Duolingo to be a superior product.  There is a substantial amount of material from which to learn.  I am at an intermediate level as I have been trying to learn Spanish for years.  This app has all the basics plus a more advanced level when you are ready for it.  I also like that the app uses a variety of words that have the same meaning.

Duolingo is great for anyone who would like to learn a language. Although it teaches better if you have a microphone on your device (so you can work on your pronunciation), you don't need it. Headings: This Is A Great App and You Do Learn
Base_Reviews: Fun and addictive.  I do Spanish and French.  Recently I took a speed Spanish course on line.  After using this app for weeks, I was ahead of the game when taking the course.  I never took Spanish in high school.  So apparently,  I actually learned something from this app!  I already understood the grammar rules and I knew most of the vocab already.  If I hadn't been usiing Duolingual, the course would  have been much too fast and too short.  I averaged 100% on every times and only missed one question on my final exam!The exercises really don't change much.  You are given a sentence in either the language you are learning or your native language to translate. If you set it, the exercises will also include you having to repeat a sentence in the language you hear.  (You can opt out if you are in public place and don't want to suddenly shout out , "I see a green pig" in Spanish in public).  Sometimes the speech recognition is iffy.  Although it seems to work much better on my Kindle than my phone.  The game runs very smoothly and doesn't crash (there was a very short period when it was crashing after an upgrade).If you don't understand why you got something wrong, you can immediately go into a forum discussing the sentence.  Usually there is a Duolingo staff person explaining, why the sentence is the way it is. Sometimes the sentences are a little weird and not something you would do in real life,  Sometimes the translation in English is a little off.  Anyway, you do have an option to send a notice to Duolingo that your answer should have been accepted if you got it wrong.The game, um, app has rewards that keep you going.  You an earn lingots which you can use to buy stuff in the store.  You earn lingots for going through an exercise without missing anything.  You get three hearts for each group of exercises. You can buy an extra one in the store.  There is a social aspect in that you can follow others.  But I don't see the worth, unless they are avid users like I'm.  There's an incentive to use it everyday so you don't break your streak.  You can also get notification or email reminders daily.You learn through repetition until you understand the grammar.  No grammar is explained.  There are not list of conjugated verbs.  From the very beginning, you are translating sentences.Research this app there's a great story behind it.  Then go view the Ted Talk video.

I'm a fan of this app.

Headings: A 100% FREE learning app based off the famous website
Base_Reviews: The Duolingo app is based off of the website with the same name. It currently has lessons in Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and English. This is a complete course that teaches you a language in bite sized pieces with a fun method. You start at the bottom of a tree and work your way to the top where you can win a trophy. By the time you are done with your tree you will have 1500 words from the target language in your vocabulary. You'll able to read and write in the language and maybe even enjoy some television. How do I know? I've completed my Spanish tree and am now brushing up. I'm currently level 17 in Spanish. Yes, you level up, because this is a game-like environment designed to inspire you to try harder to learn faster.Duolingo can be free FOREVER because they use translations provided by users to sell to companies like CNN. You are providing a service (translating) in exchange for getting a service (learning a language).If you want to learn a language fluently on your tablet get this app and the Memrise app (which is also based off a free website).

this app is great!! It allows you to fully understand and learn a language for free. It is very easy to follow and has a listening activity and a hands on. The languages are Spanish,German,Italian,and French. This app also has visual to make it a lot easier to learn the language and alot faster. It has all of the aspects needed to make a very good app to learn a language on. SO WORTH IT & FREE HANDS DOWN BEST APP

I like to study languages, it's kind of a hobby. Duolingo makes it really easy and fun. I think I could actually get proficient in Portuguese within a few months if I work with Duolingo at least 30 minutes per day. That's not bad! I can imagine that kids would do even better than adults because they take to the technology so much easier. I hope they add more languages!

Headings: I've enjoy the application for the different learning levels
Base_Reviews: So far, I've enjoy the application for the different learning levels. It's a nice plus to connect with other that can "challenge" you in pursuit of achieving more in desired language. Not sure if one likes that it does the constant reminders of practice time, but sure every good application has ways of modifying things.

Not only is this app super easy to use on my 7" fire, it gives me daily reminders so I don't even have to remember! Been using this for a few months to learn Spanish and German. Not sure I consider myself very fluent in either yet, but think I could definitely get by. Fun and easy to use. I look forward to spending a fews minutes each morning using this app.

I love this app. I had heard good things about it and I can confidently add to the praise of Duolingo. The method for teaching is simple and allows you to learn how to form simple sentences from the get go. This is useful in order to see the grammatical structure in which sentences are formulated in whichever language you're learning. You can click to see what other learners have asked/replied to to the same mistake and even contribute to the discussion. For some learners this is a key point for the learning process. I wanted to keep practicing Spanish from English and practice French from Spanish.  Sometimes the voice recognItion is a little glitch on my Kindle Fire HD. However, I use the app every day. I love this app. It generally picks up my voice correctly, and the program has been excellent in helping me relearn Spanish and pick up German. Trains you to speak, write, and read. I love you get to practice spanish and Learn a lot of new words and you can go to the area where it explains if you miss something th  only reason I gave it 4 stars was because some of the levels have no training instruction you have to of had some spanish to know it or you get it wrong so it doesn't teach first or explain why you got it wrong only other people learning the language but you do get to practice alot

I have numerous books an have taken classes in the States and Central America and I feel this is a fun and engaging way to study Spanish. Great language program!

Our of every app I've used, this one is the best. Every other language-teaching app throws you random words from the start, but this one has pattern that allows me to easily learn every word I need at my own pace.
this app combines userability with an interactiveapp that does not make learning boring.some areas of improvement could be providing explantion for controversial rules or tougher to understsnd logic

This app is so amazing! It is good for kids, adults, and elders! It teaches you how to speak, write, and use the words of a certain language of your choice. Headings: for new and "just to brush up" learners
Base_Reviews: I downloaded this app to brush up on French while I took an intermediate college class. I was surprised to see that I was still learning words and phrases that I hadn't covered in class. The creaters use Roedger's learning technique, which improves learning dramatically. My 10-year-old is a beginning learner, and he's picked up a lot of French. I love this app. I hope it stays free, without ads. I'd gladly pay for it.

Using Duolingo to learn French, and so far it's working out really well (I'm only about 5 lessons in). The lessons are easy to follow, follow a good pace of introducing new words/concepts, and the app/navigation is really nice. I've used it on the web on my laptop, on my Kindle, and on my Android phone and while there are minor differences, it's easy to use on each of them.

Headings: Great app for the casual learner
Base_Reviews: I've tried the elementary levels of both French and German and have come to the conclusion that this is a great little app for the price. Kindle fire has no mic, so it never prompts me to do speaking bits. But I also haven't had a problem figuring out tenses or grammar, as the other reviews suggest. Very intuitive play. The only problem I have is that you need to do at least a little every day, or you will forget  what you learned. I don't think you will ever achieve fluency with a language app, but this will take you through a lot of the basic vocab and structure.

Headings: Don't waste your money on something else.
Base_Reviews: This is about the best imaginable app for what it does. I think it would be great if it had more languages (I.e. Mandarin, Aramaic, Arabic, Yiddish, Latin, Ancient Greek, Elfin, etc.) Using this helps a lot with reading, writing and understanding the chosen language. I am thoroughly satisfied with this app and look forward to any improvements. Thank you.

Headings: Duolingo a good way to learn a language.
Base_Reviews: This has been quite a surprise.  I thought maybe I could learn just a few words to help me when I travel but was happy to see that not only do I learn what can help me there but words that will help me converse with my gardner for example.  Although he speaks English he is more comfortable with Spanish and it gives me a chance to practice.  If you use the mic  you get feed back on how you sound when you speak and if you are pronouncing the words correctly.  You can't beat the price when companies that teach languages can charge hundreds of dollars.  I also like the convenience of having this on my Kindle so I can learn and practice whenever I want.  The only drawback that I can see is that they have a limited number of languages that you can learn at this time.

This program is set up very well.  I know spanish, and so far, I haven't learned anything new, but it is good for refreshing the memory.  There are mistakes though.  I don't know how much confusion this could cause a beginner.

Easy to use, and learned some French. I didn't have money at the time to pay for the rest of the French class, but would recommend this app to anyone wanting to learn basic words, some phrases, time, numbers, and a good start to learning a new language. :)

Headings: A great tool to help you learn a new language-but you gotta practice!
Base_Reviews: I've taken 2 adult ed classes in conversational Spanish this spring and find I need to keep up the learning process because I have a long way to go to be somewhat proficient in speaking this language. I saw this app in time magazine and loaded it instantly. I practice writing what I hear, multiple choice and also speaking the words. This is fun and I'm learning and building on what I've learned in class.

Duolingo is a great way to learn languages. You can learn to read, write and speak whatever language you want. And you can get extra lessons like flirting or idioms in the shop plus other cool things like outfits for your owl or tools to help you during lessons. And for all you Star Treck fans Duolingo offers Klingon lessons. :) Great app!!

Decided to brush up on my French.Fantastic approach to learning; listening, repeating, multiple choice and writing. I was especially happy with the initial placement test.Well done! Maybe I'll try Spanish next as a beginner.

Over the years I have bought several CD's from various companies and some of them quite expensive. I found Duolingo to be SUPERB to all others as it allows you to travel through at your own speed and lets you know when you have successfully completed an area. Then occasionally it throws in "old stuff" to help you stay fluent. I LOVE THIS APP! Thanks SO MUCH!!!

Headings: Awesome tool to help learn languages. Can't believe it's free.
Base_Reviews: I've been using Duo for over six months to learn Italian, and I still can't believe it's free. You may still want to use other websites to learn grammar and more vocabulary, but you definitely want to use Duolingo to learn how to put everything together. Maintaining the daily streak might be the best tool I have to make sure I keep learning.

This is a remarkable program!!.  While it isn't Rosetta Stone, it is a very close second and you can't beat the price.  I bought several language books in French and Spanish, but Duolingo is much easier to use and learning can be fun. Headings: Best free app for foreign language!

Headings: Great app to practice and learn a new language

Headings: Great Way to Learn New Languages
Base_Reviews: I've actually not tried this out on my Kindle Fire yet, but I thought it would be a good idea to have it on there, just in case. I do have this app on my iphone though. I've found that it's a LOT easier and more motivating to use this app on mobile devices than it is to do it on the computer. Don't get me wrong, the website/computer version is good and well, but can be a little cumbersome. The app, if you've installed the right keyboards, which I don't think is very difficult (easy on the iphone, not sure about the Kindle yet. It was a Christmas present so I still am figuring it out), it changes automatically to the keyboard you need for each section of the lessons. I'm currently taking several languages, and it's nice to have the proper keyboard, a specified layout, and frankly, a whole lot less hassle.The downside is that the app takes longer to get the site updates. I use this mostly on my phone and tablet. Good for 4 of the languages I study.  More fun than games and you learn a lot on the 4 levels of language learning: reading, writing, listening, and speaking. I also recommend for my ESL students.

I've tried a lot of language apps, paid and free, and Duolingo is the best one.  Most language apps teach child-level vocabulary, one word at a time.  Duolingo uses complete sentences of increasing complexity from beginner lessons to advanced conversational language use.Every sentence of every lesson also has the option to discuss and comment. Headings: Using it 32 consecutive days & counting! Need prior knowledge! You will learn spelling and grammer! But doesn't explain/teach!
Base_Reviews: Over 20 years ago, I lived in Italy for 4 years (not consecutive) and had several group lessons but despite the efforts of my various instructors, I just didn't have the patience to learn the grammar.  My knowledge of vocabulary was good enough for me to communicate and function but I never could get the hang of conjugating verbs, learning about the articles, and spelling words properly.  Later lived in Latin America for 4 years and that messed up my language skills big time!  So, now I speak both languages very poorly - just throwing out words to make a mishmash sentence.  A couple years ago I went back to Italy and they asked me if I could speak english because they couldn't tell if I spoke Spanish, Italian or some unknown language!  (Note: My native language is American English)So, I'm returning to Italy again for a 2 week vacation and I'm determined to be better this time and not embarrass myself.  So, I got Duolingo on Feb 20th and believe it or not, I'm truly addicted to the program!  I have a full time job and when I come home I'm tired and yet, every single day, I spend 1 hour to 2 hours working on these mini lessons from Duolingo!  Funny, they are kind of addictive.  They force you to learn the language by making you hear the language, speak the language, interpret the phrase back and forth between languages, to spell it properly, and put it in the correct order.  If you do it wrong more than 3x then, it kicks you out of the lesson and makes you start over, but the lesson is different the next time around.  Now, you would think one would get discouraged, I mean, I've had to redo some lessons about 6x, and yet, somehow, the way it is structured, it makes me want to keep at it and do it right!  I mean it is working on me, one of the most stubborn learners!So there are a multitude of topics at every level (beginning/intermediate/advanced) and within each topic they have 4-8 different minilessons in each topic.  It visually has a graph that shows you where you are at.  And, even when you think you are done with a topic (whew), every couple of days, that topic reopens and they make you practice it again so you don't forget!  Wow!  So, even with my background knowledge/vocabulary of Italian, I'm still at the very end of the beginners (Level 8; 335 words!) and I've been working hard for a month!  Oh, another downer is I was working on it for 12 days and suddenly it reset and told me I was back on day 1.  I thought it did that every 12 days but now it says I'm at 16 days. (IF ANYONE READS THIS FROM DUOLINGO; I WANT IT RESET TO FEB 20TH THAT I'VE DONE IT EVERY SINGLE DAY!).The downside is that if you have never ever studied a latin language this would be super hard for you.  I think if you already know a similar language like spanish and how it is structured, it will be easier for you.  However, if you are a person who has never studied a romance language and absolute beginner that only knows Ciao, etc..and hever had a lesson, then, you will have a hard time.  Also, if you are a miserable speller in your native language, learning to spell Italian will kill you because it is so difficult to get all of the vowels in the right place.  I have many times translated a very complicated sentence from english to Italian, only to get it counted wrong cuz I misspelled 1 letter!  But, it forces me to really think what I'm writing and how it all comes together to form a complete sentence.  Also, it really doesn't teach you the vocabulary or the grammar rules, at all.  I kept failing the lesson because I wasn't sure what some articles meant because they seem to mean different things at different times.  Yesterday, I finally broke down and got a grammar book so I can look up what all of the articles mean.  So, this program works for people who are already familiar.  I'm worried that when I get in the more immediate level, I might need to study before using this as it isn't really a good teacher - doesn't explain or introduce new concepts.  Good for people that really want to tighten up what they already know and go farther.

Headings: Easier to use than Rosetta Stone, and free!
Base_Reviews: I am using this app to brush up on Spanish (learned 30 years ago) and German (picked up from my German family, but never studied formally).  I don't know how it would work for a language you were never exposed to before, but for brushing up purposes it is excellent.  You can easily test out of what you already know and focus on the areas that are weaker. (This function can be turned off. If you're in a noisy, crowded place or don't want to be overheard.)The program, breaks down the learning of the language in much the same way as Rosetta Stone. That is to say that unlike your high school language teacher, you're not just learning active verbs or inactive verbs or pronouns in each lesson. You are learning phrases and how to build conversational structures.A couple of words of caution, however.The app assumes you have a basic understanding of the language you're learning. For example, I have a high school level knowledge of French, and this is been an excellent refresher course and brought back much of what I learned in school. However, when I switched over to try and learn a few German phrases so that I could be just as helpful on our trip, I found it more difficult and challenging to to engage with the program. That isn't to say, that someone could just try to pick up a language (for instance, I'm also working with the Italian section of the app. So when we go through Italy, I'll have some knowledge of the language.Second, the app won't let you advance to the next segment until you can complete the first without four or five errors per segment. Although it's not, strictly speaking, concerned with spelling as long as you're in the neighborhood, it will deduct points if you consistently spell something wrong or don't use the right accent over a letter.Overall though, I have really enjoyed using this and would recommend it to someone who wants to brush up on a language or learn key phrases in order to travel.

Duolingo is the most motivating language course I've ever seen.  It feels like a game, and is designed to keep you moving forward.  It is also concise and surprisingly comprehensive.  Each part has a lesson to read at the beginning, and if you don't understand why you got an answer wrong, there are discussion boards for each and every question.  So far I have not had a question I could not get the answer to, and I am almost halfway through.  I especially like how it encourages me to go back and strengthen skills in constant review.  This ensures that what I learn will eventually get written in my long term memory, its just a matter of time and consistency.  Anybody who uses Duolingo frequently, consistently, and for a long period of time (at least a year) will learn a new language.  Go ahead and get the answers wrong as often as you need to.  The algorithms are designed to program the human brain and you will eventually find yourself getting answers right in spite of yourself, even if you don't quite understand the grammatical principles behind it all.  Duolingo is built on principles of positive reinforcement, making it easier to persevere.  I use it in conjunction with short stories written in the language I'm trying to learn, and movies also in the language with English subtitles.  In only a month, I am understanding so much morevthan I ever thought possible.  I can't believe its free.  Its better than programs I've paid good money for.

Headings: Duolingo is an awesome way to learn and practice new languages
Base_Reviews: No two ways about it, Duolingo is an awesome way to learn and practice new languages. If you already have some education (say, old high school classes you wish you'd taken more seriously), it offers an assessment to put you at the right level, considering what you might already know. Duolingo breaks everything down into lessons that build upon each other, and prompts you to practice as you go, returning to older lessons to cement them while learning new words and grammar. Having used Rosetta Stone several times in the past, I think that Duolingo's program is just as good as the $400 software, and Rosetta Stone doesn't prompt users to go back to earlier segments over time.Duolingo also has a unique system where language learners help translate webpages (often Wikipedia) from their native language to the one they're learning, and will direct users to a level-appropriate page. This is a great way to see the language in a larger context, and helps give that feeling of confidence and mastery of the language.

If you are looking to learn basic conversational phrases, this is not the right app. I would like to learn the language enough to speak, read, and write, so use this app to practice daily and continue to add new vocabulary.
Easy to use. I work at my own pace. Has already helped me at work. I get out of this app what effort I have put into it. Best one out there!!!!
Enjoyable all for language learning, it won't take the place of a good teacher or curriculum but is fun and helpful as an extra supplement.

This app has so many benefits. First, its free and user friendly. I think that anyone probably thirteen or older could use this app. Second, it's a fun way to learn.  I like that is shows me words  im becoming weak on and I have to practice those words again. Hoping this app helps me on my way to fluency.

This app is a delightful combination of having fun and learning something. Instead of messing around on the internet when I get bored, I can do Duolingo. The quality of instruction is high - I recently went abroad and was able to get by with what I'd learned through this app.

This language learning program is comparable to Rosetta Stone and it's free to use and easy to practice because the app is on my phone and I can practice any time like while  waiting in stores while my wife shops or when my kids are at sports practices.  very convenient.

Very fun and I look forward to playing it each day. It is almost addicting, exciting when you reach the next level. It has helped me learn new phrases and words. It has different learning methods, you can write what the person says, translate sentences, speak into your microphone when asked to say the phrase on the screen. Because of all these different ways you not only get better at the language but also improve the pronunciation too! Verdict= great app- definitely recommend for people seeking to be bilingual.

Headings: Improve or learn a new language
Base_Reviews: If you want to learn or better a language that you just learned, I highly recommend this application as well as being practical, it is also excellent for children, now there is no excuse to say no.

I homeschool my 3 children. We had trouble finding a foreign language curriculum that stuck; then we tried DuoLingo!!! I love how easy it is and how it makes sense. My youngest (3) is able to use it with a little help, and my older 2 love learning different languages. We love that it's free and that there's a large selection of languages to choose from.

The Duolingo app for the Kindle is really nice.  I have used the pc interface, android and ios and I really like how it operates on the Kindle.I am use a Kindle Fire HDX 7" and everything is clear and crisp on it.  I'd say the only problems I run into are the occasional restarts when I am in a lesson or the times I open up the search tab when I am trying to type an answer.Another minor issue is the auto correct on the Kindle sometimes incorrectly fixes your answer so it is best to check over what you have typed before hitting check.Overall, Duolingo is a fun language learning tool that in many ways reminds me of Rosetta Stone without the high cost to go along with that.Right now in app Duolingo offers Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Italian. Dutch, Irish, and Danish are in beta and Hungarian, Swedish, Turkish, Russian, Polish and Romanian are hatching.

Headings: A really good approach to learning is used
Base_Reviews: I am using it for Spanish and Italian.  A really good approach to learning is used.  Good practice exercises.
Has helped me a great deal. Would definitely recommend.

I am 72 yes old and learning French.  I never took French in school so it is a challenging subject to keep my mind active.  It really gives you a chance to learn all aspects  of the language at your speed.  You can go back and redue your steps so you don't forget what you thought you had learned.  Who knows I may go to France someday.
