Headings: This is a great app. I downloaded it for my daughter so ...
Base_Reviews: This is a great app. I downloaded it for my daughter so she can have something constructive to do on her tablet. I'm really glad I did, she loves it and is learning really fast, what a wonderful and fun way to learn a new language.

I've only been using Duolingo for about a week and I'm surprised how much I'm able to retain from one day to the next. I don't pick up languages easily and I just wanted to learn enough to get by. I think I may end up being able to do more than just get by.

This program is so great, I can't believe it was free.  Apparently there are multiple languages in this program, but I chose English to Spanish.  It's divided into lessons, and each lesson has multiple parts, including speaking.  It will even send you a reminder, if you so choose, so your activity is consistent.  What have you got to lose?  Definitely try it!

Headings: love the concept, now for an improvement/suggestion
Base_Reviews: Really like the app.  I am more positive about actually retaining the language I want to learn.  However, the app never could understand what I was saying into the microphone... not sure if it just didn't pick up anything or if my inflections were always too far off to count.... might be helpful if it played back what it heard.  Also would be nice if the app could change the keyboard language to the language it is asking the user to write in and every it back to original keyboard language upon quitting.... Spanish and English are at opposite ends of the keyboard language list on my Kindle fire.
Easy daily reminders - chose a five minute daily lesson.  Perfect - I can do more if I have time!

Headings: This is a great app to learn some basic Spanish and doesn't require ...
Base_Reviews: This is a great app to learn some basic Spanish and doesn't require a lot of time each day.

I love this app, usually with language apps it's either hit or miss with most of them on the miss side. This app actually teaches you not only vocabulary but also grammar in a very concise step by step guide. I'd say it's almost like a mini Rosetta stone. My problem comes when I'm in the middle of a lesson and all of a sudden it goes back to the menu. I'm using kindle fire HDX so I don't know if that has something to do with it. It's incredibly annoying and frustrating when you have to do the same lesson five times because of crashes. I really enjoy this app, and it's actually helping me learn some Spanish but I'm going to be forced to stop if I can't move forward. Please fix this.

Headings: Issue on kindle fire showing pictures
Base_Reviews: We are having issues with the app showing the pictures on our Kindle Fire 8's.  We called the Amazon support people and from what they can diagnose, it's an duolingo issue.  My kids seem to really like the app.  Being at the beginning level, they know enough Spanish to figure it out without the pictures but worried it won't be so easy as they advance levels.  Hoping we can figure out what's wrong.

Headings: Easy to work on a language for just a short time each day!
Base_Reviews: I really like exercising my brain with this app. It is fun to learn some Spanish and doesn't take much time at all. I really like how it customizes for you. It shows you the words you need to work on the most.

Admittedly, I am a language geek. But I have been coming back to this app over and over since getting a Kindle for Christmas to learn Italian, and my 11-year-old daughter has been enjoying learning French. It turns language acquisition into a game with new challenges and rewards at each level. Typical challenges include speaking into a microphone, filling in missing words, and typing in sentences that are dictated or written in the other language. It's a little frustrating to have to type accurately in the target language, though.

Headings: Fun and free! Not a ripoff like many "free" programs
Base_Reviews: I love using this app! I took this foreign language in college but haven't used it til now. Duolingo is an excellent refresher AND is teaching me more than I learned in college!

This is such a great app and I can't believe it's totally free - I love it!!!It teaches through a variety of methods, all intertwined to really immerse your brain in the learning process. For instance, I'm currently learning Spanish; I have to select correct photos with the Spanish word identifying them, translate Spanish phrases into English and vice versa, speak Spanish phrases to see if my pronunciation is correct, etc. This app reminds me a lot of Rosetta Stone (I was able to use that program for a time through a former employer) but a little less overwhelming; each lesson is very short and sweet meaning you'll actually do them (I remember dreading - and eventually stopping altogether - the RS lessons because each was at least a solid hour commitment each day which is a total buzzkill when you factor in work, social, and volunteer time). So, you can do one short lesson or if you've got the time breeze through several...the app views either as an accomplishment. And I love the owl reminders in my inbox each day because seriously: I can be a space case.This is a solid app for anyone wanting to learn a conversational foreign language, which is really the point, right? I mean, all I want to be able to do is communicate with other human beings in the language of the country in which I'm traveling (without an electronic translator!); who cares if I'm able to conjugate my verbs correctly every time I say something? I'm looking forward to learning a few languages with Duolingo!:)
This is one of my favorite learning apps. I was so glad when I discovered it is completely free. You can set daily goals,  and it helps you strengthen the areas you need help with.
Program was easy and fun!

I find it a useful and fun refresher course that helps me to communicate better with my customers at work. Both of my teen daughters use it to assist with their school French classes, keep up over the summer, and to learn additional languages.  Don't hesitate - just get it.

I use duolingo to teach English to Mexican kids.  I also introduced a friend, a retired Mexican pediatrician, to the program. He thought he could not learn English, but in just a few months he can carry on a conversation.  I use the Spanish course and it is perfect for my needs.  My friend is 75 years old, I am 68 years old, and my kids are 8, 10, and 11 years old, proof that the program works for all ages.

The Duolingo App was something I stumbled upon and I am glad that I did. I have all intentions to live and travel abroad and in order to enhance the experience I'd like to know the language. Granted that all languages aren't on the App itself, the ones that are available are top speaking languages. I have taken courses in both Spanish and French middle school through college and do not remember as much as I would have liked (no offense to my instructors, they were wonderful). Using this app is fun, effective, and encouraging. I'm looking forward to learning and speaking as many languages as I possibly can.

Headings: This is a great! I'm actually learning the language I always wanted ...
Base_Reviews: This is a great!  I'm actually learning the language I always wanted to, and they make it so easy!

Headings: It's Fun to Learn Something New
Base_Reviews: I heard about Duolingo from one of my friends at work. I am learning Italian right now and I would love to relearn Spanish. It is a fun app and it seems to be fairly easy too.

Headings: Easy to use.  Well laid out.
Base_Reviews: Very similar to expensive language lessons, but easier to use.  You can go very quickly through lessons if you're familiar with words & phrases.  Its great if you want conversational lessons.  I'm about 1/4 through so far, and I've picked up enough to have a basic conversation in Spanish if I have to ask directions, basic questions, etc. when travelling.

Headings: Very easy to use and learn a new language
Base_Reviews: Very easy to use and learn a new language!! I LOVE this app and I've been telling everyone how great it is.
This is a very good program.  It starts you with baby steps then gradually adds more challenging content.  It is not boring or too difficult. Kids and adults will love it.  I'm learning German.

I must admit I had my doubts with a free app.  But I have been amazed!!! I have been able to brush up on all the spanish I learned back in high school.  I am sure it may be a little bit more difficult for someone with no spanish background...but you would catch on quick.  It's fun and rather addicting.  At this rate, maybe I'll be fluent in a couple weeks :)

Duolingo is hands down the best app for learning a different language. It's fun, educational, and very easy to learn. Plus, it doesn't cost an arm and a leg. I have been using this app for a couple weeks now in the hopes of being decently fluent in another language when in travel out of country. And I gotta say...I picked up learning that language FAST. Thanks duolingo! 5 stars for you.

Headings: Duolingo is a fun way to learn a language
Base_Reviews: Duolingo provides a quick and simple method for studying another language in your free moments. You can sent your own pace and feel satisfied as you look back at your progress. The lessons are short, but educational. The app keeps track of what lessons you need to review to keep sharp. Finally, an app you don't have to feel embarrassed to admit you spend time using.

App works smoothly and provides a great way to improve your foreign language skills--similar to what happens when you go somewhere and just learn the language by hearing and speaking it. I'm relearning rusty language skills, and it works great for that. Look for some other reviewer to get a perspective on learning a new language from the beginning.

I have used Rosetta Stone and DuoLingo works better for me hands down. I find it more intuitive and easier to use. I am brushing up on my Spanish and now learning German. They make it so easy to learn new words and sentence constructs. I highly recommend it.
Wish they had Russian! It works good and its fun, just wish they had more languages, and more outfits for Duo.

I've been using the app to study French for a few days now and I'm really enjoying it. I have used Rosetta stone in the past and I think this is pretty comparable.  There aren't structured grammar lessons, you just jump in, start translating and learn by doing.  It's easy to use and fun!

I am living in Peru and I use this to build my spanish skills.  It is great for vocabulary and you can learn spanish, French, Italian or German.  It's very helpful, but make sure to check for updates every once in a while.  My sister had a better update than me for a long time and I didn't know how to update it.  Great app all around!!!!

Headings: This app is wonderful. It is enjoyable and actually helps you learn ...
Base_Reviews: This app is wonderful.  It is enjoyable and actually helps you learn the language.  I really like the new 'bots'  that allow you to have a written 'text' conversation with an invented native speaker.  Really brightens up the dull repetition needed to remember what you learn.
I love using Duolingo because it's easy to use. I can move at my own pace and repeat the sections as needed. I really feel that I'm learning through practice and repetition. Great app!

Great app. Learning the basics of 2 languages, about 5 minutes a day for each. Able to "test out" of a section or go back and do a "review" module rather than a full set of lessons for a section. UI is very nice, easy to navigate, no random app closing or freezing. Very pleased with the free Duolingo app.

Very user friendly - even tracks the words you struggle with and offers extra training in those areas to reinforce your knowledge.  My only complaint is the limited number of languages on the app (maybe 5 or 6 available for English native speakers), but it works wonderfully and is GREAT for a free app.

I've found Duolingo to be an excellent tool for brushing up on my French. The app seems to assume a certain minimal level of experience or outside learning, so I don't know how appropriate it would be for someone trying to use it to learn a language from scratch, but as a practice tool, it's great. One quirk is that the tablet and phone versions basically synchronize, but are not the same (there are no pronunciation exercises in the tablet version), so if you use both, you have to keep going back and forth. It's not really a problem, it just means more practice, which is a good thing!

Headings: Too bad they don't have Japanese
Base_Reviews: Sadly, they don't have Japanese, however I've been learning Italian for fun, and the style is intuitive for learning. You can compare your data with friends and sign up through Facebook as well. All for free. Go at your own pace and learn a new language. German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, French, and/or English, the choice is yours.
Love this, makes learning a language fun and easy. BUT the Kindle app needs upgrading so we can access our club. Currently have to do that on the cell phone. Other than that, highly recommend.
This makes learning fun. The repetition and interaction between languages really helps. I like use of sentences that are practical and useful for everyday conversation. Thanks

I have some Spanish background, but this revives what I've forgotten. I like the way you can keep going over things until you feel you have mastered them. It can be easy to test out without really knowing all the material. I also like their nagging emails that remind me to keep practicing every day. And it's free! Amazing!

Its amazing how much the little positive reinforcements make it more like a game than work. Each lesson starts easy then progresses. Doing about 10 minutes a day and it may take months to get good. But that is better than promising myself I'll work hard at it later and procrastinating.

Headings: This program is very user friendly and I'm doing fine so far
Base_Reviews: I took Spanish in high school, and remember various words--but I have acquaintances who don't speak fluent English, and I was hoping to somewhat improve my Spanish.  Hopefully just enough to have a conversation.  This program is very user friendly and I'm doing fine so far.
This app has all you need to learn a language except for the dedication. If you bring that, though, you will for sure learn whatever you want!
I like very good products.

This is probably the best free way to learn a foreign language available. I got this for my mother to learn Spanish. Now I'm several lessons into Italian. I only wish there were more languages available (such as Chinese). Hopefully more will be added. I highly recommend this app.

Headings: Great program and a fun way to learn.
Base_Reviews: I find this to be a very successful program. The lessons are short but well organized.  It is very easy and quick to review a lesson multiple times which makes retention easy. Each lesson uses a variety of learning strategies that aids learning and keeps lessons interesting. This is the easiest time I have had learning a new language. Give it a try., it is actually fun.

Headings: ... give the app 5 stars because it really is great. It's comparable to Rosetta Stone and is free
Base_Reviews: I have to give the app 5 stars because it really is great. It's comparable to Rosetta Stone and is free. In all honesty, though, I don't use the app often, it's better to just go to the website or use the app for apple.

Headings: not intimidating and more fun than you might think
Base_Reviews: The easy progression and chances for review make for a comfortable way to learn.  I appreciate all the embedded pronunciation by a native speaker and the chances to have my pronunciation evaluated.  I bought an introductory Spanish book to help me see some of the basic grammar.  It feels like better use of my time than Candy Crush.

Excellent app. Very informative and fun. Works differently on various devices but builds vocabulary and usage on a step-by-step method. The ability to listen and speak as well as type in Spanish are a bonus. I gave recommended it to several friends.  Look forward to doing it daily.

A perfect compliment to the Beginners German class I'm taking.  You can spend  as little as 5 minutes a day, although you'll probably find yourself doing it even longer.  I recommended it to a friend for Spanish, and she also loves it.

Having been studying Spanish since high school as well as my years in college this is a great way to practice and keep the skills learned fresh and keeps brain active. Highly recommend to anyone and hope to learn Portuguese with this app in the near future once I finish the Spanish lessons provided.
Just started using it. We're traveling to Costa Rica and Spain thus year. So far, I like the user friendliness and repetition.

Headings: What a Fun Way to Learn Another Language!
Base_Reviews: This app is awesome!  It is fun and keeps my interest.  I studied Spanish, French, and Italian when I attended highschool.  I graduated in 1973.  It has been amazing to see how much I've retained.  Try Duo Lingo.  My 3 granddaughters are also studying with This app.  They love it.

I learned j' fait bon mea s it is good 5 starts great program easy interface uses both spoken and written Interfaces....I wish there was a flash card to introduce new words.... And more on masculine/ feminine subject agreements and ending....merci beaucoup ( French word I didn't know a week ago)

Headings: GREAT WAY TO VENTURE INTO A NEW LANGUAGE
Base_Reviews: I love most the encouragement it gives to move forward day after day.  I have also increased my vocabulary which reinforced throughout the drills.

I love love love this app! It is super fun, and challenges me on many levels. The app helps me translate English to German and vice versa. I also learn grammar and vocabulary in a fun way. The best part for me is using the microphone where I must put my German pronunciation to the test. There's no cheating here! Try this. You will love it. I've tried many different ways to learn German, but this one is the stickiest. Have fun!
best language app. it helped me with spanish so much. i went from failing the class to a B. its very quick to open and learn
I would like to try the voice more often but I am only able to try it when they say.

I like this app but it surprises you by putting up words you really haven't learned. I've been using some of my French to guess what the words are. It helps to go back when you feel like you don't know something. I do like that it goes back and takes you back into the categories it thinks you need to strengthen.

Headings: Best Free Language Learning App Out There
Base_Reviews: At first, learning a new language on duolingo can be difficult but once you begin to use it more often, it becomes easier to pick up the language. The app is designed to help you learn how to speak the language, recognize what is being said in the language, as well as be able to write in the language.  I especially like how at the end of learning a section, there's an extra module that tells you what you were weak in doing and provides additional exercises for you to complete to master these weaknesses.

Headings: Very easy to use, yet challenging
Base_Reviews: Trying to learn French and German at the same time.  I love the ease of the program.  So tough writing at the same time.  I am focused more on reading and listening which this program does well.  Free, which makes it great!

I love my Duolingo app but I always get email that say "keep the owl happy." Because you're suppose to practice every day and it drives me crazy!!! The only reason I'm still using it is because of my love for French. So if you have a strong love of a culture or language and your willing to fight for than this app is for you but there are not many people out there that are like me and are willing to fight for what they love. Even if it's something as small as learning a language.  Your critic  French Girl

AWESOME app, very well implemented. Actually makes learning languages fun and it only takes a few minutes each day. I'm doing Spanish and I hope they add Japanese one of these days as I've always wanted to learn that.

Headings: Great app for knowledge and entertainment!
Base_Reviews: Wow! This is a super little app for learning or just reviewing and updating your knowledge of your chosen language. I recommend this app to my friends and former students to keep current on the language especially when you are not using it on a daily basis. It is great and really enjoyable. Never bored in the backseat on family trips anymore!
Per favore,grazie!!! My husbands relatives are "fluent" in italian,. Dispiace. No.  Fabulous  app!!! Can't  believe its free!!! Ciao! Grazie!!
I've used many language programs for several different languages and this is my favorite.
I love this little app. I wish it had Tagalog but it fine for me and my kids to learn Spanish.

This is a nice app to brush up on your foreign languages. Or for kids to learn. I'm brushing up on my Spanish have not tried others yet. You can go against others. You go in stages till you get it right to unlock others, but if your advanced you can go to next stage. Nice app for all ages that can spell.

Learning a language couldn't be easier! This is a fun and easy way to learn a language! What you are inclined to do is create an account and then do some exercises to help you Learn the words. There is a basic category for beginners, and an advanced category for people who have already learned some things. I find this pretty helpful and better than most Language-learning resources :)

Great app! This is an evolutionary way to learn new languages. It drives you with gaming features and makes your progress visible and shareable. Great for adult learners who are able to extract concepts from examples.I have been using this app to learn all languages  supported, and it has been a great  linguistic adventure. I wish it had more consistent paces across languages so I could compare and contrast the same unit in each language.Not 5 stars because of occasional content errors and synthesized pronunciation. Also, providing a lexicon and/or some other sorts of summarization of what had been covered would help me review.
Duolingo is a great hub for learning or brushing up on languages. I love the convenience and simplicity as well as the option of some fun competition with yourself or with friends. Great app!

Headings: Definitely recommend this app to everyone!
Base_Reviews: I absolutely love this app! I recommend it to everyone and have gotten a few people hooked. I am trying to learn Spanish and wow I am amazed at how much I've learned from this app, and it's free!!

Headings: fun app and im really learning!
Base_Reviews: I've always wanted to improve my Spanish. This is a fun, easy, self paced way to do just that. It helps that I have a high school Spanish foundation. Knowing the alphabet, pronunciation, and remembering a little bit  of verb conjugation helps. Some aspects of this program seems as though that is assumed. I'll have to see how I do when I move on to a language I have no foundation in...

Duolingo is a really fun app that helps you strengthen or learn a new language. It is easy and walks you through your learning really well. It is effective and really educational. For example I am a middle school student learning French in school and Duolingo really helps me memorize it at home. It is really easy to use and not a waste of your time. It is so good that I guarantee you will love it!

In retirement, my husband & I are traveling more extensively, often to Europe. I studied Spanish & German in high school 50 years ago. I chose Duolingo to brush up on Spanish. After completing some of the early levels, I thought I could complete some of the early levels in Italian to prepare for an upcoming trip to Italy. Duolingo is fun & easy to use even for me. I am one who doesn't learn languages easily. I hope my 8 & 10 year old grandsons might have interest to learn alongside me.

I do have some experience in languages (Air Force language school, Rosetta Stone, text books etc.), and while no app can replace having multiple native speakers all day every day (the Air Force language school), this one is solid. My daughter challenged me to try it briefly, and I'm on a 815-day streak! (and downloaded it for my newer Kindle). It only takes a few min a day, it does good to encourage and challenge you, and while it's imperfect, I think it works to just oversimplify the grammar at first, then differentiate it as you learn. You can also choose from a large variety of languages (so I've tried some others for fun), as well as reverse it (i.e., learn English as a native speaker of the other language), which adds to your learning (since instructions are in your actual target language and some of the specific vocab is different.

Base_Reviews: Cannot say enough good things about this app.  A fun, interactive way to learn and practice new languages. Spanish, Italian, French, German, Dutch, Danish, Irish, and others.I like that DuoLingo allows you to practice English to Spanish. Spanish to English, translation from written words and translation from sudio (occasionally difficult to recognize, but it does come with a "slow" option that phrases the sentence word by word instead of the rapid pace of a native speaker.  I would recommend that you also visit the DuoLingo.com webpage on occasion as it allows you to access sections like "Tips and Notes" that did not seem to be available from the app.Please note that DuoLingo does not actually provide "lessons."  It's more a learn as you go.  You can read the tips sections or just jump straight into practice sentences, but each sentence has a link to a "discussion" section where other Duo users (native speakers of either language) can help explain confusing grammar aspects.  I really enjoy the variety of "testing"... from translating pictures, to multiple choice, to picking the correct words out of an available group, or just typing in the translations without hints.  The web page also has the opportunity for "timed practice" so when you are reviewing lessons you feel you know well, you can set a thirty second timer and see how many translations you get right (extra seconds are added for each correct answer).Again, if I could give this app more stars I would.

Headings: Fantastic free app; not perfect, but great value and tries to keep the learning interesting and varied
Base_Reviews: For a free app, I was blown away by the value.You start by taking a sort of placement test.  After that, you're introduced to the "tree" of available subjects, in which you focus on one part of speech or related group of words: "Pronouns" or "Science" or "Past Present" or "Numbers".  These are collected in rows, and you have to finish all of the subjects in a row before you can move onto the next.Each subject consists of several "lessons", usually between 3 and 8.  You can work through the lessons one by one, and you'll be able to access definitions of words you don't know to help you learn.  Once you've completed all the lessons, you've finished the subject -- for now.  There is an alternative path to completion:  if you feel confident about the subject, you can "Test Out" by taking one roughly 20-question exam, and as long as you don't get more than 3 questions wrong, you can complete the subject that way, too.As you start filling in the tree, subjects you've already completed will open up again, so you have to keep going back to previous subjects to practice them and learn new vocabulary.  It's an effective way to keep you from "learning" something just long enough to finish the subject, but not really retaining the information.A word on the lessons themselves:  they're fairly varied.  I'm a native English speaker working on the Spanish tree, and I get questions where I have to translate a phrase or sentence from Spanish to English or from English to Spanish; spoken English where I have to type the Spanish translation and vice versa; spoken Spanish where I have to repeat it in Spanish; match-Spanish-words-to-English-definitions sets; and "choose all correct translations" multiple-choice questions.  In addition, you can access a kind of comments section for each question, where other Duolingo users post tips, comments, questions, and explanations.  You can also flag a question if you think it has an issue, and Duolingo reviews these and makes periodic updates.To up the fun factor, you earn "lingots" as you complete lessons, which you can use in the store to buy various add-ons.  You can also see your friends' progress, and a little competition can help keep you motivated!  You can also set daily email reminders and edit your goals to keep yourself on track.Overall, it's been a great way for me to refresh and improve my Spanish, which I haven't used in over ten years.

Great app! I originally downloaded this app to learn Portuguese in order to talk to my Brazilian roommate's family. After two weeks I was able to translate some song lyrics and understand parts of conversations that my roommate had with her boyfriend. I am most of the way through the Portuguese language tree and still loving it. Now I am planning to use it to learn a few other languages, as well.Some cons (possibly specific to Portuguese): The translations are not exact, so knowing some Spanish or Italian is helpful for learning the grammar rules. Also, the pronunciations are a little odd because of the computer voice; they are sometimes hard to understand and do not give you a good idea for how to say the words (e.g., "de" is pronounced like "jay" in the app, but native speakers say it more like "jee"). Listening to native speakers and doing some reading in addition to using the app would be best, but Duolingo is an EXCELLENT place to start (especially if you don't want to or cannot take a formal class).Some pros: You can report any errors in the translations and they get taken care of pretty quickly (one that I reported was cleared up within a day). Each question in the app also has a comment option where you can ask questions; there are native speakers who monitor the forums and can respond to your questions relatively quickly. There is also an online component that is really good for working on spelling. The website that is connected to your account for the app also keeps an index of all the words you have learned and has explanations about grammar rules. Finally, in the app, unlike on the web version of Duolingo, you can turn on voice recognition if you want to work on you pronunciation.Some additional notes: The sentences are created by an algorithm based on the words you have already learned. As a result, they can be a little odd (e.g., "A borboleta escreve um livro" means "The butterfly writes a book"). Some people don't like this about the app, but I think it's entertaining.Overall, I love the app! Even with some of the cons, I still give it 5/5!

Headings: Fun and a great balance of easy + challenging!
Base_Reviews: I downloaded this after trying several other, free "learn a foreign language" apps.The others were so frustrating, I mentioned the problem to friends, and - thank heavens - someone recommended Duolingo.I was skeptical at first, but once I got into Duolingo's lessons, I realized they really do work. They're exactly what I needed.I'd learned French in school, many years ago. I haven't spoken French in over 10 years, and only now and then recall it when I'm watching a French film with subtitles, or watching a Poirot mystery where it helps to know what he's muttering in French.Now, with a neighbor who speaks no English and our own planned move abroad, I need to refresh my French language skills. I'm starting from a point of recognizing a few words and phrases, but I couldn't say more than "Parlez vous..." ("Do you speak...") or "Je m'appelle..." ("My name is/I call myself...").So, I'm starting French again, not quite from scratch... but close enough.Duolingo is perfect for me. It's fun. It's light. It's free (though there may be ads on it, according to some reviewers), and I quickly learned: Pay attention during the easy lessons, because a challenge may be ahead. You'll need to remember those words and spellings.So far, the only reason I'd pay for the Plus version is because I want to support Duolingo. I love it that they provide these great lessons in basic French, free to everyone.I'm giving this an enthusiastic five stars. It's a light, fun course that feels more like play than serious study. But it still produces great results and learning.

This FREE language learning course gives bite-sized lessons. Each lesson consists of a series of sentences teaching one area. You either translate into French, translate into English, or speak what the speaker has just spoken. The program passes or fails you on each response. There are several differences between the smart phone/tablet app and doing it on-line using a laptop. In the laptop program you cannot go on until you get the pronunciation mostly correct. In the app version after two attempts it moves on. In the laptop version when you translate from French into English you have to spell every word. In the app version the words are at the bottom, scrambled, with one extra word and you pick them one at a time to form a sentence. When you translate English into French you have to spell every word in both versions. The laptop version is better but the app works if you don't have a laptop with you. The same user name and password you use on the laptop will take you to the correct place in the app. I used it with an Amazon Fire HD 6 and Bluetooth headphones because linking the headphones with the Fire was easy and inking the headphones with Windows 8.1 is beyond my technical capabilities. Headings: I am I right to give 4 stars?

When trying to learn Chinese It is unclear to the English novice speaker if it is Mandarin, Cantonese, pinyin (?) or what. Then it asks you to type in the Chinese translation, but presents only an English QWERTY keyboard. Second, there is no way to go back it you accidentally make a wrong selection from the word choices. There is no verbalization of the Chinese words that are shown on the screen. This is not so bad with, say, French, where the phonics are similar (even though not the same), but with Chinese, Korean, etc. it is a drag and it makes learning MUCH more difficult. Notwithstanding these shortcomings, I think iyou can learn something if you struggle with it. But it shouldn't be a struggle.I am giving 4 stars for effort, but feel much work is needed to make the app user friendly. In short, I like the concept and encourage it, but would want many upgrades in presentation. And the price is right (aka FREE)

Duolingo is currently offered to students of Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Irish, Russian, Turkish, Polish, Hungarian and Romanian. I have worked with Duolingo's French program on and off for several years, so I can say from experience that it just keeps getting better and better. There are a few bugs, particularly in the recorded words, phrases and sentences, but there is also the capacity to give feedback when something does not sound right, or when the program is too rigid in its interpretation of "the" correct answer. There is a lively discussion group  among students, and this helps to resolve misunderstandings when they arise, as well as serve as another feedback mechanism for the developers. There are passages in the students' target language to work on translating, which range from Wikipedia entries to novels, and here crowd-sourcing really comes into play, as the finished products are being prepared for upload to the web. If working with a language you have not studied previously, I find it can be helpful to have an introductory text to the language to consult, but even that is not necessary, as there are valuable supplementary materials to be found online (e.g., at the about dot com sites for each language.)I have recently been working with the German and Italian programs, and I am enjoying them as much as I do the French. These programs can definitely become addictive, but in the best way possible, as the learner sees her/himself making progress in reading, writing and speaking the language, even one which may have been studied for years. And I haven't even mentioned the fact that this fascinating program is free! And that it moves seamlessly between the computer, smart phone and Kindle Fire! Headings: English to Spanish has lots of material and starts simply
Base_Reviews: Based on Duolingo's rating system, I am an advanced Spanish-language learner. I got this free app hoping to brush up on my very rusty Spanish skills. For this purpose, I have been very grateful for the option to test out of each of the first three levels, and then to test out of each individual subject after that. I haven't yet reached a section test that I can't pass, but I've been studying Spanish ever since elementary school. Taking the tests provides a decent review, but I'm not sure it will help my conversational Spanish much.I certainly hope that the sections I haven't reached will cover the subjunctive as well as the future and conditional tenses. I haven't seen anything in the vosotros form either, so this may not be the best way to learn the Spanish spoken in Spain.  The vocabulary is very text-book style. There don't seem to be any words specific to a certain region or even any colloquial phrases included. I haven't seen any cultural notes, either. Those are not necessary for an introduction to the language, I suppose.It looks to me like the lessons begin very simply and build very gradually, so it would be an excellent choice for a beginner. I'm not sure yet how far it will take you into the more advanced grammar.  It probably doesn't help with conversational Spanish, but a person-to-person setting is the best for that anyway.I'm glad I've had the chance to try this out. I think I'll get a taste for French or German next!

Headings: Good place to start, but more please.
Base_Reviews: I've only just started using this app, but find it pretty good thus far.Seems like it teaches you the way you would learn a language organically, through trial and error correction.  I know, through past language study, that Duolingo is, through that trial and error process, teaching you how to use formal/familiar, male/female, singular/plural, and the like, constructions.  But, it's very subtle if you didn't have a clue about theses sort of things.That leads me to one of it's shortcomings, at least for me, and the reason the app is a 4 and not a 5.  Namely, it doesn't provide a whisper of explanation of these sorts of things.  It would be a great help, for me anyway, if the little message that pops up when you make an error gave an explanation.  For example, you have (no pun intended) tu, usted, vosotros, and ustedes, which all mean you.  Now in English there's just "you," no (in order) singular informal/formal or plural informal/formal versions of you, though generally we figure that out through context.  So a simple, "you used tu (the familiar),when you should have used usted (the formal)"  would be helpful in my being able to separate the two in my head.  And, go a step further and give me an easy place to find that tells me when I should use one over the other.In the vein of more explanations, please; How about explaining (in an initial page?) what xp points are and how they are used.  Or the meter that goes around the microphone; is more better?  I tried really butchering a phrase and pretty much got the same reaction. If more is better, then I could aim for that.

I have to say that I am honestly amazed that this application. After all, it was free.However, (bet you didn't see the "however" coming) this simple program uses all the latest techniques for teaching a language. You can also download, again for free, a variety of languages.It uses what is generally referred to as an "immersive" method of teaching. Because of this it's essential that you have the ability to speak to your phone or tablet into a microphone and be able to listen to what the program says to you. But in this day and age I don't know of any phone or tablet that doesn't have a microphone and speakers.With the immersive method of teaching there is no long explanation in English (say you're learning French or Spanish). Instead you are presented with a variety of pictures such as a little boy or a little girl, and adult man or woman, dog or cat or dog and cat or any of what seems like hundreds of combinations on screen at a time. Well, you never see more than a few different blocks with different pictures inside of each of them and they contain the label in the native language you're looking to learn. A prerecorded voice will say the name of each object in the new language. Then quiz time starts.It starts by showing you individual graphics that you had just seen, for example the young girl, and you are presented with a variety of terms in the native language and have to choose the one that represents the young girl. Of course it tells you if you're right or wrong but there are no harsh buzzers that go off or anything that makes you feel stupid. After all, you are learning a new language. The process continues and you will be presented with other images and choices to identify them.But the application doesn't just give you a collection of words. After you attain a high enough score showing that you now know the words for the pictures you've been shown the program shows you how to string them together in meaningful sentences using the correct grammar. The final step, just to make sure you've grasped what it is teaching you, is to speak into the microphone of your device (in say, Spanish if that's the language you're learning) and the program either moves on or goes back a short way in the lesson if your pronunciation is off.Not only am I learning both Spanish and French using this program but just to make sure I'm not wasting my time I showed both programs to people who speak those languages natively. I also strung together a few sentences from what I've learned so far and was told that both the grammar and pronunciation are correct.As all reviews should end the question should be asked, "would I recommend this to a friend?" If you haven't gotten it from my review, the answer is an outstanding "YES"! I can honestly say I've never given ANY program such a positive, enthusiastic review. As a final side note, the method used here for teaching is the exact same method used by a program called Rosetta Stone. This tiny little app was free and still is as of the time of this review (April 9, 2014), to learn a single language using the Rosetta Stone program just at this level could easily cost you a couple hundred dollars. Thus the enthusiasm.

My French had improved drastically just in the short time I've been using the app.The app addresses things that may seem minor, such as, allowing you to easily change your keyboard setting from English to French and back, and using the microphone to provide feedback on whether you are pronouncing things correctly. Headings: More than just a way to learn a language free....
Base_Reviews: If you don't know about Duolingo, you should probably research it some.  It is so much more than a way to learn a new language for free.  This is a top quality program that will teach you to speak a major language in the style of Rosetta Stone.  It isn't exactly like Rosetta Stone and there aren't nearly as many languages, but it is free AND it is for a good cause.  The back story on Duolingo is that once you have reached a specific level of ability, you actually begin to translate books and websites.  You see, computers are really not very good at translation, but people are.  Once you are proficient enough, you will be translating actual webpages.  Your translation will be compared with hundreds of others to find what is correct (computers are good at this part).  Don't believe me?  Go to Duoling dot com and check it out.  Not only will you pick up a super helpful skill but you will give back to humanity at the same time.

It includes pictures asking you to identify words to sentence translation to auditory exercises asking you to type what you hear as well as a voice recognition utilizing your tablet's microphone to test your diction. I especially love the play back feature on various exercises, which allows you to listen to a native speaker and practice modeling after them.I have tried a variety of free language apps and this one is superior by far. My only complaint is the "bonus" lessons you can obtain as you build "xp" are far more advanced than the language you have learned thus far through the regular lessons. However, if you re-visit these bonus lessons after progressing further through regular lessons, they begin to make more sense.As with any language app, you have to be willing to put the work in. Headings: Bite-sized daily lessons mix variety and repetition
Base_Reviews: I studied French in high school and college years ago, and I've picked up a bit of Spanish here and there, and by reading some of the Bible in Spanish. I decided to pick up some German with Duolingo because I have a nephew who studied that. Well, that started out so well I decided to brush up my French and see what I could do with Spanish. Probably not a good idea to work on three languages at once, but I'm enjoying it and making progress. I was so rusty on French my attempt to test out of the Basics failed (just barely), but it's nice to know the option is there if you don't want to review from the beginning. Repetition is an important part of learning any language, but it can get boring. This program solves the problem by mixing up the styles of questions. It starts out very easy - some of the questions are as easy as tapping the picture of the word given in your native language with the target language below it. On some questions, you can tap the given word and see its translation, so you don't have to guess even if it is a new word (but guessing can be fun and doesn't "hurt" much!). Pay attention to the little words that go with them, though! In English (which is hard to learn in other ways) we just have "the" for everything, but in French and Spanish you have variations to match the gender and number of the objects (German has three singular forms, one being neuter, I guess). How do you know if an object takes a masculine (le or el) or feminine (la)? Practice, practice, practice! Take your time and think and memorize, and write words and combinations down. And Duolingo does let you go back and review skill sets. The instant feedback is much more enjoyable than doing written homework, but the German is making me want to get a textbook and do some extra studying! Some questions let you translate phrases or sentences by selecting from a choice of words, others let you listen to spoken words, phrases, or sentences and then select the words you hear. More challenging questions require you to type in the translation or words from memory. It even has voice recognition so some questions require you to repeat things in the target language. If it doesn't recognize what you say, it doesn't count it against you (lots of things can go wrong with voice recognition, such as background noises). If you can't get away from the noise or otherwise can't or don't want to use your microphone, you can turn off that feature and it will only give you the other kinds of questions. I've noticed that it also gives some leeway for typographical errors, although sometimes it's still counted typos as wrong and other times I've just been wrong but it was counted as a typo. It generally gets it right and the two kinds of errors balance out. I've typed in a translation when the task was to type out what was spoken in the foreign language, and it gave me a do-over. But watch out, if you make a mistake in your own language, it will count that wrong, too! English speakers had better know how to properly use "to," "too," and "two," for example. Or maybe using DuoLingo will help you with that, too! Daily e-mail reminders (which can be turned off) help you to stick to it.[ADDED LATER] Well, I'm up to Level 5 in all three languages, and I'm definitely feeling the pinch of trying to make it QuadLingo. As I fail lessons, though, previous skills re-open to show where I need to go back and practice more, which is a good thing. It's exciting to be learning these languages, and I'm thinking I might dig through my collection of language texts to add to and aid my DuoLingo studies, since I've gone and set myself a three-pronged challenge. I wish I'd thought of taking notes earlier (I just added that bit with this edit); I'm sure that would be enough to make studying one language a cinch with DuoLingo.

I've been using this app on my 7" Kindle Fire HD and my HTC One SV for approximately a week... maybe a week and a half now, and I absolutely love it!I'm using it to learn German... not sure what other language options there are, although I know Spanish and French are in there. So far I am hugely impressed. The app uses a combination of written, spoken, and visual cues/questions... so one question may ask me to translate a sentence from German to English, the next question might be to translate something from English to German, and the question after that may be to speak a sentence in German or to write a sentence in German that the app speaks (the app's voice is not great, but definitely serviceable)... reinforced occasionally by visual cues such as labeled pictures (i.e. a picture of a dude labeled "der Mann"... you get the idea after a bit).The teaching method works, I have to say... and this from a guy who always considered himself critically handicapped when it came to learning new languages.  Granted, I'm early into the program, but I am retaining a large part of each lesson, which is honestly more than I can say for my experience with Rosetta Stone.There are two cons that I've noted: First, and this may have been an individual problem, the app wouldn't let me sign in with either Google+ or Facebook... it has buttons for doing that, but they didn't work... so I had to go old-school and actually create a separate account.  Minor glitch, but still worth noting.  The second con is that in the course of the lessons, I haven't yet encountered a definitive explanation of certain rules of grammar, i.e. when to use one form or another of a verb. On one hand this is vaguely annoying, as I end up with wrong answers without being entirely certain why they're wrong; on the other hand, however, I suspect that this is actually increasing the effectiveness of the program, as this makes me really think about each word before I use it, and when I'm wrong, I really study WHY I was wrong, which ultimately increases retention of the language. So kudos for effectiveness, even if it is a bit annoying.Overall... freaking awesome.  Get this app.  I can't believe it's free, honestly, but as long as it is, get it!

Headings: Such a fun way to learn or reinforce a new language.
Base_Reviews: My grandson introduced this system to me as an aid in augmenting my Rosetta Stone and Pimsleur Italian lessons and it helps a lot. I am not interested in writing Italian and it is pretty easy to figure out close enough to read because it is such a phonic language but many words are blended and therefore difficult to separate for spelling purposes.  Pimsleur is all audio and I can listen to it in my car or at home so it gives me more flexibility from that standpoint.  Duolingo offers aids that act as reminders to help reinforce your learning and gives the explanations that are missing in Pimsleur.  Maybe it is me, but I find it helpful if I can see the conjugations of verbs to make those connections.  This also has a fun aspect to it so I find I resort to it when I have a few minutes here and there to devote.  Both Rosetta Stone and Pimsleur require a more disciplined approach that needs you to set time aside each day for language learning and reinforcement.  Best of all, it is FREE....how can you go wrong!

Headings: Better than my paid subscription to a language site
Base_Reviews: Really does help you learn a language with practice. It quizzes you to verify your understanding. It mostly asks you to select an answer without actually teaching you first -- so you guess a lot in the beginning. But that is not a bad thing. The process is engaging and ultimately inspires you to teach yourself without a physical teacher present. There are User Discussions associated with lessons, but I found myself doing additional Internet searches on certain words and phrases. The extra research significantly enhanced my understanding and helped me remember better.Also, there's a lot of fun to be had here. It offers multiple ways to learn (listening, speaking, writing and translating) which all serve to help you remember your new language. Plus, there is the "gaming" element that allows you to achieve points called "lingots" that can be traded for special learning modules. I gave this app 4 stars instead of 5 because it sometimes gave me "credit" for speaking the correct words when I had actually flubbed up the language. But for the most part, it was spot on!I actually have a paid subscription to a language learning site, but I find myself returning most often to this app.

Base_Reviews: It's not setup the way I was taught or would teach it, but the method used does work. Talk about remembering a lot all at once! But that's what the program does well; it introduces those new terms and makes you go over them multiple times to get it to sink in. Even when you go to the next lesson, you're still practicing a few terms from the last lesson!

Headings: A great way to begin learning a new language
Base_Reviews: I am at the very beginning of my journey to learn French, and this free app has made it fun and enjoyable for me.  This app starts you off by jumping in with both feet. No instructions really, just trial and error right away and I was pleasantly surprised at how effective it was.  If you miss a phrase, a little word balloon will open up showing you the correction. The best part about the correction balloon is the link to a chat page where other people have already asked questions and the incredibly informative responses. I've learned a great deal about the grammar and foundation of the language just from reading these back and forth questions and answers.  You are encouraged to participate daily which isn't a problem for me as I look forward to it. As you progress you earn Lingots (I think that's what they're called)  which you can use to purchase little fun add-ons for the app. What I am very happy with is how much content they give you. For French I can see the lessons go on for quite a while, providing more and more detail about the language. I've tried listening to French audio files and have even tried a free preview of Rosetta stone, but nothing I've tried before has been as interesting and informative as the Duolingo app. Highly recommended and I hope you enjoy!

Headings: Intuitive, Easy to Use, Great Between Devices
Base_Reviews: This app is fantastic! I've been using it for weeks now to learn Spanish. The controls are intuitive and I find it easy to learn a second language. I use this app on my laptop, my Kindle Fire, and my Android phone, and the app is great for that. It always keeps up on my progress, and I've had no issues at all. It's a great way to learn another language, and the best part is that it's 100% free. However, the one tiny issue that I have with this app is that you need to have speakers. This is fine when you're working on it at home, but in public places; not so much. It plays a word/phrase in whatever language you're learning, and you are supposed to type that word/phrase out. It's a bit awkward when one is in a quiet place (think waiting room at the doctor's office). You have to turn the volume way down and hold it up to your ear, or just wear headphones. This isn't a major issue, and all in all, I think that Duolingo is a fantastic app for people of all ages to learn an important life skill of being bilingual.

Headings: Good, if you already know the basics
Base_Reviews: I love this app. I use it to maintain and strengthen my Spanish skills; however, I do not find it very useful for learning entirely new languages. Instead of teaching rules and patterns, such as stem verbs, conjugations, etc., it requires the learner to memorize practically every aspect of the language down to the smallest details. In essence, there's no explanation of why. Why does the third person plural use this verb ending? Why do I use this past tense instead of that one (since in Spanish, there are two imperfect past tenses)? As a student of languages and their historical progression, I have found it crucial to teach languages according to rules, patterns, and conjugational conventions. This app, however, seems to overlook this extremely helpful principle. I had hoped to use Duolingo to continue learning German and begin learning Italian, but I will instead have to use a textbook to first learn all the necessary grammar rules and then use the app to practice and increase my vocabulary. Overall, it is a fairly solid aid to self-education.

Headings: An excellent resource and it really is 100% free
Base_Reviews: This is a great way to brush up on language skills.  I took Spanish in high school but made it my New Year's resolution to get back into it.  I love that this is totally free.  It encourages you to log in every day to practice the skills you've learned and add new ones.  It keeps track of your progress and can compare to friends who are also using the program.  It has a bunch of languages including Spanish, French, German and Italian and several others in the works like Turkish, Vietnamese and Polish.Each "lesson" incorporates translating from English, translating to English, speaking and listening exercises.  You can turn off the speaking and learning exercises.  I do. I find that it doesn't recognize my voice very well. I think part of that is my pronunciation and part of it is the voice recognition.Duolingo has both a mobile and online computer-based components.  You can use either one or both (all for free).  I like the computer version better.  It's easier to type on a real keyboard.  The PC version gives you more practice when you make an error, but the mobile version gives three chances before you fail the lesson and have to start over. I also like that the PC version has a translation mode and gives you an estimate of how much you can understand of the "real" language.There is a lot of pattern recognition and memorization involved.  There are some little tidbits in the lessons, but some things are very much missing.  I'm still trying to sort out "por" and "para" and trying to understand the personal "a."  (Feel free to comment with some hints).  Fortunately there are other web resources to back up this learning.I've almost finished the Spanish lessons.  I will probably work on Italian (while practicing Spanish) next.  It will be interesting to see if it's as helpful when I try a language that i have had no previous exposure to.

Headings: The VERY BEST language learning app!
Base_Reviews: I have had two years of French in school and used virtually every language program available. Here are my critiques:Rosetta Stone...didn't like that because it didn't present the material in a way that appealed to me or that stuck with me. Also, it frustrated me as it seemed disorganized and a backwards approach. Plus it's expensive. At least $400  for entire program. Pimsleur: it is pretty good actually. The one drawback to Pimsleur is that I sometimes can't understand exactly what they are saying, even after having two years of the language under my belt,  therefore, you don't get the concept of how the language is organized. Plus it is expensive. The pro to it though is that you can listen to the audio in your car or while cleaning house or jogging.FrenchPod: pros: you can download audio files to listen to wherever you are. The speakers have  a natural French dialog and then go over it bit by bit and explain the various uses of the words. You can alsodownload workbook pages to refer to.Cons: There us an extremely limited list of lessons, all of which are around 6 sentences to dissect. Also, there is no practice, either speaking or writing.Textbooks: Difficult. Boring.DuoLingo: pros:  you get to hear the audio spoken at a natural speed. Then you can slow it down so you can pick up on each word as it is enunciated. You are immersed in the language by having to type out, which forces you to remember placement of nouns and verbs etc.  It is formatted sort of like a game, so it doesn't feel much like work, and it is actually quite addictive. It's totally FREE! No ads either.Cons: it can get frustrating if you get an answer wrong because you miss points, so like with any "game," you might get frustrated if you're that serious about game points.I have learned FAR more with this app in 6  months than I EVER learned in all my previous years using other methods! It's fun and free and best of all...it works!!

Headings: No more reading recipes. Just watch the video!! I LOVE IT!!
Base_Reviews: I accidentally bumped into Food Network Kitchen 2 weeks ago (Jan. 2021) and it has CHANGED MY LIFE like nothing else in the kitchen has. I was down to Wawas gas station ready-to-go sandwich meals and could retire on what I've bought in Marie Callendar's Chicken Pot Pie boxes.My problem(s)? Which there are a GREAT many in the kitchen: I don't like reading recipes. I don't like listing out the ubiquitous "weekly shopping list" of necessary ingredients nor foraging the Walmart shelves figuring out where one gets the items. (Pro tip: Do you know where molasses is kept in the stores? Me neither.)SOMETHING had to give when I realized how upset I got when my local sandwich bar at the Wawas gas station was closed due to this pest called "Covid." I mean .. REALLY!!!I've had two large cookbooks I've owned for 5 years - still in their original saran wrap.  I could get full price for what they are worth today - mint condition. And they have big pictures in them - I think they do. Not sure. Never opened them. But much like people who join a gym with the intention to workout, the concept of cooking is "Nice."Forward 53 years (which I am today) and I have 2 siblings who do cook. But alas they live too far away for me to drop in for dinner. We all began sharing our recipes during Covid - to show off what we were doing in quarantine. They showed off their couscous on a bed of lettuce with fresh squash ... I showed off my latest Wawas $2 discount shortie sandwich - courtesy of the free gas app I had just joined.They showed off their fresh steamed asparagus with honey salmon while I showed off my grilled cheese sandwich with - might I add - a touch of melted butter (This was of course after I burned the first batch of bread by leaving it on high too long under the broiler).As you can imagine this gets embarrassing - me being the oldest sibling and all. My reputation was quickly falling to not relevant. And I'm a weight lifter to boot. It didn't help that my ex was a professional chef and I never needed to cook a thing. But this had to change.I went online researching recipe apps. I figured maybe I could at least READ a recipe on line. I looked up Betty Crocker (who, btw, is NOT a real person. Look it up if you don't believe me.). And I was bored with what I saw. More recipe reading. So I skimmed over the number of people who purchased the  various food apps - as I have more apps than I can count.I saw FNK - THOUSANDS of people!! I went .. "Hey, is that THE Food Network Channel?" I mean.. the BIG kahuna?WELL YES IT WAS!!!! Then I immediately felt dejected because I ain't no cook and I know the sandwich employees at Wawas by name. But curiosity got the best of me. I LOOKED. I OPENED the FNK APP. I saw my FAVORITE personality.. REE. I own her stuff from Walmart - all of it nearly (including the pie slicer!).I saw the videos. They were short. To the point (around 3 minutes) ... they told you the order of ingredients in the video. The FNK app created my grocery list FOR ME. I could easily add and remove items from the list. I could add my own custom items onto the list - food related or not. (Ya know - Qtips). t took me 15 minutes to figure out the app - it was EASY!!!!  ! can even call ahead now and have the ingredients all ready for me to pick up at my store if I don't want to do it myself. Free curbside service!I went HOLY COW ... KERI CAN COOK!!!!!Fast forward ONE week of owning this app ... and I have cooked meals that I can actually show off to my siblings (see attached photos - all made January 2021 in 1 weeks time. That easy! I never read a single recipe. I just follow the video. This FNK app is the bomb!!!!Best money I've ever spent on an app. And my goal is to no longer know the sandwich people at Wawas by name - not unless it's just to say, "Hi."

Headings: From Recipe to Grocery List without Over-Buying
Base_Reviews: You can use the grocery list as a running list of all one has in the house-what is crossed off is what you already have or don't need.  This is saving us from over - buying.  What is not to love about an app that scans recipes on web pages for you, saves them AND adds a recipe's ingredients to your grocery list?  This is not all - the app will sync your grocery list 2 your phone so you can do meal planning in the kitchen on a tablet then as you walk into the store, have your grocery list synced on your phone and you are ready to shop!

Love this app! It is so easy to use. Helps me stay organized and easily find a recipe with tags. Being able to clip a recipe I see on the internet and add it to my collections with pictures is wonderful!

I love this app!  It's perfect to store all of my recipes in one place.  It's such a chore to go from one website, blog, online recipe file to find the recipe you want.  Sadly I came across some of my old 'saves' to find the recipe has been deleted or the blog is gone.  This app keeps those recipes in ONE place along with my collection of pins from Pinterest.com. No more worries of loosing the recipes.A great feature of this app is that you can access the recipes offline.  This helps when you are at the grocery store to pick up the ingredients you need and there is no wi-fi.The larger Pictures and Grid View are a nice improvement.  I like having pictures for my recipes and being able to add pictures is a bonus.The added tag feature makes it even easier to find specific recipes without having to scroll through the hundreds of recipes I've saved.  (I'm actually over a thousand now:))The ONLY reason I didn't give it 5 Stars is that I can't use this app on my desktop or laptop (and currently not my Blackberry.  The app is only for Android devices).  I'd like to be able to add/edit recipes from there as I've been saving them in my bookmarks lists.  I ultimately emailed the recipes links to my email account and clicked the links from my kindle. I do understand from the Chef Tap website that this along with a cloud feature are two of the things they are working on.  Good.  I'll give you the fifth star when it happens :)  It'll be nice to share one recipe file across devices.  I've been due for a phone upgrade for awhile but I'd put it off waiting for the latest to come out.  The latest features on the new phones are great but since using Chef Tap along with a few other great apps from the Amazon App store I decided to upgrade to an Android phone instead of upgrading my Blackberry (kinda a tough thing since I've had a Blackberry for 10 years at least.)To save the backup file to my desktop I had to go through Dropbox because the app said the file was too big to send via email. This isn't really difficult so I don't count it against them.  I now use Dropbox for other things like sending my personal videos, pictures and other downloads to my desktop when I need more room :)  If you don't have a Dropbox account or don't want one you can manually save by connecting your device to your computer and saving the file that way.  The Faq page on Chef Tap has details.I recently saw from their FAQ page a way to transfer files from .txt .  This is an awesome idea I haven't yet tried.  But I will because I want to add my grandmother's recipe file.  Those are actually in a REAL recipe box on REAL recipe cards.  But that will be a project for another day.The Chef Tap FAQ page and Facebook page have lots of answers to help as well as being user friendly.  A really nice change from an app creating team:) They plan on adding new features and keep you up to date in a newsletter and on their facebook page and blog.  Looking forward to having the shopping list feature.Like I said earlier it's a GREAT app!  I don't mind the ads and usually don't but will pay for the ad-free just because the app itself is worth the money.

Headings: Fast and easy way to save online recipes !!
Base_Reviews: I have hundreds of cookbooks however Chef Tap is  a valuable app that  allows me to save recipes as they are shown from my web searches. I enjoy exploring advanced cooking techniques and being able to save recipes with the original formatting and illustrations allows me to save them. This is easy with the free app but I like the app so much that I have upgraded to the paid version to get the additional functionality. I use my Fire in the kitchen while I am cooking and follow the instructions for the technique and use the pictures to expertly "plate "the food as shown in the original recipe. I am currently exploring "sous vide" techniques with the Joule immersion circulator and there are an increasing number of recipes online for this method.

However, it can be done by adding words within the recipes and the app does a decent job searching for matches.I have had a problem with the 12 tomatoes site if trying to import from a link there out of Facebook.  To solve it, just go directly to the 12 tomatoes site.

Can always add your own favorite recipes and make changes to the recipes you have imported.  Recipies can be organized however you like.  There is an annual fee for this app and it is worth every penny.  Fee is much cheaper than buying cookbooks, magazines, etc.  The developers are very responsive. I think when recipes are set up as simply as possible (like on actual recipe websites) it works the best. I imported some recipes from a friend's blog (the main focus of which is not cooking) and they didn't import 100% correctly but it was easy to fix.Really, while things like that are a bit of a drawback the app tells you up front in the tour that recipes written in certain formats (such as being wordy) don't always import well. I wouldn't want to harsh on the app too much for something like that considering how it does import many things correctly.

Headings: Love but I could madly love...
Base_Reviews: I love Chef Tap App.  Pure and simple best app for recipes I have found.  And I have tried at least three others but I always go back to the Tap!  I would madly love with three changes or added features. 1) I wish the app could generate a shopping list from choosen recipes.  2) I wish there were subset tags.  For instance, Vegetables but within Vegetables could add corn and beans, etc. And 3) in a perfect world I wish I could share a recipe with a friend in a recipe template.  When I share now the email is one big text.  I wish what I sent them was in "recipe card" format.  In the most perfect world it would be in a template I could customize with my name and  cutesy photo!  I brag about how wonderful the app is I think if when I shared a recipe it was in a nifty format more folks would want.  I know a lot of old ladies who do not easily change!I use Chef Tap with my Kindle and I did upgrade and am happy I did!Easily imports from most sources, especially easy with Pinterest on the Kindle.
