But overall it's a great app to have if you like to collect recipes and cook. Beats pieces of paper laying around in a drawer unorganized.

After installing this app,find a recipe, open the Kindle "options" select "save to" and "cheftap".  It downloads the recipe to your Kindle then in a second or two, automatically imports to ChefTap (can take a minute). A successful import shows the dish name, a photo of the dish ( if available on the site), the ingredients, the preparation directions.  You can then edit it,add it to category(s), or find a photo if the webpage didn't have one, and add it.With the huge variety of web pages & their technical differences it is obviously going to be difficult to collect the right info, yet this app does most of the time. In the 6 months I've used it they have made many improvements in the importing accuracy and they track which websites don't import right then fix the process for that site. This app does something so complicated that I don't consider problems with a few websites (cookscountry.com is one of them) significant enough to take off a star, especially since they are so good about fixing problem sites. The down side is a Kindle problem not a Cheftap problem and that is that its a pain to enter my own or cookbook recipes since the Kindle doesn't support a keyboard (one finger typing a recipe is time consuming).I love this app and have recommended it to all my friends. I like having recipes in one place, on the Kindle, that i can use in the kitchen instead of paper or books. It makes the cost of the Kindle worth it to me.  I don't know of another app that goes to the website and imports both ingredients and directions with a couple of taps.  That alone makes it worth a lot, just in the time it saves me, as well as not having to print or get pen/paper, or track where I put the paper copy.The programmer is working on setting up cloud backup (a worry with the kindle) and each time you open the app it creates a backup and prompts you to send it to yourself until cloud saving is working. I do wish they had an option to use it on iThings as well as Android, but I will keep my Kindle for this alone if they never have an Apple version.I'm like the other reviewer who commented they couldn't believe this app hasn't gotten more attention. It is one of the most useful apps ive found and it is free.
Wish I had known about this year's ago, so nice not to have pages and pages of printed recipes.

I have been using this app for over two years. It certainly has continued to improve and evolve over time. Yes, to use the app for free, you can only have up to 100 recipes. I have found the annual renewal fee to be a minor issue. I am willing to spend a nominal annual fee to have the convenience of having my favorite family recipes, stored in the cloud and available on my tablet or smartphone at the touch of a button. I love being able to import recipes from different websites. No more newspaper clippings or recipe cards to lose. Also sharing a recipe with friends is a snap. Good investment for those who like to cook.

I absolutely love this app. It has a seamless interface that works well with my Kindle Fire. So quick and easy I couldn't believe it at first. I would go and peek at my recipe files. I recommend this app to anyone trolling the internet for new recipe ideas just click the share button on your tablet and select the Chef Tap app.I should also mention the formatting, Chef Tap re-tools and creates a clean, easy to read format for any recipe I've gotten from the Internet. Try it, I think you'll love it.
Easy to use, a great storage mechanism for recipes. Fabulous app.

I love love love this app! Previous to finding ChefTap, I had hundreds of internet bookmarks for recipes I wanted to try. ChefTap gathered them all up and they are in one convenient virtual cookbook of recipes that I know i love. If I make changes, no problem..changed right there. If I decide I don't like one after I try it...delete! It's very user friendly and super convenient. I have the free registered account. May be bumping up to pro! If you like to treasure hunt recipes, this app is a must!
I use this app almost every day. I love cooking and I love recipes. I can clip any recipe on a whim, even if I might not make it. When I do make it, I can scale it to my needs, modify, make it MINE!
My go-to app. Love the scaling feature.

I've had Chef Tap on my kindle fires for over 2 years. The newest version has made an already easy to use app easier, faster and more comprehensive. I've been a chef tap pro subscriber for a year. Well worth the $7.99 annual fee.

I love the ease of getting the recipe directly off a web page.  Also, it's great that you have access online on your computer. I would recommend this app to those that love collecting recipes and cookbooks. When I purchased a new tablet, one of my deciding factors was checking to see if Chef Tap was available for download on the new device. Ha ha but there you have it. Try it you won't be disappointed.

I use this app more than any other. I love the fact that I can pull a recipe off the web and everything is in one place. The "make" button is also handy way to organize a rudimentary weekly menu. If it had a shopping list I'd be thrilled (hint).I use this in my kindle and phone... I wish I could have all recipes on both devices, but that is not currently available. The only issue is remembering which recipe is on which device, and if it's on the kindle, I can't pull up the recipe at the store so I have to write down my ingredients beforehand. Otherwise I highly recommend this app!

I don't have internet at home, but was able to download all my Pinterest recipes onto my Kindle Fire HD from work. I used to have to remember to print a page or two to take home with me, so this is great!! I love that these are all hand-picked-by-me recipes that I wanted and not a book filled with only a few I might actually want to try. It's easy to sort and type in any that you already have at home. Home run of an app, I absolutely love it!

Headings: just what I've been looking for
Base_Reviews: I have been wishing there was a way to build a data base of recipes as a result of searching the internet. This program not only will help build a list of recipes, but it also helps build menus and gives the home cook a way to record successes and flops. Another reason I love this program is that I have only a little room for cookbooks and the good ones tend to run more expensive than I can afford right now. This allows me to build my own "cookbook". I like that.

Headings: Great as a Free App - Even Better w/ Upgrade
Base_Reviews: Great as a Free App - Even Better w/ Upgrade

This is such a great app for cooking. I'm not sure what my Kindle settings are at the moment, but when I use this app, the Kindle doesn't go to sleep. This is great for when my hands are messy, and I don't want to "wake up" my Kindle. I love the way this separates the ingredient listing from the cooking steps. I have recommended this to several friends. Also - you can change ingredients to your liking.
I rely on ChefTap daily. It's easy to use, easy to clip recipes, and easy to edit for my own personal experience. I've been using ChefTap for four years now. Love it!

Headings: great app for every day UAE
Base_Reviews: I give the developers give stars because ( in my own experience) they were very responsive to my issues and fixed them right away (and that was around Christmas when I expected to wait due to the holidays).I do love the app, would give it five stars if I could make my grocery list from the recipes I want to make, and then add additional shopping items. I think the developers are working on something like that....It is just awesome to have my recipes in the kitchen off the counter, I don't have to turn pages, get books messy (I am not a neat cook!) and my four year old doesn't accidentally close to cookbook!It is easy to import and add manually.

Headings: I have this on my phone and Kindle... very useful.
Base_Reviews: I have this on my phone and my Kindle.I have my recipes with me to share with friends and family if needed, but can use one of my Kindles as a cookbook when in the kitchen.You can enter your own recipes, import them from websites, and so much more.

I love cooking and love trying new recipes. I have notebooks full of clipped recipes fully organized. Since going totally digital I have been searching for a great way to organize the many new recipes I try. Through trial and error with countless promising apps I had settled on evernote as my best option, but it had some issues with certain sites that required extra steps to make it available in the application.Well all that is over with Chef Tap. It is so easy to save recipes in a very readable and usable standard that is search able I may never go back. It is not perfect. A synching feature is sorely lacking as I use multiple devices. I would also like to see a desktop plug in for when I'm on my laptop.Still, all things considered it is the best app out there for organizing recipes. Now my only problem is keeping up with cooking all my new found dishes. What a terrible problem to have...

Headings: Finally found a useful recipe app !!!
Base_Reviews: Ever since I got my tablet I've been looking for a useful recipe app that I could download recipes from any site.  Chef Tap does everything I want it to do !!!  Plus, once I have the recipe downloaded I can edit it, add more pictures, and tag it.  I like how I can have the ingredients on one half of the screen and the directions on the other half.  If you need help with any of the functions it's easy enough to google Chef Tap help to get instructions and/or videos.  I was able to load and edit a recipe in under 3 mins.  There are other ways to download the recipe other than 'share' but this was the option I found easiest for me.
Neat way to store recipes

Very easy to use, and lets the user store up to a hundred recipes for free. I might buy up into the premium, that's how much I like it, but I'm cheap. My only wish is that it could store videos of recipes. I've been using ChefTap for a few years now.

Love love this app! It isn't one with a gazillion recipes I'll never use but rather holds all my personal ones in one place. Exactly what I was looking for & free to boot! The import from new ones I see elsewhere & want to try is very easy. HINT: Make one of your tag catagories 'to try ' for a quick way to look up all those accumulated 'oh this sounds good ' ones when you're in the mood for something different!

This is a great app. Just go online with your Kindle, find a recipe you like, tap share, hit Chef Tap from the options and the recipe is sent to your Kindle and saved in the app. I use it all the time. Keep only the recipes you want. Save them from your favorite websites and authors. You can create your own organizational system for the recipes. Bottom line,just get it. Well , a low cal pumpkin pie awaits.
Kept the kids busy for a little while.  Nice app

I love this little app. I am hard pressed to choose my favorite feature...the ability for it to snag a recipe effortlessly from a webpage or blog or the ability to view the instructions either step-by-step or all at once. Best of all, it's free! The only enhancement I would love to see is the ability to select several recipes and then generate a shopping list like the Epicurious app. Thanks to the developer of this nifty little app.

Headings: Exactly what I've been looking for!
Base_Reviews: I have been using pinterest to find new recipes but found it cumbersome having to go to the individual websites for each recipe.  It was on my to-do list to download them all into some sort of cook book on my computer.  I downloaded this app without really knowing what it was.  I wasn't expecting much because it was free.  When I finally got around to looking at it, I was so excited.  It was exactly what I have been looking for.  The only improvement I would like to see is a shopping list function, but according to the website it is in the works.

I have used ChefTap since the first Kindle Fires came out. I have tried a few recipe apps, and this is my favorite, and now the only one I use for recipe storage and for cooking.The app is very versatile. You can add recipes by importing directly from a web page, or a file, or by typing it in yourself. You can keep photos of every recipe, even your own results photo. You can cook from the recipe proper, or from step by step view. You can edit, add comments, import additional links, star favorites, sort into multiple customizable categories, and add to a "make" list.Recent improvements include the ability to search for recipes directly from the app, sync your recipes to the cloud and across devices, and get rid of flash ads for a small upgrade fee. You can easily upload your back-up file to your personal file sharing service. I keep a back-up in Box, which has made the transition to replacement Kindles very easy.I have been cooking for 60 years, have a bookshelf of cookbooks, yet ChefTap has refreshed my passion for cooking by making it easy to source and try new recipes, and adapt and cook them. Bravo!
So easy to look up a recipe and to add new ones from the web and from my own collection. Rarely use an actual cookbook any more..Highly recommended.

Love this app.  It makes meal planning so easy.  We sit down on Sunday morning, scroll through our recipe tiles, pick five, and it creates a shopping list for us.  It's easy to add new recipes, and easy to favorite real winners so you don't forget to make them again.

I think this app has a lot of functionality on a Kindle fire! I am not overly tech savvy but, I can recognize capability. ChefTap does what it states it will do and, it does it pretty well.  I have successfully imported from numerous websites; I have also imported many non-food "recipes."  I really like the versatility and having the ease of several forms of entry/import.

This app is the perfect way to organize the recipes I frequently find online, wish to try and then forget where I found them.  Now when I find a recipe, I simply share the page to Chef Tap and I have only one place to look on my Kindle Fire, instead of digging through e-mails I've sent to myself or pages I've bookmarked.  If only I could put magazine couplings into it!!

I really like using this app because I can find recipes on the internet and put them into the app without any retyping.  The only problem I have run across is that the recipes sometimes just don't appear when it has finished downloading.  I simply try again and it usually works the second time.  I'm sure there are a lot of little things that could make it better but overall it is a very handy app which works pretty well.
I really enjoy using this app for cooking. I am able to easily import recipes that I find online and add them to my collection. The grocery list is great and works really well for me.
Love this.  Easy to use. Have been using this several years. Able to create categories (tags) which makes it very simple to find each recipe.

Headings: Love It Enough to Pay for It
Base_Reviews: The title says it all.  I don't pay for apps.  Seriously, I've paid for the grand total of three apps in my five years of smart phone and table use.  This is worth every single penny.  And if you don't want to pay, try out the free version first.  I'm willing to bet that after you've used it for awhile, you'll go ahead and buy that app.  It's that good.
My wife sends me recepies all the time. I use this to sort them and scan for an answer to "What do you want for dinner this week?"
It's awesome to pull my favorite recipes from online all into 1 place. The shopping list feature is convenient, too.

I think it's amazing how this thing works. It's easy and convenient to add, delete, or edit records. I also love that the link stats attached as well so you can reference the website of there are any issues with the download.My only complaint about the app is that it doesn't have a shopping list option so it can gather the ingredients to certain recipes you want to make. If the option is there, I haven't seen it yet. If it isn't there, it would be a really great feature to add! That way I won't have to use a different list for shopping. If I see the option for it, it'll be 5 stars.

I really like the way you can add recipes to this app from the Internet without leaving the app. It does freeze up at times which is why I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5. I would also like it if I could add recipes from the Internet when not in the actual app and on my P.C. rather than my Fire. This might be available with the paid account. I haven't check that out yet.

I truly love this app. All my pinterest recipes plus additional ones, are stored on here. Since I carry my kindle in my purse I always have my recipes,  so if I stop at the store on my way home from work I just pull up recipe and shop. I can try new recipes and if we don't like them I just delete, no wasted paper, and ones we really like I copy and export to my computer.

I love that I can store recipes I've found online in a way that is easier to follow than is presented on the websites. It is much more practical for use in the kitchen than just using a tablet on the webpage.But its also wonderful for storing recipes that I've gotten through friends and family. Those are not on webpages but still important to me. I dont want to loose them...and once again they are stored in a way I can use them in the kitchenone thing I'd love to see would be a temp converter. That wound be really useful.

I was APPrehensive about this app but it sounded like what I had been looking for and it hasn't disappointed me. I am always looking up new recipes and then having to copy and paste to a new email and so far this app has made it so very simple for me.

I use Chef Tap on my second generation Kindle and Kindle HD also my android phone. Both my husband and I do the cooking in our house. We both love the ease of use and convenience of having our favorite recipes at our fingertips. I highly recommend upgrading to get the unlimited sync so you can sync across multiple devices. The formatting of recipes is great. Being a diabetic, I use the notes section to add nutritional info. And being able to create my own tags is invaluable. We have never had problems on any of our devices. And I use it so much, I don't know what I would do without it!

Headings: This is the Recipe App you want!

I love recipes and subscribe to multiple sites that send weekly recipes via email.  I also pin recipes in pinterest.  Having so many places to store recipes makes it difficult to retrieve them.  I found this app which allows me to consolidate all my recipes in one place.  It is very user-friendly and I don't have any trouble finding recipes now.
Can't recommend this app enough!  All 2895 recipes saved and organized. Shopping list for ingredients on my phone too. Totally awesome

It's so nice to have all my recipes in one place! It syncs with my phone, laptop, and kindle so I've got backups everywhere, and its awesome to be at the grocery store, craving something in particular, and be able to open up the recipe on my phone...voila, ingredients list!

Headings: This is my go to recipe app

This is the most important app on my tablet. I have been using this app, since I purchased my first Kindle  Fire a couple of years ago. I am now using a new Kindle Fire and I upgraded this application. I love cooking, baking, and shopping using this app. I have close to 800 recipes and I add recipes daily.
Love it, use it often, great to have  my recipes accessible on all my devices.

I absolutely love this... so easy to import recipes and then revise to fit my cooking style and ingredients... so easy to put in recipes from scratch, too, and easily add pictures!  The app looks great, and I love that I can also input recipes from my PC with a full-sized keyboard too.  Simple and extremely useful -- my most-used app!

I can't tell you how much I love this app.  It's so much faster and easier to find my saved recipes with Cheftap on my Kindle fire than to go to Pinterest, find the right board, then find the recipe, and after that it still takes a few clicks before I have the recipe I am looking for.  Cheftap is fast and there is no Internet connection needed to use recipes that you have already saved.  I use this daily!

I'd been searching for an app to put all my recipes on and get away from paper recipes all over my house.  Once I understood how this works, I love it.  Especially since I get most receipes from other web sites.  You just click on the recipe, share it to a page and pick Chef Tap and it's there.  And their support system is great too.

Headings: You need this app if you like to cook
Base_Reviews: I love this app and the fast interaction to view and save recipes. The reviews and suggestions from other users is awesome and raises the usefulness to a high level above other apps. It is useful to surf for dinner ideas when you need a nudge to be creative.

This is a useful app that allows me to visit different cooking websites searching for recipes I want to try and then I can click on the recipe and Chef Tap copies it to a folder where I can browse without going back to the original website where it was listed.I can create tags (categories) for the recipes and even add my own notes.

I use Chef Tap for all my recipes. What I like most is that I can edit a recipe and change it the way I want. Wany times I edit a recipe and translate it into a different language, so my relatives can try them out too.

Headings: I love it. I love how it syncs across devices ...
Base_Reviews: I have been using this app for over a year now.  I love it.  I love how it syncs across devices and that I can access it from the web.

I love being able to do easily collect recipes from web sites. Everything works fine for me. I see some people have had problems with the app after a while, but things are fine so far. It is nice to have such easy access to recipes on my Kindle in the kitchen.

I use this app almost everyday!! My husband downloaded it for me so I would have a place to keep all the recipes I want off the internet. It works great and you can save any type of instructions, not just recipes!! I have not only saved recipes but jewelry making instructions, also. You can also put your own recipes in it. This app has many more options that make it very useful!!
I upgraded but even loved the free part. So easy to use and don't understand the reviewer who complained about "permissions".

Got this yesterday and have already loaded my favorite recipes from my computer. Just convert them to text files and import them. I also used Backup/restore to move all the recipes from my  android tablet to my Fire. And, of course, you can get recipes from the Web. Greatest app ever!

Headings: Love having recipes available all the time
Base_Reviews: It's great to have access to my recipes on Kindle Fire even when it's not on line.  Updated app is excellent.  It captures recipes more than 90% of the time, even some that appear in strange disorganized formats on the web.  It's pretty easy to edit and organize recipes and bring them together in one very convenient list.

Headings: Didn't know I needed it. Use it all the time.
Base_Reviews: This app is perfect for a cook like me whose always on the lookout for new recipes. You really do just tap and save the recipe. I downloaded it to my Kindle Fire and it works perfectly with most sites. I also reset my auto shut off time to 30 minutes so that I have plenty of time to do my prep work and start cooking with no annoying turn offs.TRY IT!

I come across recipes online all the time and would think, "hey that looks good". Then email it to myself and completely forget about it. With tapchef I just copy the url and load it in and it saves it in a nice format and includes the original link. I've been using it a lot for new meal ideas.

I LOVE chef tap! I don't cook without it...it is my favorite kitchen gadget! All my recipes on one easily portable place...easy to access, make changes, create your own recipes, etc. Oh, and my family lives how easily I can share my recipes. Thanks for this amazing app!!

Headings: My go to recipe management app
Base_Reviews: I have been using this app for at least three years and it is one of my "go to" apps. I have upgraded Kindle Fire tablets three times and with the ChefTap cloud, the migration has been seamless. I clip recipes at least 3 times a week, use it while cooking at least 5 times a week, updated recipes with my notes, and have added a few "family" recipes from scratch.  There may be other acceptable recipe management apps, but I'm so happy with this one, no need to try anything else.

Chef Tap is amazing!  If you browse recipes on the internet, you must have Chef Tap.  I enjoy the app Zite and often want to keep recipes from there and it is as simple as pressing "share" option and choosing Chef Tap.  The recipe is entered into ChefTap complete with photo. I have chosen to have the upgraded version that has an annual fee. It is better than a cooking magazine subscription, because every recipe is one that I have chosen. Money well spent!  Every time I bring another recipe into Chef Tap, I say, "I love this app!"

I don't usually write reviews but I need to share my honest opinion of Chef Tap which I have been using for 2 years.  It is wonderful!!!  So easy to use and simple!  I am now importing from my Pinterest boards!  Wow.  Love simply selecting "share" with Chef Tap of bookmarking the recipe page and the app will scan and import all the recipes I have saved in recipe boxes.  I use several cooking sites including Food Network, Epicurious, Saveur, Wms Sonoma,Big Oven, Martha Stewart, All Recipes, Pinterest, Bon Apetit, etc....  I import my saved recipes from all these sites and Chef Tap keeps them organized and easy to find in one place, a single app.I can't recommend this enough to anyone who truly enjoys cooking and learning new techniques or simply enjoys collecting recipes.  I have even saved cocktail recipes!  This imports photos as well!!!  And you can edit your recipes and add your own notes.  Excellent!I haven't upgraded to the Pro version yet as I am awaiting the invitation or word that a seamless transfer of my recipes will take place with a Pro account.  I hope this is the case because now that I can import my Pinterest board recipes, I will need more capacity!Great application!
IMO, this is the absolute best app for people who like to keep easy access to their recipes. It keeps the pictures, it keeps the ENTIRE recipes without having to have internet access.  I just love I.

While I like this app, and love that I am suppose to be able to import but it freezes or is slow quite often, with that being said, once it does import and I can use, it is a great program.04/06/13 Update:  Had to up my review of this program. since the initial update the program has been great.  I use it all the time when looking for a new recipe to try.

I have amassed quite a collection of recipes on my kindle fire.  The problem was I had them on several different apps, and a ton of bookmarks and saved blogs.  ChefTap enabled me to have all my recipes in one place.  they have thought of everything I might need, and for what they haven't thought of yet, they regularly update.  Awesome job!

I first got this app on my kindle in 2012. This is quite a simple app, and yet it does so much. When I found recipes I would put them onto cheftap and it would store them not only ordered but in a easier format to read then the site. Then, when my kindle broke and had to be replaced, I had to erase all my data from all my apps. It was a relief, however, when I found that amongst all my erased apps, cheftap had stored my data to the cloud, and I still had my recipies!!! ALL IN ALL, CHEFTAP IS THE BEST APP I HAVE EVER ENCOUNTERED.
The app is great and easy to use. Great place to store recipes you see on the Internet.

I love this app, I use it EVERY DAY.  So nice to grab a recipe that sounds good then when the cooking or baking bug strikes-I get to work!  I did upgrade so I could keep up with over 800 recipes.Thanks so much!  I love the new app logo, too !!!!!

Love this app.  It puts all those scattered webpage recipes in one place with lovely format.  For the blog like recipes that it has some difficulty deciphering the recipe from the blog it allows you to edit and retrieve missing text.  You can tag your saved recipes to categorize.  All in all I love it!
One of my most favorite and used apps! So quick and simple! I highly recommend!
Have had this app (pro level) God yrs & have ALWAYS been pleased;  especially with the "support"!

Headings: best app. ever for recipe collectors and cooks
Base_Reviews: Can't say enough wonderful things about Chef App. Unbelievably useful and well done for recipe collectors and cooks. Because I can edit the recipes, I have been adding my weight watcher points plus to each recipe as well, adding another level of convenience. Love that I can share my recipes w friends and family. Wish this was available on-line.

I love the design and functionality of this app. I can't tell you how many 'recipe software' programs I have run through and lost for different reasons (Mastercook- bigoven) boo to both of you. I can't wait until Chef tap offers up the ability to sync up all devices!! Hope this will be a keeper for the long term. I've lost oh so many recipe collections.....

If you're looking for your own personal cookbook for your tablet, this app is IT!  I looked at several different apps and decided on this one because it is so easy to import recipes from nearly any source.  It also offers categorizing, which makes it a snap to find your recipes when you need them.  I'd give this 10 stars if I could.  LOVE LOVE LOVE it! (AND it's FREE!)

This app has helped me like to cook again, it very easy to use & to sync between my phone . computer & kindle.  It allows you to find recipes in many other places & to store thenm all in one place, plus it allows you to make a grocery list for those recipes & it FREE!

Headings: I searched and searched and this is perfect!
Base_Reviews: 5 stars all the way!  Easy to use and the syncing between my PC, Kindle Fire (which I keep in my kitchen) and my Android phone is great!  The clipping feature is amazing since a lot of my recipes are from the internet now I can go find them and clip then and throw away the STACK of paper I have printed.  And now I can instantly send my recipes to my friends at work.  We are mindless eating machines, LOL.  It is my new best toy. Finally all my recipes are getting organized  *SMILE*  Support is fantastic also and I hear a new addition will be a shopping list.  I am a graphic designer so I have a blast using my OCR software to add my typed recipes and finding pictures on the internet to add to my personal recipes is easy and fun.  And in the future I will start adding my own photographs.

I have downloaded a lot of great recipes from different websites and had no problems at all. Have already tried several recipes and think the fact that Chef Tap will hold the recipe on the screen until I have finished with it is a terrific plus. Since I am not a computer wiz by any means I was also very pleased at how easy it is to use.

This is a great cooking app.  Instead of trying to remember which website I saw that great recipe on, I can import it, or add my own and keep them organized the way that I want so I don't have to spend a lot of time looking for my favorites or ones that I want to try.

I have used this app for seven years and it is ,hands down the best recipe app out there. I have tried several others and none of them have the features and ease of use as this one. Boot only can I load recipies from anywhere almost, I can even input the old family recipes out of my recipe box. You can even look up inspiration right from the app. I have the pro version . I would be heartbroken if this app was no longer available.

I use ChefTap every day, both for importing from websites and typing in my own recipes. I've even loaded jpegs I took with my iPhone from a magazine in my doctor's office because I don't like "borrowing" her reading material. I just type in the name of the recipe and then load the photo of the recipe as the picture. Headings: Best app for clipping recipes from blogs
Base_Reviews: Part of the reason I bought my Kindle Fire was to organize my digital recipes and have them available without needing to print. I experimented with a number of apps, some of which do things Chef Tap doesn't -- Chef Tap doesn't have a searchable database of recipes, or do menu planning, or create a shopping list for you.  IOW Chef Tap doesn't offer features I really wasn't interested in.When it comes to clipping recipes from blogs and websites, Chef Tap is magic. Somehow it finds the recipe hidden in wordy blog posts about the blogger's day and clips out exactly (and only!) what you need to know to make the dish. No other app, including Evernote, does that as well. I resisted paying for an account, but in the end, I decided it was worth it. SUMMARY: I have used from Thanksgiving planning through to New Year's. Wonderful! I have never found an app of any kind worth the price of a "full version" or subscription, but I will be subscribing to the full version of Chef Tap.PROS: First and foremost, extremely accurate on big name sites, and surprisingly accurate on smaller sites (see "Testing Accuracy" below). Between the clipping and recipe sizing features alone, this app is amazingly handy.There is also an easy editing feature that allows you to make it your own, as well as a notes section if you want to leave the original unsullied. I like the ability to tag and synch, but haven't played with them much.TESTING ACCURACY: I clipped 75+ recipes from  about a dozen different "big name" sites (Betty Crocker, BHG, Tablespoon, All Recipes, etc) and a half dozen or so from smaller blogging sites (Home-ec101, Acadian Table, etc). I double-checked both the ingredient and instructions on every single clip.Bottom line, the accuracy of the app is tied to how "well-formed" the source website is.Here's what I found...1. One error on a big name site - a recipe missing its last step.2. Several errors on small blogging sites - missing or duplicate ingredients or steps.2. One annoyance - several recipes that had numbered steps were missing the numbers (not the content, just the number itself). This is a step above cosmetic, because it happened almost every time, even on well-formed sites.3. A few rare, random "cosmetic" issues - duplicate titles, bad line breaks, or random bolding.However, all errors can be corrected with the editing mode. In addition, because the link is included in the clip, you can go back later in case you think something is missing.CONS:Together, the following cons mean I am frustrated every time I try to use the app. If it were not so accurate and useful, this would be enough to make me delete it and move on to something else:1. Takes too long to load - my devices are fast overall, with this app being noticeably longer loading on all of them.2. Loads back to it's "home" location instead of back to the recipe I was last looking at. By the time it opens and I remember what recipe I was going to look at, I have forgotten why.3. Synching across devices is confusing, but I suspect that is due to the limitations on the free version.

Headings: Does what ESPN does, without being ESPN.
Base_Reviews: I really like the user friendliness of the app, the layout looks nice, and it keeps me up to date on my teams. I really like the option to be able to quickly add my teams as a favorite and locate news and scores for those teams.There are some ads in the application, but they are placed at the bottom of articles, not in the way.Those tired of ESPN, this is a great alternative.

Headings: I was able to watch the Super Bowl with this app
Base_Reviews: I downloaded this app on my Fire Stick because I saw that CBS was live streaming the Super Bowl this year.  I cannot pick up CBS with my antenna, so this was the perfect alternative.  I was able to watch the Super Bowl hassle free.  This was my only reason for downloading the app as I have no other use for it because I do not watch sports year round.

Downloaded it specifically to watch what turned out to be the lowest scoring Superbowl ever but the picture quality was great. No skips or lags. I cut the cord so no dedicated cable providers for me so my over the air signal is sometimes spotty. The app let me watch through my Fire TV with perfect clarity.

The streaming was excellent and great informational programs. I was looking for a live NFL game. Our cable company removed the channel that was needed to see the game. I didn't find the live game so will probably rarely use it.

Headings: Worked well for the Super Bowl
Base_Reviews: I used this to stream the game live from my projector for a party I had with my friends.  We enjoyed watching the funny commercials during the game.  After that, I've had absolutely no use for this app, but that's just me; I'm not a sports fan.

Headings: Excellent app incuded in CBS All Access
Base_Reviews: As easy to use as any other app. I forgot about Masters coverage last year. Watched every day this year. Included with CBS All Access which I've subscribed to since it became available. It's only gotten better since then.

The stream buffered frequently, also it was approximately 30 seconds behind the live broadcast from my antenna, other than that the quality was was pretty good. I found it made a good backup to catch up on anything I missed from the live (antenna) version. I'm sure it may come in better if I had faster internet.

I had no idea how I was going to watch the Superbowl this year since I cancelled all my subscription TV. CBS Sports Stream came into view for me just in time. Awesome picture with the occasional buffer spot but no complaints here. Looking forward to getting to watch sports again.

CBS All Access includes CBS Sports HQ, but this free CBS Sports Stream & Watch Live app goes considerably further. Special broadcasts like the Super Bowl have their own stream without the local affiliate commercials. And, a scroll down directory has a slate of "just aired" HQ topics, as well as special slates of NFL, NBA, etc. Nice app. Great price.

I was texting friends during the game, so I was aware that I was just a few seconds behind the live TV broadcast, which is actually amazing for a live feed with so many viewers, I had expected it would be worse. And for me, a few seconds was totally fine since we only texted gossip about the halftime show and not the actual plays... Amazing opportunity for me (who refuses to get cable TV or any traditional TV for that matter) to be able to watch Super Bowl from home instead of heading out to a crazy bar. I also loved that the advertisements were the same ones as on TV. Previous years' Super Bowl apps were slower and didn't have the real ads. Well done!

Base_Reviews: Sep 30, 2017 **UPDATE**I committed to cutting the cord over a year ago, and obviously the biggest drawback is Live Sports. My original frustration with this app pushed me to delete it, but today gave it a second chance (for a specific CFB game). Whatever update they did between then and now seems to have addressed any issues so I bumped it from * to ****. They fixed the constant need for authorization upon closing the app, the stream quality no longer clips audio (though certain graphics do cause short buffering), and they apparently have deals worked out with PAC12 Network allowing streams of 'some' of their games.Most of all, I was amazed at how well the PIP, Split screen and Mosaic features worked for watching multiple games. Easy, intuitive and seamless streams that are perfect for a Sat Afternoon of College Football. Aside from WatchESPN this turns out to be the best streaming sports app. The only reason it isn't a perfect 5* is the somewhat limited amount of live streams to choose from. The ESPN app offers all games on ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNNews, ABC and ESPN3 gives you games that aren't even broadcast. You can even tune in to the raw feeds of "Sky Cams" for certain games if you want a different perspective.Thanks to Fox Sports Go for updating this app, and it has been added to my favorites list. If you enjoy sports its a must have.*ORIGINAL*Decent quality app with a clean UI. HD Stream quality is okay, with occasional audio clipping. HOWEVER it requires activation/authorization FAR too often.If you plan on leaving this on the whole time... You're fine. But if you exit out of the app to watch something else and come back to it, expect to pull out your laptop/tablet to reactivate every. Single. TIME.It has required "Activation" FOUR TIMES in the last 24 hours. Four star app if this is ever fixed, but as it stands it is nearly unusable and not worth the continuous hassle. Headings: One of the best options for streaming TV
Base_Reviews: Let me start by saying that like many others I became a cordcutter due to frustration with ever-escalating cable bills. Plus I was already spending money on Netflix, Hulu and Amazon Prime so literally thousands of shows and movies available but still wanted a decent option for viewing live broadcasts and cable channels when away from home, which the cable company didn't provide. Therefore, when I initially cut the cord and returned my cable box and TiVo cablecard, I spent several months with DirecTV NOW, and also trialed the live tv options from Hulu, Sling, YouTube and a few others as well and either had issues with the interface, the channel selection or the price.fuboTV provides a robust assortment of channels and was the only option that provided access to local NBA coverage within the base package (which is priced at $45 and depending on which promo you get may be discounted for the first month or two). With the competitors, local NBA coverage was either unavailable or a paid upgrade.The image quality is superb, sharper than any image I've seen before as they broadcast in 4K. However, perhaps due to the speed of my internet connection (20mB/sec), oftentimes the image will be pixelated for a second when a program is initially loaded. I love the fact that I can watch on my Firestick, my phone, my laptop from anywhere and DVR the programs I'm viewing.In addition to viewing live tv, fuboTV provides an EXTENSIVE library of current and past TV shows (both from the major networks and cable channels) and movies that you can watch on demand, very similar to Hulu. Most of the TV shows are popular shows but some have are very good shows that I had never heard of before. Prior to last week, you couldn't type a title to search for a program or movies on the Amazon app, only browse alphabetically. Now that you can search on any device I'm a happy camper and I love being able to watch programs on any device. Also, if you need to login to an app such as CNN or SYFY, fuboTV is on the listing of supported cable providers.I have two minor quibbles:1. The standard DVR recording capacity is just 20 hours and it's $10 to upgrade, which gets you 500 hours of capacity. If they had an option in the middle for $5 I would go for it but as my objective is to save money versus having cable TV, I'm good for now.2. When you first open the app it will feature sporting events playing currently or later in the day and you have to make a few extra clicks to get to the program guide. Typically they will feature soccer games and as I'm not a big soccer fan I could do without this and would prefer an option to load the guide by default.

Headings: Best value of all the Streaming services we tried.
Base_Reviews: Had the absolute least missing channels my family watches vs all of the other services we reviewed, being 2. ABC and The CW were missing. About a week later they added The CW to there line-up. Very good service and quality, 3 available streams concurrent and 500 hours of DVR for $55 a month as of this writing. Hulu was missing 5 channels, ATT watchtv was missing more and on down the list they went. Almost none of them other then ATT and Hulu carry ABC since ABC is a Disney Property, and they want you to use their services. Not happening. The only downside we have had with Fubo.TV was using USA as the commercials (and the service tells you bottom left) how many commercials during the break, it would sometimes play 1 of 5 then 2 of 5 then 3 of 5 then go back to 2 of 5 then 3 of 5 then back to 1 of 5. Playing the same commercials over and over and over. I reported this issue to Fubo. So far no change. Using the USA app ( a cable or TV account like Dish or Direct etc, is necessary to use any APPS solo outside of Fubo), doesn't have that issue, nor amount of commercials as high as 15. Other channels within Fubo don't seem to suffer this bug.  I use it mostly for Netflix or Prime, so obviously no commercials. The cons if you wanna call them that, doesn't change my mind of how great this service is and how easy it is to use it.

I absolutely love Fubo. They have something for everyone. Nickelodeon  and Disney for children, Hallmark, Lifetime, TLC, A&E, AMC, Discovery, MTV,VH1, WE, Food Network and more for people who like lifestyle channels and Sports. I have Roku and Firestick. With Roku you can fast forward and see the tiles but with Firestick you cannot. That would be nice if they offered the same feature for Firestick. It never buffers...of course because I have great internet speed. Fubo offers more channels than Hulu Live and YTTV. I hope Fubo stays at this price with the channels weâ€™re getting. If not Iâ€™m going back to cable.

It is a good service.  I didn't have any problems with service, but it is on the high end of price without having a good amount of channels that I usually watch.  If you are a fan of sports, especially Latin American and European based teams, this is for you.  There are a good amount of channels that you would typically pay extra for to get in the base package here (maybe the cause of the higher price).  I did have a slight problem with navigation, but I only had the 7 day trial and did not get a good feel for how it worked.  I think with time I would get used to it.  Overall a good product but I would go with Hulu TV, YouTube TV, or Sling if I had the choice.  They offer things I like to watch at a slightly lower cost.

I can't believe how good the video quality is! If I had known this, I would have dropped PSVue a long time ago, especially because we love watching Bruins' hockey games. We can see the puck now! We only get 10 to 12 Mb/sec internet speed with our Wifi connection using the Firestick and the streaming quality far surpasses PSVue. No buffering now. I cannot understand all of these negative reviews. What on earth are they talking about? I was very skeptical to try FUBO due to all of the complaints. I'm sure that most of those complaints are coming from people who either have poor internet service or are terribly upset that they have to learn a new way to navigate their tv service. (paradigm shift anyone?) To be fair, there are some minor differences that may be annoying to some, like the fact that you have to schedule each and every episode of the shows you want to DVR. But DirecTV's satellite service had the same limitation. We became spoiled with PSVue's DVR functionality. Hopefully, FUBO resolves this in the future. We are paying the extra 5 bucks/month for one extra device and the extra DVR space. I am so glad that Sony dropped NESN!!! Thank you Sony for steering us to FUBOtv! Don't believe the BS about not being able to cancel your FUBO free trial. Just set up your account on the web and you can access your subscription from there. Simple. No one is trying to steal your money. I also had one quirky thing happen the very first time I logged into my free trial. I had two audio tracks playing simultaneously with about a one second delay between. I simply exited the FUBO app with the Firestick's home button, arrowed up to Amazon's top menu, over to "settings", down to "FireTV" and selected "Restart". While I was waiting for that to reboot, I decided to click on the help button of FUBO's website. I started a chat session with their customer service. They recommended deleting the app from the Firestick menu and then restart the Firestick but since I had already begun the reboot, I let it finish. I had no problems at all since then. So it was a minor glitch, easily remedied, and customer service was available within seconds! Outstanding, great job FUBO!!!

Headings: If you like sports. This is the App for you
Base_Reviews: Got this for my Father-in-law. He stayed up until 4:30 am watching it and playing with it. after one night of using it. they cancelled their Dish Network account and are completely happy to pay the 50.00 a month. Besides the all of the sports channels someone could ever want (he is a soccer fan and loves the BeIn sports channels and there are 10 of them). there is regular programming like A&E, CBS, NBC, Hallmark ect.... WIll save them 80.00 a month compared to their satellite service.

WHAT OTHERS HAVE MARKED THIS OFF FORContinuing to charge them after cancellation: I am continuing my subscription, so I cannot comment on this.Freezing: I watched the third place World Cup game and had no issues. I watched Leicester v. Man U and it only froze once when I took it to mobile and left the house. A few other PL games on NBC Sports have frozen for a minute or two. But overall, I do not get what others talk about when they say that it is so terrible. Even cable has its moments, sometimes much worse.Bad picture: Looks fine to me. Maybe the first ten seconds aren't great, but again, isn't that true with almost anything?Slow loading: Okay, here I have a hack. When I start fubo.tv from my Amazon Fire TV homepage, a loading circle comes up, often with the fubo background, but not always. It will rarely come out of this by itself. But I have noticed that if I press the back button, it immediately snaps out of it and doesn't take me back but instead takes me directly to fubo. Odd thing, but in the end, it's fine for me.You cannot rewind a live game, the way that you can on NBC Sports apps or Fox Soccer Match Pass, et al: Accurate. Goals may happen and you won't be able to see them if you are not there at the exact time or you didn't record it.MY MARKDOWNSPremier League: You think that you are getting NBC Sports, Bravo, USA (?)--every possible network you could in order to watch the Premier League (aside from the money-grubbing NBC Sports Gold). But you forget the obvious: NBC. It comes with your local Fox and CBS, but not ABC or NBC. I have found articles on fubo that say that with the TVEverywhere app, you can log-in to the NBCSports app with your fubo credentials and it will treat it like a cable subscription. This has not been the case for me. I am not clear why I was rejected, other than a message that said something like "We're sorry, this provider does not have retransmission rights in your region". From a fubo page, it appears that NBC in my market (Oklahoma City) is not carried (while others like Tulsa and tons of other markets are). I have confirmed this both on the NBC Sports site and on the app, where I have received the same message. So if I were 90 miles to the NW, then I would have this? This is not progress. The fubo article also says that I must have the TVEverywhere channel in my fubo subscription in order for this to work, yet when I search fubo packages for this channel, I find no such listing.Champions League: Heads up--I thought that I would be getting TBS & TNT, and the last I heard, the Champions League was moving to this family of stations in the coming year. But those are not actually included. I just overlooked it.How to make this better: NBC sucks. When it split its games across NBC, Bravo, USA, NBC Sports, it could act like it is helping the fan, but then when it puts some things on a platform like fubo and others, like NBC, not, then that's a big pain. It is either mistakenly not considering this or it is intentionally doing this for its own benefit to make things like this more cumbersome for the consumer, hoping that they buy something like fubo/sling and cable on top of it. I look forward to when NBC and others catch on to how they could make even more money by making life easier for the consumer rather than harder. After all, I hardly watch American football at all anymore. Everyone can turn you off.But what does that mean for fubo? I would like to see fubo make it easier to see NBC, or to at least have my questions answered. It knows that I want to see the Premier League. So list every game. When I click on it, tell me that it is on NBC Sports or Bravo, which I have, and take me there. If that particular game is on NBC Sports Gold, tell me that, and maybe NBC will pay for that ad. If it is actually on NBC itself, then give me a brief and clear instruction on how to watch NBC, and if I cannot, then please tell me why.I also don't find the guide that helpful. I prefer not to look at what is on TV currently because by the time you scroll through all your channels, if you want to go back up to the top and watch something that you saw up there, it takes so long just to get up there. I wind up perusing just the networks, where it lists them in rows of four, which allows me to scroll through to the channel that I want faster, if not the exact programming.WHAT IT GETS RIGHTI watch mostly BBC World News, HGTV, and sports-related channels. The Fubo network is pretty good--kind of like ESPN classic for soccer, but without actual game film. It also has Bein Sports, which has worked well the few times that I have watched it so far. The website is also pretty good.OVERALLIt does great with giving access to French and Spanish games via Bein Sports, which is nice. However, it offers access to only roughly 1/2 of Premier League games, due to some being on NBC itself and some being on NBC Sports Gold. And it does not offer Champions League games in English at all, although worldsoccertalk.com appears to say that I could watch Champions League and Europa League games in Spanish on Univision, which is on fubo. I don't have a problem with that if it will really happen. But what I want to see is an option where you can click on the sport and then the competition; it does have this, but if I am to judge by that, then that points out a few things: (1) No Serie A; (2) No Champions League or Europa League; (3) just 5/10 Premier League games on this particular weekend.As a stand-alone service judged compared to cable, I am pleased with this. It doesn't give you everything, but it does give you some international soccer extras and things like CBS Sports. Comparing to something like Sling, it appears that Sling wins on your regular cable networks, though they are comparable. But if you are really a big soccer fan, understand that you are basically comparing Bein Sports + $10 to TNT/TBS & ESPN, aka La Liga and Ligue 1 to the Champions League and whatever soccer ESPN offers. If you care a great deal about Mexican and South American games, then that will push up fubo in your eyes.

Headings: Missing ESPN, but excellent enough you may not care
Base_Reviews: Superb picture quality and audio quality. I have Verizon FiOS gigabit internet. The Roku version of the app is the superior version, with the ability to watch television in background as you surf the guide at the lower portion of the screen. There's also a regular vertical guide. Sling and Philo have picture-in-picture capabilitiy on mobile. Fubo TV does not. PS Vue does not, but is ending January 30th, 2020 anyway. Despite the lack of that little mobile convenience, Fubo TV mobile is superb in picture and audio quality. Fast & fluid. Same experience as on Roku and Amazon Fire stick. Can not speak to the experience on PC. Had no interest in that. Incidentally, the experience on mobile, I was making reference to the Android version. On Roku & Firestick 4k I don't like that sometimes I have to back out to another menu to get information on a particular program. But then it is only a few clicks away. Nitpicking. With the glaring omission of ESPN, almost every Sports channel that you could possibly imagine is there. So I will be supplementing this service with a base package subscription to Sling, which carries ESPN. YouTube TV does as well, but I don't desire a full package with YouTube TV. The base package on Sling is cheaper, and I only need the ESPN channels.  Awesome service that is equal in quality and in some ways surpasses that of YouTube TV and the others that are more popular like HULU Live TV. Those are also excellent cord-cutting alternatives, though. So choose the one that's right for you. I've made my choice. Hope this helps.Oh, and Fubo TV I understand is the only live streaming service that has 4k resolution built into the app. I have a TCL & Sony Bravia 4k TV's, and I can attest to the superb picture quality on both using the app. Thanks for reading!

I'm stunned by all the negative reviews for this service. I've run the gauntlet of streaming TV services. PS Vue, directTV now (AT&T TV NOW) sling tv and hulu + live. By far Fubo is the best I've had for many reasons. The best thing I'll say for fubo is this is the one I've had the least buffering with and I mean by a long shot. All of the other services were at times completely unwatchable. I've only had fubo buffer on me a few times for like a few seconds and never more then once in a night of viewing. Plus it's got the best channel lineup of any. The picture quality is noticeably better then the others I've had as well. It is a little pricey but still much cheaper then traditional cable.

You have nothing to lose and it may just meet your needs.

Headings: Works great and you can take it anywhere there is decent WIFI
Base_Reviews: I bought FUBO along with Sling and disconnected from Dish.  I use Amazon Fire TV recast and antennae for local channels. I use the Amazon Fire TV Stick on my home TV.  I  got FUBO because it has Fox News, which Sling does not, and Animal Planet.  I have traveled a fair amount and it works great on the road.  I bring my Chromecast dongle with me and cast FUBO to the TV I am using from my Iphone.  The picture is great.  I do love college football and FUBO has most channels other than ESPN.  Like all streaming services, if you like the channel lineup, you won't regret purchasing it.

Headings: I don't regret my choice, after the fact.
Base_Reviews: I find the service good.  This change has reduced my bill substantially.  My bill will be $100.00 less per month all-in (that reduction takes into account that I have added services that I did not previously have - add-ons to FUBO).  I did not have the top of the line cable service from my provider.  Instead I had the third best out of four options from my provider.Is it more complicated than cable TV? Change means adjustment to a different format.  The learning curve is not overwhelming.  For those not well versed with changes in TV services I would recommend getting a younger family members assistance to make the change.  I chose to load FUBO via the Amazon Fire platform.  After the fact I found out that I cannot watch HBO on Amazon's platform.  I can stream it on my iPhone and iPad, as it can be streamed on other devices.  That is inconvenient, but not a deal breaker.  Solution, use the Apple TV platform, the Youtube's platform or I believe ROKU's platform.Note: the number of channels I had access to on cable totaled 220.  On FUBO it is substantially less.  For me this was not a problem, as I complemented what FUBO offers me with HPO and Disney (still I have the stated cost reduction).  I also have Netflix and am an Amazon Prime member, which I had before I left the cable service.  I have more than I have any possibility of ever watching.Best part of this change?  I no longer have a contract.  I can switch any or all of the services I have from one month to the next.

Headings: Some Problems But No Show Stoppers
Base_Reviews: I must say from the start that the only reason I purchased this app for to watch the Giro d'Italia (Italy's version of the Tour de France). I use NBC Sports Gold to watch cycling but the Giro was not a covered race. A quick Google search led me to fubotv. I primarily watch TV through FireTV so I downloaded the fubotv app and then subscribed through my computer. I have been using fubotv for less than a week. Based upon that experience I offer the following observations.I am able to watch the Giro as I desired. There are quite a few other channels available but I have not watch any, for reasons to be discussed below. The picture quality is fine and as with all internet apps it is dependent on you internet speed/quality.My biggest disappointment is the limited capacity of the "DVR" feature. While it is true you can "record" shows for later viewing you are limited to three "recording" total. Also, you must watch those recording within 72 hours of there recording, after which they will be deleted. This limitation has prevented me from recording any thing other than the Giro (which is a 21 day race) which explains why I have on experience with other channels. This wouldn't be too bad except the DVR does not provide the ability to record a "season". Rather, I have to go the desktop each day and set the DVR to record the next program (in my case, the next race three days in the future). A "Season" or "Record All" option sure would be nice.Another limitation, at least from the FireTV standpoint, is that you can't set the DVR to record a show from your TV. You can access the DVR to play a recording but to set new recordings you must use a computer. Also, the schedule on the FireTV fubotv app is limited to about 12 hours in the future.Finally, I have noticed that when the app is paused and then resumed there is a lot of buffering time before the show starts again. I don't believe this is a ISP problem as the buffering is much longer than with PBS, NBC Sports Gold, HBO Now or YouTube.Bottom line, I am pleased to be able to watch the Giro "legally". The fubotv allows me to do this. The grips above are really are more observations than show stoppers. With that said, to get cycling with the DVR feature I am paying more than $40 per month. I will cancel my subscription after the Giro is done, not because of the app but because I really don't have any interest in the other channels. If fubotv offers some programming that your looking for I would go for it.

Fubo has lots of channels and gave me the option of adding on the NFL network.  The streaming works fine on my TCL Roku TVs and the only drawback I see so far is much of the content is in 720p and not true HD. Also 4k content is very limited. Sometimes they broadcast Fox NFL games in 4k. My TCL struggles with that channel but my Amazon fire tv works fine with Fox NFL 4k. With the Fubo app, I can install it on my iphone and all my apple devices so I can watch tv anywhere.  You can even stream it on a Windows laptop through the website.I did the free week trial before I finally selected Fubo as I didn't know anyone using the service so I was skeptical. We're saving about $100 a month by cancelling Comcast's phone and cable.  For the savings, I can put up with the lower resolution.

It has NFL Network and NFL Redzone and apparently a recently added full complement of ESPN channels. I have only been able to find NFL Network and Redzone on FuboTV so it's an easy decision.  It also has NBA TV.I have gigabit internet so streaming and picture quality are great. It also has all of my local broadcast CBS, NBC, Fox and CW channels except local ABC which is not good.  You can also set favorite channels on the guide. At the end of my trial, I'm cancelling my AT&T.The only downside is FuboTV dropped TNT, TBS and CNN so I'll use their respective apps on the fire stick. These are small sacrifices to have have have NFL Network and Redzone. You can get everything else on Fire TV.Disappointed live ABC channels are not available.

Our free trial is now over and we plan to keep Fubo basic.  We get all our favorite channels and some that our cable provider charged a premium for. In addition we have had no outages with Fubo in a week, but 24 hours of dead time on cable in the same period. The 1080 picture is better too.There are some nice pluses like 30 free hours of cloud recordings, and two day access to programs you forget to watch. We will save over a hundred dollars a month- I ditched cable this morning and only wish I'd done it a year ago.There are choices in streaming providers but FuboTV was by far the best for our tastes. Well deserving of five stars.I wrote the above yesterday and then read an astonishing number of bad reviews by others blaming Fubo and/or Firestick for buffering problems and poor picture quality. I think these authors are uninformed. If you want to receive a high definition picture streaming live then the critical issue is the speed and strength of your internet connection from your internet provider, not Fubo and not Firestick. Mine is 100 Mbp/s and there are very few obstacles in the way of the receivers. No buffering and a perfect picture is the result. So to those reviewers- I suggest you look there first and get more wifi speed or a good repeater before laying blame in the wrong place. Most technical reviews (like CNET and others) rate Firestick and Fubo as best in class.

got the latest update and this is great!....everything works great....and 500 hours DVR!....they seem to have fixed all the bugs from the earlier app version....and I did spend time with Fubotv support about some of the problems....and they seem to have listen very well.... to me it's well worth the money......and not having espn in no problem for me....they have all the channels I want...and the DVR!.......much better now with this update.....have tried all the others but to me no one beats Fubo....just saying.....

Headings: First complete streaming service for my area.
Base_Reviews: Streaming services take some time to get used to. We are used to instant on. I use Amazon fire sticks for my TVs, which are not smart TVs. Fubo has given us these necessary programing to make the switch from our very expensive cable. This is the first streaming service in our area to give live local programing. It also has a nice lineup of channels and you can add on or subtract. So all in all it is quite a value and has a nice favorites app so we don't have to go through the entire guide to find our most watched shows. It also offers 250 hours of cloud DVR in the basic package.I do find it a little tedious to work with, but that is likely because I don't have the smart TV.

Headings: Left satellite company for Amazon Programs and Fubo TV
Base_Reviews: I had been a satellite-provider customer for over 15 years and was becoming very dissatisfied.  I have to include Amazon in this review because of their great marketing strategy with Prime Video.  Also, if it wasn't for Amazon and showing Fubo TV as a potential channel, I could have missed this channel completely.  After reviewing the shows I was watching through satellite, and doing my research, Fubo provides all of the sports channels I like, my local channels (for real--my actual local channels!) and other channels I watched through satellite.  AND, they have a great DVR storage program and the channels I can still watch live.  I have no regrets; my family can watch their shows without add-on.  Everything dear to us is included.  Great job Amazon and Fubo TV; thank you!  Very satisfied customer.

Headings: Cheaper and better than Satellite and Cable with better picture quality
Base_Reviews: Very easy to use with Smart TV and fire stick. All the channels you could possibly want and many more! Best part is the cloud dvr that you can access from anywhere. We have only had it a week but so far very happy. Plus it is incredibly cheaper than cable or satellite providers without all the stupid shopping channels and garbage fillers to tell you have 400 channels. No contract and all the sports channels are included along with local networks. Actually much better picture quality as well.

We cancelled our very expensive satellite TV subscription. We bought antennas and Fire TV set up on both of our televisions. They canceled BEIN sports on most satellite providers, but FuboTV has 12 BEIN sports channels. My husband has more football (soccer) than he can watch. I get all of the channels that I ever want or need to watch. Don't wait to switch. The antennas are a cinch to hook up. The Fire TV is fool proof. I am very, very impressed with the set up. Our Alexa remote is a universal remote, controlling the TV and soundbar. FuboTV is inexpensive and has an amazing channel line up. Check it out!

We did a one week trial during the World Series.  It was a little more difficult to set up than expected, but only took about 15 minutes, I guess.  At one point, we were just watching the video, and the stream just paused.  Did a netspeed test on my phone, and we had 200mbps download...stream still paused.  Had to restart the stream to get it going again.  Took about 5 minutes.  Also, the second time we started it up no audio, switched to Netflix and the audio popped in, then back to fubo and there was audio.For $65/mo I would just expect a better interface.  Enjoyed games 5 and 6 of the series, but then cancelled right away.  For the price, definitely not for us.

Headings: Great choice over cable for sports fans
Base_Reviews: I am enjoying using FuboTV for watching all of my sports (baseball, football, golf, basketball, etc..).  The service is the only one that I have found that includes the sports channels that carry my local teams.  The only reason I did not give a 5 star rating is that while watching local channels like ABC it will skip back 30 minutes or so all of the sudden.  If you are not paying attention you will not realize you are watching a stream from 30 minutes in the past.  You just have to switch channels and switch back and it goes back to a live stream.  I have only noticed this on the local channels like ABC.  I did watch the Redzone channel this past Sunday and did not experience buffering which was great.

I recently moved and have been unable to get suddenlink cable or directv or dish satellite services to provide service at my location (too many trees for satellite and the cable company is a joke, won't even provide a quote to extend service) so I began exploring cable alternatives.  FuboTv has a great selection of channels and it works on the devices I have.  The stream quality has been decent with the limited bandwidth I have (approx. 15mbps) and the picture quality is good most of the time.  I suspect this has more to do with my internet provider than it does the FuboTV service, I will try to update when my speeds get an upgrade in a month or so.  The cost isn't bad, but when compared to other services, it is probably about $10/month higher than it should be.  I WOULD recommend this to others as a good cable/satellite alternative.

Headings: The most channels Sports and Non - are in this app
Base_Reviews: I have used Sling, Pluto, Hulu, and a few others - attempting to replicate the amount of channels you would have with satellite, and I am happy to say with this APP I have done it.  On Sling - they advertise local channels but you don't get all of them - with Fubo you do.  Sling you have about 50 hours DVR - here you have 500.  Sling does not have Oxygen, WE and a few other channels that I like and that are included here.Sports - I don't' care - but if you do - there is a ton to choose from.I did only give them 4 stars however for 2 reasons:A.  The volume on some commercials is crazy loud so you have to run and turn the tv down when they come on.B.  There is no continue watching or way of going to the last show you were watching from the Home Screen.  If you are not in your recordings - then selecting continue watching - you would not see anything else you had been in the middle of.  So when I pause and go back into the app - I have to manually search for the last show I was streaming, or watching to continue and have to remember that.  HULU, PLUTO, SLING all have that feature so if you were watching a show 2 days ago - you can find it rather than searching - and that makes a real difference!

I liked the channel line up.  I primarily wanted the regional Foxsports channel (my local teams) and Foxnews, Foxbusiness.After that I wanted the more popular cable channels...USA, TNT, WE, AMC, TCM, Hallmark, History, etc.The initial load time is fairly quick.The FF and REW function works well.I like that the cloud DVR recordings do not expire.I have noticed the picture quality occasionally deteriorates (probably more my ISP than Fubo).I cancelled because I had already signed up with another service.As soon as that service expires at the end of the month, I will come back to Fubo.

At $65 a month, Iâ€™m not really cutting my cable bill when you factor in internet. BUT Iâ€™d rather pay these guys than the cable company who just canâ€™t seem to update to lower prices or offer you less and pay less.We have kids and this is simple to use and has all the stuff they want (â€œneedâ€� lol). Way easier to use than the dumb cable boxes and still have the option to record and DVR.Itâ€™s also got golf channel which isnâ€™t on one of the SLING packages. Therefore you have to get both if you have kids because none of the kids channels are on the sports one.Give it a try; you wonâ€™t be upset.

It's early days still, but this has changed TV life for the better. We cancelled our cable because we only had it for Bein Sports and then Comcast removed it from the lineup. We decided to try FuboTV. Now we have multiple Bein Sports channels and the resolution is way better than it was from Comcast. Not to mention that you get a whole lot of other channels that rack up your price in cable packages. We have the regular Fubo package. The one hitch we have experienced is that at times there is a brief hitch sometimes while watching, however it is always resolved in 5-10 seconds. What an improvement from cable.

Headings: Lagging compared to other devices that are streaming with Fubo
Base_Reviews: The fubo TV app as a whole is the same across devices, I have it on iphone and ipad and the experience is the same. However, the fubo TV app on the fire stick lags about 20-25 seconds compared to having the same stream on iphone or ipad. Considering that the iphone/ipad are 10-15 secs behind a TV provider like spectrum, it makes it hard to view live sports so far behind. I am okay with 10-15 seconds behind but not 35-40 secs behind. If the Fubo guys can fix this and make all devices have the stream at the same time it would be awesome. For now, I am still using the lighting to hdmi converter and using my ipad to view fuboTV on the big screen.

Great cord cutter app for FireTV or Roku. They offer plenty of sports channels but I watch mostly the local channels and news channel. Works great on my smartphone and iPad as well when I am not home, over WiFi. The app seems to always work well never see any buffering (unless there is a local internet issuse going on on - but i find that hardly ever to be the case.) They have a good lineup of channels for the money. The DVR feature works great. They give you 30hrs DVR time and offer more for a fee but 30 hrs for me is plenty! I like how a show may almost be over - just DVR it before it is over and you get the whole show! Nice!

Headings: The answer I was looking for
Base_Reviews: We had to get rid of cable because of the cost. I love this app. So easy to find shows and record what I want to see later. That part actually works better than my cable did. It has exactly the 7 channels that I needed for watching my shows. The rest that are included are bonus for me. I highly recommend it if you see the channels that you like in the package

Headings: Almost a 5 star if they had ABC
Base_Reviews: I would give this a 5 star but a local channel is missing for me as they have no ABC. But they do have everything else you can think of including the weather channel. (Big one for me in Florida)With all the others either stopping their services or continuing to go up in pricing I landed on Fubo. Not the cheapest and hope they don't start to go up, but I think the best out there. My only wish list is they has their GUI set up so you could have more than one profile so my wife could have her own set of favorites and a little more 4K. But all good otherwise.

Headings: FUBO works great on my system
Base_Reviews: I have been using FUBO for one week using my Amazon FireStick.  I had a few growing pains with my fire-stick and Amazon provided nearly immediate help that solved my problems.  I subscribed to FUBO because it had the VERY BEST array of channels that we watch.  Everyone must review all of the streaming services to determine which is best for personal or family viewing habits.  I did not select FUBO for their movie library, but rather for streaming live TV programs that I used to watch on cable.  My biggest problem with FUBO was to learn how to navigate the HOME page with the fire-stick remote.  FUBO customer service and Amazon customer service representatives were very helpful.  For my "big network" viewing, I purchased a digital antenna and placed it behind a picture.  I receive 54 channels and picture clarity is great. VERY HAPPY WITH FUBO!

Headings: I definitely recommended to friends who do enjoy sports
Base_Reviews: Got 30 days free with Roku purchase. Worked flawlessly for FIFA 2018 (the only sports event I am interested in). HD quality reception, no buffering and cloud DVR all worked perfectly for me. Since I only wanted it for the world cup, I unsubscribed after the final game which was also a smooth process. If I watched enough sports  to justify the price, I would not hesitate to continue the service. I definitely recommended to friends who do enjoy sports.

I use Fubo TV for most of my TV News and entertainment experience.  I got the app for the Hallmark channels and Fox News, plus my husband can get all the sports events that he likes.  One of the big reasons I have stayed with Fubo is their tech support.  I use an old version of Roku and when I had trouble getting Fubo, they adapted my Fubo app to fit my Roku.  That made me really happy.

To those thinking about subscribing:-FuboTV provides a superb quality HD stream on PC.. I can't speak for Roku's quality because I don't own one.-If you want Serie A coverage, you'll have to get the "Spanish add-on", which is an extra $3 - 4 per month (worth it, IMO)-Aside from the EFL cup, there is no coverage of the English Premier League. I don't mind this quite so much because I have NBCSN and FS1 on cable.. However if you lack cable and EPL coverage is a necessity for you, I'd recommend Sling Blue.
