Headings: The Content is not free, and I'm more than OK with that
Base_Reviews: This is a great app, as it provides additional coverage and replays of sports from the NBC family of networks, where NBC is permitted by their contract with the leagues, associations, or other governing bodies to show them. During the English Premier League campaign, it's a handy app to have in case your team isn't playing one of the featured games. Olympic coverage has been great for watching replays of events that I missed or live events that aren't front line (Think Canada Ladies Football or Curling).Don't let most of the other reviews cloud your judgement, this provides quality playback for content that I pay for with a cable subscription. Most of the 1-star reviews have outlandish expectations that because the app is free, they should also be receiving content that is paid content elsewhere. The review pool is full of these ridiculous expectations.If you're trying to get NBC Sports content after cutting the cord, this isn't the app for you. They don't currently have a paid-subscription app, maybe try Sling TV if you're looking for access to the content.As for the performance, I'm on 100Mbps  internet provided by Optimum (also my TV provider), and very rarely have any issues playing back in HD (resolution dependent upon programming) while using a wired ethernet connection. Only during the Stanley Cup Playoffs did I encounter any technical issues, and that was with the placement (or misplacement) of digitally inserted ads during the course of play.Excellent Uses for the app:- Live Coverage of events not on broadcast channels- Replays- Making the channel portable to TVs without cable access (ie. Secondary Bedrooms, Travelling in hotels)

You still have to put up with commercials that it seemed like you couldn't skip and some really long intermissions that you could FF through, but hey there's never a totally free lunch so OK.  The commentary was the real deal, just like you were at the show, without any commercialized hype so that was a fair tradeoff. Headings: A good security camera monitor that takes technical skill to use and set up.
Base_Reviews: This app allows you to monitor your video security system at home.  Please be aware that if you are not on a WIFI you are using your mobile deviceâ€™s data plan and you may be using a lot of data transferring videos and photos.  You can actually make your Android device a mobile DVR.  Remember.  Donâ€™t forget your data plan limits.I own and use multiple security camera and DVR systems within my home that monitor and record the video on internal hard disk drives.  All of them are accessible via the internet and WIFI as they all come with their own Apps that allow interfacing to my Android and Apple devices.  This software is thus redundant for me to use.When I first scanned my network for cameras the system found none.  It is because it was on the wrong WIFI network and I had to change the WIFI settings for my Samsung tablet to the same network that the security system is on.  If you canâ€™t find your camera you have to go to your smart device settings and change the network access.  If you have not used that WIFI on your device you will have to know the SSID and the password for that WIFI system to sign on.Once I scanned the right network the system found my servers, security cameras and my ubiquity Network system.  I logged into the Foscam system and the app then asked me what the camera password was.  Remember you can lock your security DVRs and even individual cameras for privacy and you will have to know that data to sign on.  Upon entering the correct data the camera location popped up and displayed the cameraâ€™s live video.By tapping on the live video I was able to see the camera video full screen and touch the record icon and record the video.  You are also able to use the camera motion detection systems to minimize the amount of transferred data and only collect data when movement is present and being monitored.The benefit of this app is that you may be able to combine multiple camera networks into one app for monitoring and checking.  Just be aware that if you are not on the same WIFI network the ability to see the video may be blocked by your cable modem.  That is a long discussion and it is not possible to cover here. You can possibly even add in local camera if you have their IP address like a local school or weather network.  As part of a demo you can see random action cameras working around the world that are public for example.This is a nice app but again I warn you to be aware of your mobile data plan limits. Headings: ... app is top-notch if you have IP cameras you'd like to control remotely
Base_Reviews: This app is top-notch if you have IP cameras you'd like to control remotely. I know most IP cameras offer some sort of proprietary app with limited features -- "light versions", and then also their own with advanced features -- "pro versions". I own 2 IP cameras, different models, but same company and still find that tinyCam Monitor PRO meets my needs.The camera discovery option is great. I like being able to press a button to have it discover all of the cameras on my network. The only problem I have with this is that it will use the local IP address to add it. If you plan to use the app away from home (outside of wifi range), you'll need to adjust the (advanced) IP settings accordingly. Also depending on your home setup, you may have to forward a couple ports etc.The PTZ (pan tilt zoom) is great -- you can use a single-button option, where you press and it moves a little, or you can use what I'll call a "continuous" version where you swipe and control the movement more fluidly.I really like having almost ALL of the same options the manufacturer's own software provides. Kudos to the developers on a great product!I received this product for free around June-ish -- I can't remember if it was an Amazon promotion or one from the developer. I only was able to review it now since I only now have compatible IP cameras. With that said, trying to add a camera that isn't network-discoverable (through the built-in search option) offers plenty of manufacturers. If you go to the developers website they have an easier to follow list of compatible machines.

Overall this is a great app that I've used for about 3 years.  I have multiple Foscam cameras and the app has worked well from my phones, tablets and Fire TV devices.  My biggest complaints would be: (1) there is no side-by-side two camera view on widescreen displays, and (2) the network auto-detect gets some settings wrong for my cameras.  But once configured, this app has worked reliably for me.I previously wrote a negative review citing problems with this app after updating my Samsung Galaxy Note 5 to the latest version of Android.  However, after some digging I found that the problem was with with Amazon.  There was a major hiccup with Amazon's licensing system that caused problems with many apps, not just TinyCam Monitor.The solution was to remove my phone from my list of Amazon registered devices, then re-register it.  Anyone facing the same issue can remove their device by going to Amazon.com, Your Account > Your Apps and Devices.  Then go to the Amazon app store on your device and you will be prompted to log in which will fix the registration.  If the app still doesn't work then you can try reinstalling it.----------------------------------ORIGINAL REVIEW:This used to work perfectly until the most recent update.  Now I get an prompt about an internal error and not having a network connection followed by an error about not having a license (both of which are wrong). Headings: IMO TinyCam has a superior operating interface than Amcrest Video Pro
Base_Reviews: Here's how to set up an Amcrest IP Cam with TinyCam.IMO TinyCam has a superior operating interface than Amcrest Video Pro. Just my humble opinion.WARNING: There is one import issue I have with TinyCam Montor. When you close out of it on your Android cell phone(at least older ones)... it doesn't actually close the program, and that sucker will run in the background sucking up your data GB, and also the power in your battery. Do yourself a favor, and download a decent APP Killer, to prevent this, and remember to kill TinyCam when you're done using it.=========================================================================Setting up an Amcrest IP2M-841 on TinyCamMonitor Pro on Android Cell Phone or Tablet.=========================================================================Note that you need to set up port forwarding (HTTP & RSTP Ports) in your Router and your Amcrest Camera before being able to remotely access the camera with TinyCam Monitor Pro (using  CameraDomainName.amcrestddns.com). I have an in depth discussion & instructions on setting up port forwarding, and setting up the Amcrest in my review of the Amcrest IP2M-841.Check my reviews to find that if you're interested. In that review, we used example numbers for the HTTP and RSTP forwarded ports, and gave them some pretend numbers for example's sake. The numbers were HTTP PORT = 12345  RSTP PORT = 23456.I make reference to these pretend numbers in these instructions.======================Instructions======================Make sure WiFi on the android device is turned on,and logged into the network that your Amcrest I/P Camera is on.From the drop down menu at top left, select "Manage Camera"Click the "+" to add a camera, and then "Scan Network".It should see your camera. Select your camera and tap "+" again.Then it shows your camera selected in a list with any other cameras (TinyCam Monitor comes with a default of several webcams.I simply un-check them because it sucks up data...BIGTIME.Hold your finger on your camera and a drop down list pops up... select "Edit Camera".It shows your cameras I/P address and HTTP port automatically (assuming yo already set up your port forwarding.Select Camera Name, and give it whatever name you like.Select Camera Vendor, and click Amcrest from the drop down list.Select Camera Model and pick IP2M-841 from the dropdown list.Select Username, and enter the username you use for logging into camera (please tell me you changed it from admin)Select Password, and enter the Password you use for logging into camera (please tell me you changed it from admin)Select the RSTP port and change it from the default value to the number you picked (in our example it was 23456).At the very bottom of the list, select Advanced Settings which takes you to a different page.Select Remote Hostname/IP Address, and change it from your current WAN address to the camera name you gave it on the Hostname in the DDNS setting. Follow the name with .amcrestddns.org. From or example in the main discussion it would be amcrest12345.amcrestddns.comSelect Web Port and enter the HTTP port number which you forwarded. In our example it was 12345Select Remote RSTP port, and enter the RSTP port which you also forwarded. In our example it was 23456That's it... you're done. The camera should be working with the Wifi on through your network, or Remotely with the WiFi off via cell phone signal.

All you have to do is make sure you have the app that goes along with this app on and open on your Fire TV and it will mirror your Fire Tablet to your Fire TV, as long as you also have this app open on your Fire Tablet.  This app also works on TVs that have a Fire Stick attached to it, as long as you have the apps open on your Fire Tablet and TV that has a Fire Stick attached to it.  What is beautiful about the apps is you do not have to have the mirroring option on your Fire Tablet, because I don't have the mirroring option on my Fire Tablet since my Fire Tablet is a newer Fire Tablet and this app works like a charm.  If the apps are open on your Fire Tablet and Fire TV or TV that has a Fire Stick attached to it and the app does not pick up your Fire TV or TV that has a Fire Stick attached to it, then pick the option on the mirroring app that is open on your Fire Tablet that is designates mirror by ID, then type in the six digits that are right beneath the bar code that is on your Fire TV or TV that has a Fire Stick attached it that is on the open app on them.  It definitely works like it supposed to work.  You should also pay the $4.99 (cost of this app at time of this writing) for the Pro Version, because it works a lot better than the free version, as long as you buy the Pro Version for the Fire Tablet that mirrors to the Fire TV  and Fire Stick attached to your TV. Please be aware that if you are not on a WIFI you are using your mobile deviceâ€™s data plan and you may be using a lot of data transferring videos and photos. Donâ€™t forget your data plan limits.I own and use multiple security camera and DVR systems within my home that monitor and record the video on internal hard disk drives.  All of them are accessible via the internet and WIFI as they all come with their own Apps that allow interfacing to my Android and Apple devices.  This software is thus redundant for me to use.When I first scanned my network for cameras the system found none.  It is because it was on the wrong WIFI network and I had to change the WIFI settings for my Samsung tablet to the same network that the security system is on.  If you canâ€™t find your camera you have to go to your smart device settings and change the network access.  If you have not used that WIFI on your device you will have to know the SSID and the password for that WIFI system to sign on.Once I scanned the right network the system found my servers, security cameras and my ubiquity Network system.  I logged into the Foscam system and the app then asked me what the camera password was.  Remember you can lock your security DVRs and even individual cameras for privacy and you will have to know that data to sign on.  Upon entering the correct data the camera location popped up and displayed the cameraâ€™s live video.By tapping on the live video I was able to see the camera video full screen and touch the record icon and record the video.  You are also able to use the camera motion detection systems to minimize the amount of transferred data and only collect data when movement is present and being monitored.The benefit of this app is that you may be able to combine multiple camera networks into one app for monitoring and checking.  Just be aware that if you are not on the same WIFI network the ability to see the video may be blocked by your cable modem.  That is a long discussion and it is not possible to cover here. Headings: ... app is top-notch if you have IP cameras you'd like to control remotely
Base_Reviews: This app is top-notch if you have IP cameras you'd like to control remotely. I know most IP cameras offer some sort of proprietary app with limited features -- "light versions", and then also their own with advanced features -- "pro versions". I own 2 IP cameras, different models, but same company and still find that tinyCam Monitor PRO meets my needs.The camera discovery option is great. I like being able to press a button to have it discover all of the cameras on my network. The only problem I have with this is that it will use the local IP address to add it. If you plan to use the app away from home (outside of wifi range), you'll need to adjust the (advanced) IP settings accordingly. Also depending on your home setup, you may have to forward a couple ports etc.The PTZ (pan tilt zoom) is great -- you can use a single-button option, where you press and it moves a little, or you can use what I'll call a "continuous" version where you swipe and control the movement more fluidly.I really like having almost ALL of the same options the manufacturer's own software provides. Kudos to the developers on a great product!I received this product for free around June-ish -- I can't remember if it was an Amazon promotion or one from the developer. I only was able to review it now since I only now have compatible IP cameras. With that said, trying to add a camera that isn't network-discoverable (through the built-in search option) offers plenty of manufacturers. If you go to the developers website they have an easier to follow list of compatible machines.

Anyone facing the same issue can remove their device by going to Amazon.com, Your Account > Your Apps and Devices. Do yourself a favor, and download a decent APP Killer, to prevent this, and remember to kill TinyCam when you're done using it.=========================================================================Setting up an Amcrest IP2M-841 on TinyCamMonitor Pro on Android Cell Phone or Tablet.=========================================================================Note that you need to set up port forwarding (HTTP & RSTP Ports) in your Router and your Amcrest Camera before being able to remotely access the camera with TinyCam Monitor Pro (using  CameraDomainName.amcrestddns.com). I have an in depth discussion & instructions on setting up port forwarding, and setting up the Amcrest in my review of the Amcrest IP2M-841.Check my reviews to find that if you're interested. In that review, we used example numbers for the HTTP and RSTP forwarded ports, and gave them some pretend numbers for example's sake. The numbers were HTTP PORT = 12345  RSTP PORT = 23456.I make reference to these pretend numbers in these instructions.======================Instructions======================Make sure WiFi on the android device is turned on,and logged into the network that your Amcrest I/P Camera is on.From the drop down menu at top left, select "Manage Camera"Click the "+" to add a camera, and then "Scan Network".It should see your camera. Select your camera and tap "+" again.Then it shows your camera selected in a list with any other cameras (TinyCam Monitor comes with a default of several webcams.I simply un-check them because it sucks up data...BIGTIME.Hold your finger on your camera and a drop down list pops up... select "Edit Camera".It shows your cameras I/P address and HTTP port automatically (assuming yo already set up your port forwarding.Select Camera Name, and give it whatever name you like.Select Camera Vendor, and click Amcrest from the drop down list.Select Camera Model and pick IP2M-841 from the dropdown list.Select Username, and enter the username you use for logging into camera (please tell me you changed it from admin)Select Password, and enter the Password you use for logging into camera (please tell me you changed it from admin)Select the RSTP port and change it from the default value to the number you picked (in our example it was 23456).At the very bottom of the list, select Advanced Settings which takes you to a different page.Select Remote Hostname/IP Address, and change it from your current WAN address to the camera name you gave it on the Hostname in the DDNS setting. Follow the name with .amcrestddns.org. From or example in the main discussion it would be amcrest12345.amcrestddns.comSelect Web Port and enter the HTTP port number which you forwarded. In our example it was 12345Select Remote RSTP port, and enter the RSTP port which you also forwarded. In our example it was 23456That's it... you're done. The camera should be working with the Wifi on through your network, or Remotely with the WiFi off via cell phone signal.

Just a note: a lot of unpopular sports do not have commentary or even sound equipment, so don't be thrown off when the World Billiards Tournament Game is silent. The NBC Sports website wasn't particularly responsive when it came to pairing my Fire TV either. Make sure you log in asap and not wait until a game is about to come on!

Headings: NBC Sports INDYCAR commentators also carried on NBC Gold
Base_Reviews: NBC Sports did a good job at St Pete and I fully expect the rest of the season to go as "smoothly", relatively. The professional commentators were a pleasure to see on the net and I appreciated the consistency of the weekend broadcasts. However, to further promote the sport itself, which is still in its year-by-year upswing in both spectator attendance and TV ratings, I would have preferred NBC Gold offering free practice and qualification runs and a smaller charge for the race itself this year only. This would promote more transference of the website over the continuation of buying NBCSN cable for motor racing only.

Headings: Olympics on Fire TV Stick. Yes with this specific App. Here is how.
Base_Reviews: This works for Olympics on Fire TV Stick without a cable provider but watch the glitch. Each time the app reopens it toggles in the top left between the logo for this app, and the logo for the standard app which needs a cable account. Pay attention, ignore the other logo. I will add a pic if it goes through with this review.When you are in this app on this device there will be a row with hundreds of live or upcoming events. When the network is showing Olympics on NBC broadcast TV, a box for this will be in the mix of events. That mirrors the NBC broadcast, and will end as the network does. Look at the pic I will try to attach.The majority of the events are raw with no announcers or scoring, but is excellent quality, and some of the practices are shown as well.A similar App on Roku misbehaved badly for me.

I have to sign out,and resign in, by going to nbcsports.com/active and type in a code This is an irritating "feature".  Overwall, I still love the PL and quality of shows and otherwise ease of use.

Headings: Amazing Olympic Games coverage on Amazon Fire TV
Base_Reviews: The Olympic Games represent the highest accomplishments of the athletes who have made it to these games in Brazil. As a native South American, I am tremendously proud of these games being held in the continent of my birth and, as far as I have witnessed, the great success that is being accomplished by the host country. I'm very appreciative of the coverage which is available on NBC Sports through my Amazon Five TV service and I am able to follow all of my favorite sports through this brilliant service. Headings: Good quality stable HD streams, easy to navigate on Fire TV
Base_Reviews: This app works fine. The video quality is good. Slight motion blur, but this is common with all streaming apps. I'd really like a sports app in 1080@60hz, but I don't think we'll see this until ISP's stop capping bandwidth use.Also, I find it a little silly that people mark the app down because you need a cable subscription. This is a premium cable channel. Yes, you'll need to pay for it. Yes, even for the app. How could you expect anything different? What, they'll just give away their channel in an app when everyone else has to pay for cable to get it? What sense does that make? At least they don't charge you an extra monthly fee like so many other apps do. If you're already paying for the channel via cable, then you get it on mobile too. This is common sense and has nothing to do with how well the app itself works, which is actually quite good.

Headings: The Content is not free, and I'm more than OK with that
Base_Reviews: This is a great app, as it provides additional coverage and replays of sports from the NBC family of networks, where NBC is permitted by their contract with the leagues, associations, or other governing bodies to show them. During the English Premier League campaign, it's a handy app to have in case your team isn't playing one of the featured games. Olympic coverage has been great for watching replays of events that I missed or live events that aren't front line (Think Canada Ladies Football or Curling).Don't let most of the other reviews cloud your judgement, this provides quality playback for content that I pay for with a cable subscription. Most of the 1-star reviews have outlandish expectations that because the app is free, they should also be receiving content that is paid content elsewhere. The review pool is full of these ridiculous expectations.If you're trying to get NBC Sports content after cutting the cord, this isn't the app for you. They don't currently have a paid-subscription app, maybe try Sling TV if you're looking for access to the content.As for the performance, I'm on 100Mbps  internet provided by Optimum (also my TV provider), and very rarely have any issues playing back in HD (resolution dependent upon programming) while using a wired ethernet connection. Only during the Stanley Cup Playoffs did I encounter any technical issues, and that was with the placement (or misplacement) of digitally inserted ads during the course of play.Excellent Uses for the app:- Live Coverage of events not on broadcast channels- Replays- Making the channel portable to TVs without cable access (ie. Secondary Bedrooms, Travelling in hotels)

Headings: One of the best options for streaming TV
Base_Reviews: Let me start by saying that like many others I became a cordcutter due to frustration with ever-escalating cable bills. Plus I was already spending money on Netflix, Hulu and Amazon Prime so literally thousands of shows and movies available but still wanted a decent option for viewing live broadcasts and cable channels when away from home, which the cable company didn't provide. Therefore, when I initially cut the cord and returned my cable box and TiVo cablecard, I spent several months with DirecTV NOW, and also trialed the live tv options from Hulu, Sling, YouTube and a few others as well and either had issues with the interface, the channel selection or the price.fuboTV provides a robust assortment of channels and was the only option that provided access to local NBA coverage within the base package (which is priced at $45 and depending on which promo you get may be discounted for the first month or two). With the competitors, local NBA coverage was either unavailable or a paid upgrade.The image quality is superb, sharper than any image I've seen before as they broadcast in 4K. However, perhaps due to the speed of my internet connection (20mB/sec), oftentimes the image will be pixelated for a second when a program is initially loaded. I love the fact that I can watch on my Firestick, my phone, my laptop from anywhere and DVR the programs I'm viewing.In addition to viewing live tv, fuboTV provides an EXTENSIVE library of current and past TV shows (both from the major networks and cable channels) and movies that you can watch on demand, very similar to Hulu. Most of the TV shows are popular shows but some have are very good shows that I had never heard of before. Prior to last week, you couldn't type a title to search for a program or movies on the Amazon app, only browse alphabetically. Now that you can search on any device I'm a happy camper and I love being able to watch programs on any device. Also, if you need to login to an app such as CNN or SYFY, fuboTV is on the listing of supported cable providers.I have two minor quibbles:1. The standard DVR recording capacity is just 20 hours and it's $10 to upgrade, which gets you 500 hours of capacity. If they had an option in the middle for $5 I would go for it but as my objective is to save money versus having cable TV, I'm good for now.2. When you first open the app it will feature sporting events playing currently or later in the day and you have to make a few extra clicks to get to the program guide. Typically they will feature soccer games and as I'm not a big soccer fan I could do without this and would prefer an option to load the guide by default.

Headings: Best value of all the Streaming services we tried.
Base_Reviews: Had the absolute least missing channels my family watches vs all of the other services we reviewed, being 2. ABC and The CW were missing. About a week later they added The CW to there line-up. Very good service and quality, 3 available streams concurrent and 500 hours of DVR for $55 a month as of this writing. Hulu was missing 5 channels, ATT watchtv was missing more and on down the list they went. Almost none of them other then ATT and Hulu carry ABC since ABC is a Disney Property, and they want you to use their services. Not happening. The only downside we have had with Fubo.TV was using USA as the commercials (and the service tells you bottom left) how many commercials during the break, it would sometimes play 1 of 5 then 2 of 5 then 3 of 5 then go back to 2 of 5 then 3 of 5 then back to 1 of 5. Playing the same commercials over and over and over. I reported this issue to Fubo. So far no change. Using the USA app ( a cable or TV account like Dish or Direct etc, is necessary to use any APPS solo outside of Fubo), doesn't have that issue, nor amount of commercials as high as 15. Other channels within Fubo don't seem to suffer this bug.  I use it mostly for Netflix or Prime, so obviously no commercials. The cons if you wanna call them that, doesn't change my mind of how great this service is and how easy it is to use it.

I absolutely love Fubo. They have something for everyone. Nickelodeon  and Disney for children, Hallmark, Lifetime, TLC, A&E, AMC, Discovery, MTV,VH1, WE, Food Network and more for people who like lifestyle channels and Sports. I have Roku and Firestick. With Roku you can fast forward and see the tiles but with Firestick you cannot. That would be nice if they offered the same feature for Firestick. It never buffers...of course because I have great internet speed. Fubo offers more channels than Hulu Live and YTTV. I hope Fubo stays at this price with the channels weâ€™re getting. It is a good service.  I didn't have any problems with service, but it is on the high end of price without having a good amount of channels that I usually watch.  If you are a fan of sports, especially Latin American and European based teams, this is for you.  There are a good amount of channels that you would typically pay extra for to get in the base package here (maybe the cause of the higher price).  I did have a slight problem with navigation, but I only had the 7 day trial and did not get a good feel for how it worked.  I think with time I would get used to it.  Overall a good product but I would go with Hulu TV, YouTube TV, or Sling if I had the choice.  They offer things I like to watch at a slightly lower cost.

I can't believe how good the video quality is! If I had known this, I would have dropped PSVue a long time ago, especially because we love watching Bruins' hockey games. We can see the puck now! We only get 10 to 12 Mb/sec internet speed with our Wifi connection using the Firestick and the streaming quality far surpasses PSVue. No buffering now. I cannot understand all of these negative reviews. What on earth are they talking about? I was very skeptical to try FUBO due to all of the complaints. I'm sure that most of those complaints are coming from people who either have poor internet service or are terribly upset that they have to learn a new way to navigate their tv service. (paradigm shift anyone?) To be fair, there are some minor differences that may be annoying to some, like the fact that you have to schedule each and every episode of the shows you want to DVR. But DirecTV's satellite service had the same limitation. We became spoiled with PSVue's DVR functionality. Hopefully, FUBO resolves this in the future. We are paying the extra 5 bucks/month for one extra device and the extra DVR space. I am so glad that Sony dropped NESN!!! Thank you Sony for steering us to FUBOtv! Don't believe the BS about not being able to cancel your FUBO free trial. Just set up your account on the web and you can access your subscription from there. Simple. No one is trying to steal your money. I also had one quirky thing happen the very first time I logged into my free trial. I had two audio tracks playing simultaneously with about a one second delay between. I simply exited the FUBO app with the Firestick's home button, arrowed up to Amazon's top menu, over to "settings", down to "FireTV" and selected "Restart". While I was waiting for that to reboot, I decided to click on the help button of FUBO's website. I started a chat session with their customer service. They recommended deleting the app from the Firestick menu and then restart the Firestick but since I had already begun the reboot, I let it finish. I had no problems at all since then. So it was a minor glitch, easily remedied, and customer service was available within seconds! Outstanding, great job FUBO!!!

Headings: If you like sports. This is the App for you
Base_Reviews: Got this for my Father-in-law. He stayed up until 4:30 am watching it and playing with it. after one night of using it. they cancelled their Dish Network account and are completely happy to pay the 50.00 a month. Besides the all of the sports channels someone could ever want (he is a soccer fan and loves the BeIn sports channels and there are 10 of them). there is regular programming like A&E, CBS, NBC, Hallmark ect.... WIll save them 80.00 a month compared to their satellite service.

WHAT OTHERS HAVE MARKED THIS OFF FORContinuing to charge them after cancellation: I am continuing my subscription, so I cannot comment on this.Freezing: I watched the third place World Cup game and had no issues. I watched Leicester v. Man U and it only froze once when I took it to mobile and left the house. A few other PL games on NBC Sports have frozen for a minute or two. But overall, I do not get what others talk about when they say that it is so terrible. Even cable has its moments, sometimes much worse.Bad picture: Looks fine to me. Maybe the first ten seconds aren't great, but again, isn't that true with almost anything?Slow loading: Okay, here I have a hack. When I start fubo.tv from my Amazon Fire TV homepage, a loading circle comes up, often with the fubo background, but not always. It will rarely come out of this by itself. But I have noticed that if I press the back button, it immediately snaps out of it and doesn't take me back but instead takes me directly to fubo. Odd thing, but in the end, it's fine for me.You cannot rewind a live game, the way that you can on NBC Sports apps or Fox Soccer Match Pass, et al: Accurate. Goals may happen and you won't be able to see them if you are not there at the exact time or you didn't record it.MY MARKDOWNSPremier League: You think that you are getting NBC Sports, Bravo, USA (?)--every possible network you could in order to watch the Premier League (aside from the money-grubbing NBC Sports Gold). But you forget the obvious: NBC. It comes with your local Fox and CBS, but not ABC or NBC. I have found articles on fubo that say that with the TVEverywhere app, you can log-in to the NBCSports app with your fubo credentials and it will treat it like a cable subscription. This has not been the case for me. I am not clear why I was rejected, other than a message that said something like "We're sorry, this provider does not have retransmission rights in your region". From a fubo page, it appears that NBC in my market (Oklahoma City) is not carried (while others like Tulsa and tons of other markets are). I have confirmed this both on the NBC Sports site and on the app, where I have received the same message. So if I were 90 miles to the NW, then I would have this? This is not progress. The fubo article also says that I must have the TVEverywhere channel in my fubo subscription in order for this to work, yet when I search fubo packages for this channel, I find no such listing.Champions League: Heads up--I thought that I would be getting TBS & TNT, and the last I heard, the Champions League was moving to this family of stations in the coming year. But those are not actually included. I just overlooked it.How to make this better: NBC sucks. When it split its games across NBC, Bravo, USA, NBC Sports, it could act like it is helping the fan, but then when it puts some things on a platform like fubo and others, like NBC, not, then that's a big pain. It is either mistakenly not considering this or it is intentionally doing this for its own benefit to make things like this more cumbersome for the consumer, hoping that they buy something like fubo/sling and cable on top of it. I look forward to when NBC and others catch on to how they could make even more money by making life easier for the consumer rather than harder. After all, I hardly watch American football at all anymore. Everyone can turn you off.But what does that mean for fubo? I would like to see fubo make it easier to see NBC, or to at least have my questions answered. It knows that I want to see the Premier League. So list every game. When I click on it, tell me that it is on NBC Sports or Bravo, which I have, and take me there. If that particular game is on NBC Sports Gold, tell me that, and maybe NBC will pay for that ad. If it is actually on NBC itself, then give me a brief and clear instruction on how to watch NBC, and if I cannot, then please tell me why.I also don't find the guide that helpful. I prefer not to look at what is on TV currently because by the time you scroll through all your channels, if you want to go back up to the top and watch something that you saw up there, it takes so long just to get up there. I wind up perusing just the networks, where it lists them in rows of four, which allows me to scroll through to the channel that I want faster, if not the exact programming.WHAT IT GETS RIGHTI watch mostly BBC World News, HGTV, and sports-related channels. The Fubo network is pretty good--kind of like ESPN classic for soccer, but without actual game film. It also has Bein Sports, which has worked well the few times that I have watched it so far. The website is also pretty good.OVERALLIt does great with giving access to French and Spanish games via Bein Sports, which is nice. However, it offers access to only roughly 1/2 of Premier League games, due to some being on NBC itself and some being on NBC Sports Gold. And it does not offer Champions League games in English at all, although worldsoccertalk.com appears to say that I could watch Champions League and Europa League games in Spanish on Univision, which is on fubo. I don't have a problem with that if it will really happen. But what I want to see is an option where you can click on the sport and then the competition; it does have this, but if I am to judge by that, then that points out a few things: (1) No Serie A; (2) No Champions League or Europa League; (3) just 5/10 Premier League games on this particular weekend.As a stand-alone service judged compared to cable, I am pleased with this. It doesn't give you everything, but it does give you some international soccer extras and things like CBS Sports. Comparing to something like Sling, it appears that Sling wins on your regular cable networks, though they are comparable. But if you are really a big soccer fan, understand that you are basically comparing Bein Sports + $10 to TNT/TBS & ESPN, aka La Liga and Ligue 1 to the Champions League and whatever soccer ESPN offers. If you care a great deal about Mexican and South American games, then that will push up fubo in your eyes.

Headings: Missing ESPN, but excellent enough you may not care
Base_Reviews: Superb picture quality and audio quality. I have Verizon FiOS gigabit internet. The Roku version of the app is the superior version, with the ability to watch television in background as you surf the guide at the lower portion of the screen. There's also a regular vertical guide. Sling and Philo have picture-in-picture capabilitiy on mobile. Fubo TV does not. PS Vue does not, but is ending January 30th, 2020 anyway. Despite the lack of that little mobile convenience, Fubo TV mobile is superb in picture and audio quality. Fast & fluid. Same experience as on Roku and Amazon Fire stick. Can not speak to the experience on PC. Had no interest in that. Incidentally, the experience on mobile, I was making reference to the Android version. On Roku & Firestick 4k I don't like that sometimes I have to back out to another menu to get information on a particular program. But then it is only a few clicks away. Nitpicking. With the glaring omission of ESPN, almost every Sports channel that you could possibly imagine is there. So I will be supplementing this service with a base package subscription to Sling, which carries ESPN. YouTube TV does as well, but I don't desire a full package with YouTube TV. The base package on Sling is cheaper, and I only need the ESPN channels.  Awesome service that is equal in quality and in some ways surpasses that of YouTube TV and the others that are more popular like HULU Live TV. Those are also excellent cord-cutting alternatives, though. So choose the one that's right for you. I've made my choice. Hope this helps.Oh, and Fubo TV I understand is the only live streaming service that has 4k resolution built into the app. I have a TCL & Sony Bravia 4k TV's, and I can attest to the superb picture quality on both using the app. Thanks for reading!

I'm stunned by all the negative reviews for this service. I've run the gauntlet of streaming TV services. PS Vue, directTV now (AT&T TV NOW) sling tv and hulu + live. By far Fubo is the best I've had for many reasons. The best thing I'll say for fubo is this is the one I've had the least buffering with and I mean by a long shot. All of the other services were at times completely unwatchable. I've only had fubo buffer on me a few times for like a few seconds and never more then once in a night of viewing. Plus it's got the best channel lineup of any. The picture quality is noticeably better then the others I've had as well. It is a little pricey but still much cheaper then traditional cable.

Weâ€™ve been using Fubo for about a month and love it! We dropped DirecTv (pretty difficult to do) as the price was getting crazy. Otherwise, itâ€™s only available with DirecTv or a cable provider.The price is a bit higher than I wanted to pay but itâ€™s half of what DirecTv was charging and about 2/3 of Suddenlinkâ€™s cost. Headings: Works great and you can take it anywhere there is decent WIFI
Base_Reviews: I bought FUBO along with Sling and disconnected from Dish.  I use Amazon Fire TV recast and antennae for local channels. I use the Amazon Fire TV Stick on my home TV.  I  got FUBO because it has Fox News, which Sling does not, and Animal Planet.  I have traveled a fair amount and it works great on the road.  I bring my Chromecast dongle with me and cast FUBO to the TV I am using from my Iphone.  The picture is great.  I do love college football and FUBO has most channels other than ESPN.  Like all streaming services, if you like the channel lineup, you won't regret purchasing it.

Headings: I don't regret my choice, after the fact.
Base_Reviews: I find the service good.  This change has reduced my bill substantially.  My bill will be $100.00 less per month all-in (that reduction takes into account that I have added services that I did not previously have - add-ons to FUBO).  I did not have the top of the line cable service from my provider.  Instead I had the third best out of four options from my provider.Is it more complicated than cable TV? Change means adjustment to a different format.  The learning curve is not overwhelming.  For those not well versed with changes in TV services I would recommend getting a younger family members assistance to make the change.  I chose to load FUBO via the Amazon Fire platform.  After the fact I found out that I cannot watch HBO on Amazon's platform.  I can stream it on my iPhone and iPad, as it can be streamed on other devices.  That is inconvenient, but not a deal breaker.  Solution, use the Apple TV platform, the Youtube's platform or I believe ROKU's platform.Note: the number of channels I had access to on cable totaled 220.  On FUBO it is substantially less.  For me this was not a problem, as I complemented what FUBO offers me with HPO and Disney (still I have the stated cost reduction).  I also have Netflix and am an Amazon Prime member, which I had before I left the cable service.  I have more than I have any possibility of ever watching.Best part of this change?  I no longer have a contract.  I can switch any or all of the services I have from one month to the next.

Headings: Some Problems But No Show Stoppers
Base_Reviews: I must say from the start that the only reason I purchased this app for to watch the Giro d'Italia (Italy's version of the Tour de France). I use NBC Sports Gold to watch cycling but the Giro was not a covered race. A quick Google search led me to fubotv. I primarily watch TV through FireTV so I downloaded the fubotv app and then subscribed through my computer. I have been using fubotv for less than a week. Based upon that experience I offer the following observations.I am able to watch the Giro as I desired. There are quite a few other channels available but I have not watch any, for reasons to be discussed below. The picture quality is fine and as with all internet apps it is dependent on you internet speed/quality.My biggest disappointment is the limited capacity of the "DVR" feature. While it is true you can "record" shows for later viewing you are limited to three "recording" total. Also, you must watch those recording within 72 hours of there recording, after which they will be deleted. This limitation has prevented me from recording any thing other than the Giro (which is a 21 day race) which explains why I have on experience with other channels. This wouldn't be too bad except the DVR does not provide the ability to record a "season". Rather, I have to go the desktop each day and set the DVR to record the next program (in my case, the next race three days in the future). A "Season" or "Record All" option sure would be nice.Another limitation, at least from the FireTV standpoint, is that you can't set the DVR to record a show from your TV. You can access the DVR to play a recording but to set new recordings you must use a computer. Also, the schedule on the FireTV fubotv app is limited to about 12 hours in the future.Finally, I have noticed that when the app is paused and then resumed there is a lot of buffering time before the show starts again. I don't believe this is a ISP problem as the buffering is much longer than with PBS, NBC Sports Gold, HBO Now or YouTube.Bottom line, I am pleased to be able to watch the Giro "legally". The fubotv allows me to do this. The grips above are really are more observations than show stoppers. With that said, to get cycling with the DVR feature I am paying more than $40 per month. I will cancel my subscription after the Giro is done, not because of the app but because I really don't have any interest in the other channels. If fubotv offers some programming that your looking for I would go for it.

Fubo has lots of channels and gave me the option of adding on the NFL network.  The streaming works fine on my TCL Roku TVs and the only drawback I see so far is much of the content is in 720p and not true HD. Also 4k content is very limited. Sometimes they broadcast Fox NFL games in 4k. My TCL struggles with that channel but my Amazon fire tv works fine with Fox NFL 4k. With the Fubo app, I can install it on my iphone and all my apple devices so I can watch tv anywhere.  You can even stream it on a Windows laptop through the website.I did the free week trial before I finally selected Fubo as I didn't know anyone using the service so I was skeptical. We're saving about $100 a month by cancelling Comcast's phone and cable.  For the savings, I can put up with the lower resolution.

It has NFL Network and NFL Redzone and apparently a recently added full complement of ESPN channels. I have only been able to find NFL Network and Redzone on FuboTV so it's an easy decision.  It also has NBA TV.I have gigabit internet so streaming and picture quality are great. It also has all of my local broadcast CBS, NBC, Fox and CW channels except local ABC which is not good.  You can also set favorite channels on the guide. At the end of my trial, I'm cancelling my AT&T.The only downside is FuboTV dropped TNT, TBS and CNN so I'll use their respective apps on the fire stick. These are small sacrifices to have have have NFL Network and Redzone. You can get everything else on Fire TV.Disappointed live ABC channels are not available.

Our free trial is now over and we plan to keep Fubo basic.  We get all our favorite channels and some that our cable provider charged a premium for. In addition we have had no outages with Fubo in a week, but 24 hours of dead time on cable in the same period. The 1080 picture is better too.There are some nice pluses like 30 free hours of cloud recordings, and two day access to programs you forget to watch. We will save over a hundred dollars a month- I ditched cable this morning and only wish I'd done it a year ago.There are choices in streaming providers but FuboTV was by far the best for our tastes. Well deserving of five stars.I wrote the above yesterday and then read an astonishing number of bad reviews by others blaming Fubo and/or Firestick for buffering problems and poor picture quality. I think these authors are uninformed. If you want to receive a high definition picture streaming live then the critical issue is the speed and strength of your internet connection from your internet provider, not Fubo and not Firestick. Mine is 100 Mbp/s and there are very few obstacles in the way of the receivers. No buffering and a perfect picture is the result. So to those reviewers- I suggest you look there first and get more wifi speed or a good repeater before laying blame in the wrong place. Most technical reviews (like CNET and others) rate Firestick and Fubo as best in class.

got the latest update and this is great!....everything works great....and 500 hours DVR!....they seem to have fixed all the bugs from the earlier app version....and I did spend time with Fubotv support about some of the problems....and they seem to have listen very well.... to me it's well worth the money......and not having espn in no problem for me....they have all the channels I want...and the DVR!.......much better now with this update.....have tried all the others but to me no one beats Fubo....just saying.....

Headings: First complete streaming service for my area.
Base_Reviews: Streaming services take some time to get used to. We are used to instant on. I use Amazon fire sticks for my TVs, which are not smart TVs. Fubo has given us these necessary programing to make the switch from our very expensive cable. This is the first streaming service in our area to give live local programing. It also has a nice lineup of channels and you can add on or subtract. So all in all it is quite a value and has a nice favorites app so we don't have to go through the entire guide to find our most watched shows. It also offers 250 hours of cloud DVR in the basic package.I do find it a little tedious to work with, but that is likely because I don't have the smart TV.

Headings: Left satellite company for Amazon Programs and Fubo TV
Base_Reviews: I had been a satellite-provider customer for over 15 years and was becoming very dissatisfied.  I have to include Amazon in this review because of their great marketing strategy with Prime Video.  Also, if it wasn't for Amazon and showing Fubo TV as a potential channel, I could have missed this channel completely.  After reviewing the shows I was watching through satellite, and doing my research, Fubo provides all of the sports channels I like, my local channels (for real--my actual local channels!) and other channels I watched through satellite.  AND, they have a great DVR storage program and the channels I can still watch live.  I have no regrets; my family can watch their shows without add-on.  Everything dear to us is included.  Great job Amazon and Fubo TV; thank you!  Very satisfied customer.

Headings: Cheaper and better than Satellite and Cable with better picture quality
Base_Reviews: Very easy to use with Smart TV and fire stick. All the channels you could possibly want and many more! Best part is the cloud dvr that you can access from anywhere. We have only had it a week but so far very happy. Plus it is incredibly cheaper than cable or satellite providers without all the stupid shopping channels and garbage fillers to tell you have 400 channels. No contract and all the sports channels are included along with local networks. Actually much better picture quality as well.

We cancelled our very expensive satellite TV subscription. We bought antennas and Fire TV set up on both of our televisions. They canceled BEIN sports on most satellite providers, but FuboTV has 12 BEIN sports channels. My husband has more football (soccer) than he can watch. I get all of the channels that I ever want or need to watch. Don't wait to switch. The antennas are a cinch to hook up. The Fire TV is fool proof. I am very, very impressed with the set up. Our Alexa remote is a universal remote, controlling the TV and soundbar. FuboTV is inexpensive and has an amazing channel line up. Check it out!

We did a one week trial during the World Series.  It was a little more difficult to set up than expected, but only took about 15 minutes, I guess.  At one point, we were just watching the video, and the stream just paused.  Did a netspeed test on my phone, and we had 200mbps download...stream still paused.  Had to restart the stream to get it going again.  Took about 5 minutes.  Also, the second time we started it up no audio, switched to Netflix and the audio popped in, then back to fubo and there was audio.For $65/mo I would just expect a better interface.  Enjoyed games 5 and 6 of the series, but then cancelled right away.  For the price, definitely not for us.

Headings: Great choice over cable for sports fans
Base_Reviews: I am enjoying using FuboTV for watching all of my sports (baseball, football, golf, basketball, etc..).  The service is the only one that I have found that includes the sports channels that carry my local teams.  The only reason I did not give a 5 star rating is that while watching local channels like ABC it will skip back 30 minutes or so all of the sudden.  If you are not paying attention you will not realize you are watching a stream from 30 minutes in the past.  You just have to switch channels and switch back and it goes back to a live stream.  I have only noticed this on the local channels like ABC.  I did watch the Redzone channel this past Sunday and did not experience buffering which was great.

I recently moved and have been unable to get suddenlink cable or directv or dish satellite services to provide service at my location (too many trees for satellite and the cable company is a joke, won't even provide a quote to extend service) so I began exploring cable alternatives.  FuboTv has a great selection of channels and it works on the devices I have.  The stream quality has been decent with the limited bandwidth I have (approx. 15mbps) and the picture quality is good most of the time.  I suspect this has more to do with my internet provider than it does the FuboTV service, I will try to update when my speeds get an upgrade in a month or so.  The cost isn't bad, but when compared to other services, it is probably about $10/month higher than it should be.  I WOULD recommend this to others as a good cable/satellite alternative.

Headings: The most channels Sports and Non - are in this app
Base_Reviews: I have used Sling, Pluto, Hulu, and a few others - attempting to replicate the amount of channels you would have with satellite, and I am happy to say with this APP I have done it.  On Sling - they advertise local channels but you don't get all of them - with Fubo you do.  Sling you have about 50 hours DVR - here you have 500.  Sling does not have Oxygen, WE and a few other channels that I like and that are included here.Sports - I don't' care - but if you do - there is a ton to choose from.I did only give them 4 stars however for 2 reasons:A.  The volume on some commercials is crazy loud so you have to run and turn the tv down when they come on.B.  There is no continue watching or way of going to the last show you were watching from the Home Screen.  If you are not in your recordings - then selecting continue watching - you would not see anything else you had been in the middle of.  So when I pause and go back into the app - I have to manually search for the last show I was streaming, or watching to continue and have to remember that.  HULU, PLUTO, SLING all have that feature so if you were watching a show 2 days ago - you can find it rather than searching - and that makes a real difference!

I liked the channel line up.  I primarily wanted the regional Foxsports channel (my local teams) and Foxnews, Foxbusiness.After that I wanted the more popular cable channels...USA, TNT, WE, AMC, TCM, Hallmark, History, etc.The initial load time is fairly quick.The FF and REW function works well.I like that the cloud DVR recordings do not expire.I have noticed the picture quality occasionally deteriorates (probably more my ISP than Fubo).I cancelled because I had already signed up with another service.As soon as that service expires at the end of the month, I will come back to Fubo.

At $65 a month, Iâ€™m not really cutting my cable bill when you factor in internet. BUT Iâ€™d rather pay these guys than the cable company who just canâ€™t seem to update to lower prices or offer you less and pay less.We have kids and this is simple to use and has all the stuff they want (â€œneedâ€� lol). Way easier to use than the dumb cable boxes and still have the option to record and DVR.Itâ€™s also got golf channel which isnâ€™t on one of the SLING packages. Therefore you have to get both if you have kids because none of the kids channels are on the sports one.Give it a try; you wonâ€™t be upset.

It's early days still, but this has changed TV life for the better. We cancelled our cable because we only had it for Bein Sports and then Comcast removed it from the lineup. We decided to try FuboTV. Now we have multiple Bein Sports channels and the resolution is way better than it was from Comcast. Not to mention that you get a whole lot of other channels that rack up your price in cable packages. We have the regular Fubo package. The one hitch we have experienced is that at times there is a brief hitch sometimes while watching, however it is always resolved in 5-10 seconds. What an improvement from cable.

Headings: Lagging compared to other devices that are streaming with Fubo
Base_Reviews: The fubo TV app as a whole is the same across devices, I have it on iphone and ipad and the experience is the same. However, the fubo TV app on the fire stick lags about 20-25 seconds compared to having the same stream on iphone or ipad. Considering that the iphone/ipad are 10-15 secs behind a TV provider like spectrum, it makes it hard to view live sports so far behind. I am okay with 10-15 seconds behind but not 35-40 secs behind. If the Fubo guys can fix this and make all devices have the stream at the same time it would be awesome. For now, I am still using the lighting to hdmi converter and using my ipad to view fuboTV on the big screen.

Great cord cutter app for FireTV or Roku. They offer plenty of sports channels but I watch mostly the local channels and news channel. Works great on my smartphone and iPad as well when I am not home, over WiFi. The app seems to always work well never see any buffering (unless there is a local internet issuse going on on - but i find that hardly ever to be the case.) They have a good lineup of channels for the money. The DVR feature works great. They give you 30hrs DVR time and offer more for a fee but 30 hrs for me is plenty! I like how a show may almost be over - just DVR it before it is over and you get the whole show! Nice!

Headings: The answer I was looking for
Base_Reviews: We had to get rid of cable because of the cost. I love this app. So easy to find shows and record what I want to see later. That part actually works better than my cable did. It has exactly the 7 channels that I needed for watching my shows. The rest that are included are bonus for me. I highly recommend it if you see the channels that you like in the package

Headings: Almost a 5 star if they had ABC
Base_Reviews: I would give this a 5 star but a local channel is missing for me as they have no ABC. But they do have everything else you can think of including the weather channel. (Big one for me in Florida)With all the others either stopping their services or continuing to go up in pricing I landed on Fubo. Not the cheapest and hope they don't start to go up, but I think the best out there. My only wish list is they has their GUI set up so you could have more than one profile so my wife could have her own set of favorites and a little more 4K. But all good otherwise.

It's not the best or worst app for Fire TV. The app is easy enough to navigate, but nothing great. The picture sometimes pixelates or buffers.My main complaint is the FF/RW options! Why are we limited to 15 second skips? It would be far nicer if we could do a standard FF/RW. If I'm somehow missing how to do so, please let me know.Update: Added a star since you can press the FF/RW button repeatedly to add skip time in increments of 15 seconds. I've done as much as 3 minutes. I don't know if there's a limit. It would still be easier to have a regular FF/RW so I could watch any interesting ads.

I signed up to replace Sling TV when that service lost the NFL Channel and NFL RedZone. Fubo has both. Although it cost considerably more than Sling, it has a more stable platform that doesn't freeze up or interfere with other Fire TV apps like Sling did. Headings: Better than I thought at first
Base_Reviews: I'm retracting my original review (and deleting most, if not all, of it), which was very negative and premature.Actually, I quite like this app on my Amazon Fire TV (and I also like the EarthCam app on my android phone). It's better than I thought. And, I have discovered several fallacies in my previous reviews. The only detractor is that there is no screen of all available webcams through which one might scroll in order to navigate to a particular site. The lineup changes every day, and sometimes more than once a day, depending on popularity of displayed activities such as parades, or even newsworthy events such as hurricanes.Soon after I paid the fee to break out of the automatic schedule, which changes to a different camera location every five or ten minutes, I bemoaned the fact that I could not set up my own custom list of preferred webcams, but could only choose one, which would remain constant until I manually changed it to another one. This is actually somewhat of an advantage, because it enables me to watch one scene as long as I desire. For instance, a few days ago, we watched an awesome display of fireworks at the bridge over the Danube River in downtown Budapest, Hungary. We also recently watched a surprisingly long parade in Vinita, Oklahoma, celebrating Will Rogers Day.My previous assessment of the process of returning to the scheduled rotation of webcams was also premature. We just navigate to another webcam that we want to see. As it turns out, we rarely wish to get back to the set rotation anyway.All in all, we're pretty satisfied with the lineup and the way it operates. I recommend it highly.

Headings: Around the planet from your home.
Base_Reviews: Go around the world from your living room recliner!  This app on my Amazon Fire TV Stick is free, but well worth the low price to upgrade annually, giving you more control in what you view.  The HD (and often 4K) picture quality is incredible; many include sound.  The webcam worldwide locations -and the webcam placement at these locations- are like living postcards.  Oh, and that's what makes viewing Earthcam a neat experience... the fact that what you're viewing is, indeed, live (there's a "Live" label at the upper left of the screen).  So it's definitely a heightened sense of reality as you watch, for example, the 4K views (there are several) of Times Square in NYC; or the Elvis Wedding Chapel in Vegas; or Abbey Road in London.  Love that most cam views also provide the locale's time and temp, plus optional background music as you watch (you can select the music genre and auto-cycle thru the cameras at selected intervals or manually move from camera to camera).Again, my review is on the app for my Amazon Fire TV and I'm completely pleased, using it practically every morning with my first cup of coffee. I realize this app is also available for other media devices (desktops and laptops) that have additional features, like camera pan & tilt.Lots and lots of locations throughout the world. Hey! Mall of America.  Sure would like to see a Nickelodeon Universe webcam.  Or Disneyworld?

Headings: Great service for a good price
Base_Reviews: TripIt is a very good product, I just wonder how long it will last. I have been a free user and now use the paid version. In chronological order I now see a sensible list of my flights, car rentals and hotel reservations with contact information.Try it for free and you'll love it. I only use two of the Pro features, but they are a big deal. The flight change notifications kept me from being left at the Philly airport because you couldn't hear the overhead notifications. Another is the ability to easily search for alternate flights, in my case due to weather changes.There is a 30 day free trial of Pro and if you travel frequently it is money well spent.

Headings: This app may not make travel fun, but at least it's much more efficient
Base_Reviews: The big value of this app, especially with the pro subscription, is that it gathers all the info you may need in one place. You can continue for forward various things like shuttle arrangements, activities while on a trip to plans@tripit.com and for most of them tripit parses them and inserts all the relevant info in your trip itinerary. On a recent trip, the airline had made some goofy codeshare arrangement where a separate ticket was issued by the other airline. Their agent couldn't find my ticket when I tried to check in. I looked in Tripit, there was the other ticket number, she recognized it was a different airlines ticket number and was able to help me. What are the  odds I would have made that flight without TripIt? Pretty low..

Headings: Great Way to Keep Track of Trip Plans
Base_Reviews: I've been using TripIt for the past several trips.  It serves the purpose of keeping track of my full itinerary, and I can build it little by little as reservations are made (or modified).  It includes such things as airport transfers, flights, cruises, tours, hotels, etc.  The coolest thing is that, with most reservations, you can simply forward your confirmation e-mail to plans@tripit.com, and TripIt automatically incorporates it into your itinerary, subject to any editing you may wish to do later.  Once built, itineraries can be e-mailed easily to travel companions, family members, etc., so they have all the info as well.  You can easily print out the itinerary, or keep it available on your mobile device, such as a tablet.

It warned us but about 2 hours later than the airline did.Other than that, simply emailing your travel plans and easy viewing make this a winner.

Headings: Elegant and Multi Platform and has a unique import feature
Base_Reviews: I don't travel a lot, but if I did I couldn't live without this.I have it loaded on my phone and my tablet and I use the web version as well and they all sync each other !  Change it on my phone and the others get changed. I love it.You can create multiple trips. Then you create a plan within the trip. Plans can  have segments within them.  The metaphors are natural.  Then comes the wizard feature. Set the program up to read an email account and it takes emails and turns them into plans !! Good stuff Maynard.One of the tricks I learned was to just put the zip code in for the address and it makes the time local. If you put a complete address in you can actually get a map.I feel bad I failed to pay for the full version, but I don't travel enough to worry about worry about alerts, alternate flights and seat tracking.  This is one of the five best apps I have

Make your reservations nonlinear.Email the confirmations to Tripit.Within a few minutes they magically appear on a single itinerary in your account.I use it allot the time now.  I don't have to print anything out or write anything down anymore.  Once viewed, the information is even available while off line.  I can share the information very easily with others.  It's easy to make changes to my itinerary.  I can even add my own personal notes or make manual entries if I would like.Overall it's a great repository for all of my travel information.  The only thing even remotely negative that I could say is that once I made a reservation for a hotel whose confirmation the atripit software couldn't read.  I simply entered the information manually.  That happened only once out of dozens of airline, train, hotel, and rental car reservations I've made over the last few years.

Headings: Great service for a good price
Base_Reviews: TripIt is a very good product, I just wonder how long it will last. I have been a free user and now use the paid version. It culls my e-mail to help develop an itinerary which was a cumbersome manual task in the past. In chronological order I now see a sensible list of my flights, car rentals and hotel reservations with contact information.Try it for free and you'll love it. I only use two of the Pro features, but they are a big deal. The flight change notifications kept me from being left at the Philly airport because you couldn't hear the overhead notifications. Another is the ability to easily search for alternate flights, in my case due to weather changes.There is a 30 day free trial of Pro and if you travel frequently it is money well spent.

Headings: This app may not make travel fun, but at least it's much more efficient
Base_Reviews: The big value of this app, especially with the pro subscription, is that it gathers all the info you may need in one place. You can continue for forward various things like shuttle arrangements, activities while on a trip to plans@tripit.com and for most of them tripit parses them and inserts all the relevant info in your trip itinerary. On a recent trip, the airline had made some goofy codeshare arrangement where a separate ticket was issued by the other airline. Their agent couldn't find my ticket when I tried to check in. I looked in Tripit, there was the other ticket number, she recognized it was a different airlines ticket number and was able to help me. What are the  odds I would have made that flight without TripIt? Pretty low..

You can add all your travel plans via the website and will update when loaded.  Your confirmation letters from your airline and hotel reservations can be forwarded to a special email address that will be added to your plans.  I've used it for various trips both near and far.  I do like it.

Headings: The organization of MY trips is very good.
Base_Reviews: I would have given it a 5 star rating except for the fact that when my children travel and send me their itineraries, it records them as my trips, asks for a hotel, sends me updates, etc.  Perhaps there's a way to avoid that, but directions are hard to come by these days.  The organization of MY trips is very good.

Headings: Great Way to Keep Track of Trip Plans
Base_Reviews: I've been using TripIt for the past several trips.  It serves the purpose of keeping track of my full itinerary, and I can build it little by little as reservations are made (or modified).  It includes such things as airport transfers, flights, cruises, tours, hotels, etc.  The coolest thing is that, with most reservations, you can simply forward your confirmation e-mail to plans@tripit.com, and TripIt automatically incorporates it into your itinerary, subject to any editing you may wish to do later.  Once built, itineraries can be e-mailed easily to travel companions, family members, etc., so they have all the info as well.  You can easily print out the itinerary, or keep it available on your mobile device, such as a tablet.

Headings: A great way to keep track of travel

Even so, it's an essential part of my travel material.

Don't leave home without it.  Every time we have to attend a world mark presentation ( I don't like to attend)  to stop the sales person and to get them off the sales pitch I show them the Tripit app..it's so good they ask me for Info.

Headings: I use TripIt Pro - GREAT convenience!
Base_Reviews: I travel a lot - 125,000 miles per year is common. What a pain to have all these air, hotel, cruise etc. bookings - except now I e-mail them all to TripIt and it aggregates them into my trips. So on my Kindle Fire HDX or my smartphone, I have it all at my fingertips - ticket and reservations numbers, times, dates, appointments, you name it. How very smart, and how very convenient! "Don't leave home without it" seriously applies to this app!TripIt Pro proactively feeds flight changes, allows you to look at alternate flights and available seat inventory and offers some additional bells and whistles - in my opinion well worth the slight upgrade price.

Only issue I ever have is if I'm tracking 2 flights it dumps them into one "trip" and you need to go to web version to split them up (that's the only way I've found to do it).Love the app though and find it very useful. Recommend it to my friends all the time.

Headings: The perfect GPS app for off-line mapping and routing. Saves a lot of data.

All search in a slightly different way: you set a filter for the country, city, street and then cross street which is easy to do. You can also pick a building or landmark as the cross. They choose show on map and refine exactly where you want to go.The turn by turn directions are great and as good as anything else. Like any route mapping system, once in a while you might make an extra turn but there isn't a system made that doesn't do that once in a while.I've used this on tablets and smartphones, it works great on all of them.To save data if you don't have an unlimited plan, simply turn your data off and this app will work off-line. It does also work well using WiFi or your data access if you want to go that route but I found that using this saves a lot of money and is hassle free.To get started, remember to download the Global base maps and then the maps for the country or state you need. The free version limits the number of downloads but unless you need more than that, the free version works just great. The paid for version isn't that expensive and you can get some additional advanced features.What I like is using this app on a tablet with the tablet's camera point at the road. Then whenever you want to you link a picture or video to a location for your records. It is simple to do.Adding favorites is super easy. Touch the location on the map and then choose add to my places from the menu. It is super easy and works.

We use it every week. My improvement suggestion would be able to create a master set of items. For each list, be able use the items like a database. Intother words, for Soda, for STore 1 be able to save it as being in Isle 4, while for Store 2 Soda is in Isle 10. In other words make a little more flexible.

I frequently travel in places where there's no wi-fi or cell signal, so it's important to me to have map data installed locally. OsmAnd is by far the best offline mapping program I've found -- it's packed with features and the offline maps work really well. It's been great for exploring dirt roads in the Mojave desert as well as trails all over the western US. It's also open source and has a great mailing list where you can ask questions. I haven't used the routing much, but for basic maps, favorites, waypoints and elevation, it can't be beat.

Some of the comments by dissatisfied users make me think of folk who don't vote but complain about who gets elected. OSM (the map database, which is different than the mapping program that uses it) is of, by and for the users. If something is missing, YOU, the user, can participate by adding to or fixing it. (Search for OSMbug for more info.) If you prefer someone else to be responsible for doing this, then buy commercial and go rate that. Moreover, the mapping programs such as this are often provided by dedicated non-commercial coders.

Headings: Best walking and cycling maps with OpenStreetMap
Base_Reviews: OsmAnd visualises OpenStreetMap maps. OpenStreetMap are much more up to date and better for walking and cycling than Google Maps. OsmAnd has many functions, and the interface can appear clutter. Configuration can greatly reduce the clutter but takes patients. OsmAnd permits the maps to be updated and corrected - very useful for an open source mapping system. The maps are download OFFLINE - ideal for areas without mobile cover (forest, mountains, etc). Navigation screen is Ok but not as clear and attractive as other apps. Excellent: the dynamic route planning. If you choose not to follow the route, the route will be recalculated. Route calculation options are limited for cycling. Komoot does a better job of distinguishing between road, touring, gravel, and mountain bike routes. The information is on the map, but the routing algorithm needs to be smart enough to use it. Komoot, however, does not have dynamic route planning. Choose, therefore, the less of two evils. With hourly updates of OpenStreetMap, OsmAnd is ideal for OpenStreetMap mapping community as you can see your corrections quickly and identify errors.

The app itself is free, and you can access all maps free so long as you have an internet connection. To manage storage, you can choose to download all 50 states, or pick and choose, which I thought was a nice feature.

It also makes one look a bit less like a tourist (and hopefully less of a target for thieves then).The points of interest included most of the common tourist sites, many public transportation spots (subway, tram stops), restaurants, hotels, and more. The only time the application seemed a bit confused by the streets was in Munich where the streets can be navigated a bit differently on foot than by car (and the app does provide different directions by foot or by car). Overall I was very happy with this application.
